seo.title: Destiny matrix compatibility 10: The Wheel of Fortune in a couple
seo.description: Destiny matrix compatibility 10: a union that lives in cycles, luck, debts and a “silence, then conflict” seesaw. Where the ten stands and how to read it.

items.title: The 10 in a compatibility matrix: The Wheel of Fortune in a couple
items.short: With a ten in a couple’s matrix, the union lives in cycles. Rises give way to crises, moves to lulls, good years to hard ones, and this is not a breakdown but a rhythm. In the plus it is a lucky, sociable couple with a sense of a fated meeting, who change jobs, homes and interests together. In the minus — a seesaw of “silence — conflict”, debts and a habit of blaming fate. Most often the ten stands in the middle of the couple’s tail and in its attitude to money.

sections.h2: How the Wheel ends up in a couple’s matrix
paragraphs: Compatibility is calculated separately from the personal matrices: the two partners’ matching points are added together and reduced to a number from 1 to 22, adding the digits of the sum if it is above 22. The result is a third matrix — the couple’s matrix. A ten in it does not mean the same as tens in both personal charts, and a match of arcana between partners says nothing about the union on its own. The meanings below follow Yuliana Lisovskaya’s book Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024); the method gives no compatibility percentages.
Three sums give a 10: 10, 28 and 37.

**An example.** The partners were born on 18 October 1986 and 27 May 1993. The material point is calculated from the year: 1 + 9 + 8 + 6 = 24 → 6 and 1 + 9 + 9 + 3 = 22. 6 + 22 = 28, 2 + 8 = 10 — a ten in “Attitude to material things”. In the middle of the tail the partners have 19 and 9: again 28 and again a ten. This couple’s tail is 3-10-16.

**An example with the centre.** The partners were born on 25 March 1996 and 3 March 1989. Their personal centres are 7 and 3, 10 in total — a ten in the couple’s centre. Their days of birth give the same 7 and 3, so the ten also stands in the image of the couple.

sections.h2: Where the Wheel turns: points and frequencies
paragraphs: The ten is one of the energies found almost everywhere in a couple with a similar frequency: apart from the centre, for six to nine couples in a hundred. Slightly more often than elsewhere — in the middle of the tail. The shares cover all pairs of dates from 1900 to 2026; in brackets is Lisovskaya’s label, transliterated from Russian.

sections.h2: The couple’s tasks: stability amid change
paragraphs: The couple’s tasks are the three bottom points, the tail of the couple’s matrix; the key one is “Main task”, read mostly in the minus. A ten in the tail is a frequent guest.

**“Middle of the task”.** This is the ten’s most frequent place in a couple — for almost one couple in eleven. It says that the way to the main task lies through change: not clinging to what is already past and not waiting for everything to sort itself out. The Wheel turns, and the task is to move with it rather than stand across its path.
**“Main task”.** The Wheel in the main task asks you:

ul: to arrive at shared stability: not to live from crisis to crisis;
to accept the partner with all their faults;
to speak sincerely rather than through hints and resentment;
to look for solutions instead of complaining about fate and each other;
to move away from manipulation, grudges and hysterics;
not to narrow your circle down to just the two of you;
to overcome fears together — of change, of poverty, of loneliness.

paragraphs: Lisovskaya gives examples of couples with a ten where one partner pulled the other out of a destructive relationship or a severe crisis. The Wheel in the tasks is also a chance: to get through together a turn that cannot be got through alone.

sections.h2: Money and home life: luck that has to be held on to
paragraphs: **“Home and things”.** With a ten in home life there is a shared budget and generosity towards each other. You believe in luck, and it often comes: an unexpected bonus, a side job that grew into a business, a well-timed move. You treat the budget responsibly, but rather formally: the spreadsheet exists, but nobody has opened it for ages. If you take loans, you think them through.

**“Where it leaks” and “Success and the union”.** The ten stands here often, and its holes are recognisable: thoughtless spending in good months, loans taken “on a wave”, problems left to drift in the hope that they will blow over. Unjustified risk and envy of those who were luckier. And status and success affect the union in cycles: one partner is on the rise while the other is in a dip — and it is important not to turn this into a competition.
**“Path to prosperity”.** For the ten, money comes from opportunities: noticing a chance in time, changing jobs, moving, trying something new. Sudden sources of income are its path too.

**“Way into money”.** The ten comes into money in bursts: feast or famine, and in the lean months it is hard for the couple not to quarrel. For this couple a safety cushion is not a dull precaution but a way to get through the bottom of the wheel calmly.

sections.h2: Under the heart: turns of fate taken together
paragraphs: The card “What connects” is the very point people look for as “under the heart” in compatibility. It holds the events and activities that bring two people together.

With a ten, what connects you is the turns of fate you have taken together. The story of how you met, told as a small miracle: you missed a train and ended up in the same compartment. Moves, job changes, new interests you made up your minds to as two. Memories of good moments — photographs, places, songs. A ten under the heart is the feeling that you did not meet by chance.

sections.h2: Seesaw and lightness: quarrels and what brings you back
paragraphs: **Where it sparks.** With a ten in this point, quarrels go round in a circle: silence, silence, silence — and an explosion. You stop hearing each other, and it turns out you see life differently. Mood swings, indifference to the partner’s feelings, blame — of fate, of circumstances, of each other. Being together is hard, but something holds you, and that “something” is worth naming out loud.

**What fills.** The ten is fed by luck and growth, trips, conversations and support, shared memories and lightness. After a hard period, a spontaneous trip or an evening spent going through old photographs and laughing will bring you back to each other. This is one of the points that are read only in the plus.

sections.h2: Parents who are never boring
paragraphs: The couple as parents is about what kind of elders the two of you are: for your own children or for all the younger ones who end up near you.

**“What you teach”.** The ten teaches children not to fear change: a new school, a new city, a new interest is an adventure, not a catastrophe. It teaches them to notice opportunities and to be grateful for the good. The minus is unpredictability: the rules change with your mood, and it is hard for a child to know what to rely on.

**“Parents together”.** With a ten you are easy-going, cheerful parents who are fun to be with. You support each other in this role by turns: when one is in a dip, the other pulls. The risk is living in cycles in upbringing too: a month of strictness, a month of anything goes.

sections.h2: Lucky from outside and a rhythm to learn
paragraphs: **“Image of the couple”.** The partners’ days of birth add up to the image others see. With a ten you look from outside like a lucky, sociable, decisive couple, a happy family. You change jobs, homes and interests together, and you pay debts back on time. In the minus the image becomes anxious: always in trouble and in debt, the seesaw in full view of everyone, “it’s complicated” as the relationship status.

**“What to create together”.** Lisovskaya reads this point only in the plus and gives no separate answer for the ten — it follows from its strong side. You were brought together to learn to live in the rhythm of change: to take the turns of fate together, notice opportunities in time and come out of crises together stronger than you went in.

sections.h2: A 10 in the centre: a sense of a fated meeting
paragraphs: A ten in the couple’s centre turns up for about one couple in twenty-five. For that the partners’ personal centres must add up to 10 or 28: for example, 3 and 7, 5 and 5, 12 and 16, or 8 and 20.

Such a couple has a sense of a fated meeting. You suit each other very well, see life in a similar way, have many shared interests, and each accepts the other in any mood. Joy, gratitude, trust. In the minus — you do not hear each other, each has their own truth, and both wait to “get lucky”.

sections.h2: Advice for a couple that lives in cycles

ul: **Accept change with gratitude.** Don’t fight the turning of the cycles; use it as a reason to move.
**Don’t close in on each other.** Shared friends, new activities, people around you — the ten needs air.
**Sometimes let go of control** and simply enjoy the moment.
**Be generous to each other** — with attention, with time, with forgiveness.
**Lower your demands on your partner.** They are going through their own cycles too.
**Keep a reserve for the bottom of the wheel.** Money, strength, and an agreement on how you behave in a crisis.

sections.h2: When one of you has a 10
paragraphs: A ten in the personal chart of one of you is that person’s sense of the moment, knack for seizing a chance and pull towards change. It will not appear in the couple’s matrix by itself: it adds up with the partner’s number in the same point. Two tens in one point give the couple a twenty.

faq.q: What does 10 mean in destiny matrix compatibility?
faq.a: It is the energy of cycles and change. In such a union rises and crises take turns, and this has to be accepted rather than fought. The plus is luck, lightness and a sense of a fated meeting; the minus is the seesaw, debts and a habit of blaming fate.

faq.q: Does a 10 in a couple mean the relationship will be unstable?
faq.a: Not necessarily. The ten speaks of rhythm, not chaos. In the plus the couple goes through the turns together and comes out stronger. In the minus crises become a reason for blame. The ten’s main task is precisely shared stability — not the absence of change but the ability to stick together while it is happening.

faq.q: What does a 10 in the middle of the couple’s tail mean?
faq.a: It is the ten’s most frequent place in a couple. The middle of the tail suggests how to solve the union’s main task. With a ten — through movement: not clinging to the past, changing in time what has stopped working, and not waiting for things to resolve by themselves.

faq.q: When does a 10 end up in the couple’s centre?
faq.a: When the partners’ centres add up to 10 or 28 — for example, 3 and 7 or 12 and 16. This happens for about one couple in twenty-five.

faq.q: We both have a 10 in our personal matrices. Is it fate?
faq.a: A match of arcana between partners says nothing about the union on its own. Compatibility is read from the couple’s matrix, where the points add up: two tens in one point give twenty. The sense of a fated meeting in a couple comes from a ten that stands in the couple’s matrix itself.

seo.title: Destiny matrix compatibility 11: Strength in a couple
seo.description: Destiny matrix compatibility 11: two strong people who charge each other up, passion, money under control and a struggle for the lead. Where Strength stands.

items.title: The 11 in a compatibility matrix: Strength in a couple
items.short: Two strong people who charge each other up — that is how the eleven reads in a couple’s matrix. They sense finely what the partner needs, the tension between them goes into passion, and from outside this is a couple with a voice and weight: ringleaders, organisers, people who get things done. In the minus the same strength turns into a struggle: for the lead, for being right, for who controls the money. The eleven is a frequent energy in a couple, and it most often stands in money, home life and the point under the heart.

sections.h2: Strength in the couple’s chart: the sums 11, 29 and 38
paragraphs: Compatibility in the destiny matrix is usually worked out not by comparing two charts but through a third matrix — the couple’s matrix. That is how Yuliana Lisovskaya, author of Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024), works too: the matching points of two personal matrices are added together and reduced by the usual rule — if the sum is above 22, its digits are added. The method gives no compatibility percentages: it describes what the couple rests on and what it trips over. The numbering here is the matrix’s: 11 is Strength. In the Waite deck Strength is numbered VIII, and XI is Justice.
Three sums give an 11: 11, 29 and 38.

**An example.** The partners were born on 12 October 1996 and 3 October 1993. Their personal centres are 4 and 7: 4 + 7 = 11 — Strength in the couple’s centre. The years give 1 + 9 + 9 + 6 = 25 → 7 and 1 + 9 + 9 + 3 = 22: 7 + 22 = 29, 2 + 9 = 11 — Strength in “Attitude to material things” as well. And in the point “Path to prosperity” both have 19: 38, 3 + 8 = 11. This couple has the eleven three times — both in the atmosphere and in money.

sections.h2: Where Strength stands and how often
paragraphs: Strength is scattered across a couple’s matrix almost evenly: in each point for seven or eight couples in a hundred, and in the centre for five. The figures are shares of all pairs of dates from 1900 to 2026; the letter in brackets follows Lisovskaya’s book, transliterated from Russian.

sections.h2: Money and home life: strength that has to be kept in balance
paragraphs: **“Home and things”.** In material matters Strength is energetic and inventive. You see a problem more deeply than others and find unconventional solutions: where the neighbours take out a loan, you find a side job, a swap or a way to do it yourselves. You can save quickly when there is a goal. You do not grudge money on hobbies, pleasures, sport and looking after your bodies. In the minus — workaholism at the family’s expense, mess and envy of those who have more.

**“Where it leaks” and “Success and the union”.** Here the eleven stands for one couple in twelve. Strength’s hole is control: all the money is with one partner and is handed to the other by the rules and against receipts. And work that eats up the family: one disappears into projects, the other carries the household without help. And status affects the union through demands: inflated expectations of the partner’s position and looks, “you have to measure up”.

**“Path to prosperity”.** Strength gets prosperity through energy and persistence: sport, work with people, organising, a business in which you have to bear a heavy load. Balance helps too: Lisovskaya advises such couples to keep an equilibrium between stinginess and spending, between work and family.
**“Way into money”.** Strength’s income suffers from overstrain: you took on everything at once and burned out. An even pace pays better for this couple than bursts.

sections.h2: Under the heart: charging each other up
paragraphs: The point “What connects” — searches call it “under the heart” — shows what two people come together on. The eleven stands here often — for one couple in twelve.

With Strength, what connects you is that you charge each other up. Sport together, morning runs, a hike after which both of you are proud of yourselves. Giving up a bad habit, with one supporting the other and not letting them slip. Shared interests you invest in seriously. And intimacy: in such couples passion does not fade for a long time, because the tension between them goes not into quarrels but into attraction. Under the heart, the eleven is also a feeling of being protected: beside you is a person who can take the strain.

sections.h2: The couple’s tasks: what to do with your own power
paragraphs: The couple’s tail is read as a list of the union’s trials — first of all in the minus; the key point is “Main task”, and the middle reveals it. For Strength the trial is one, in different forms: what to do with your own power.

**“Middle of the task”.** An eleven in the middle of the tail stands for roughly one couple in thirteen. It says that the key to the main task lies in managing your strength: not pressing, not snapping, but directing the energy into something useful. In the tail Lisovskaya analyses in the book — the couple born on 13 September 1970 and 2 July 1973, whose tail we write as 6-11-5 — Strength stands exactly in the middle, between the six and the five.
**“Main task”.** In the main task Strength has to:

ul: learn to handle its anger and drive so that they do not hurt the one close to you;
respect each other — including when you disagree;
keep a balance of work, rest and family;
share the housework fairly, without “I already do plenty”;
say from the very start what you like and what you don’t, instead of storing it up until it explodes;
express feelings openly and set priorities for your attention.

sections.h2: Strong parents
paragraphs: Even if you have no children, these points describe how the two of you lead and protect the younger ones — in the family, in sport, at work.

**“What you teach”.** The eleven teaches children to cope: with difficulties, with fear, with their own emotions. It teaches discipline, sport, responsibility, the ability to stand up for oneself without cruelty. The minus is demanding strength from a child before they are ready for it and not noticing their weakness.

**“Parents together”.** With an eleven you are energetic parents who support each other with deeds: one drives to the competition, the other packs the bag. The child sees two strong adults who know how to reach agreement. The risk is a struggle over whose approach to upbringing is right, in front of the child.

sections.h2: A struggle for the lead and movement that charges you up
paragraphs: **Where it sparks.** Strength’s conflicts in this point are a struggle for the lead. Each has their own truth, and the two speak “different languages”. Suppression, rudeness, false expectations, demands about the partner’s status and looks. This is a signal that you need to learn how to argue: without mockery, without pressure, without “I’m stronger”.

**What fills.** Strength is replenished by moving together and looking after yourselves: sport, active holidays, giving up what is harmful, with one charging up the other. Accepting the partner’s way of life. Intimacy, shared interests, a feeling of being protected. Here Strength is always in the plus: even its drive works for the union.

sections.h2: Being strong together: the meaning of the meeting and the image
paragraphs: **“What to create together”.** The book gives no “why you met” answer specifically for Strength; it is read from its plus. You were brought together to learn to be strong together: to support rather than suppress, to strengthen each other rather than compete in strength. To create a union in which both have a voice. This point is not read in the minus.

**“Image of the couple”.** This point is built from the days of birth — in other words, from the partners’ calling cards. With an eleven people see you as energetic, collected, punctual and responsible. You are the ringleaders and organisers: if something needs arranging in your circle, you are the ones who get the call. Sporty, creative, keen on your work in a good way. In the minus it is visible from outside who is in charge in the couple, and mockery of the partner can be heard even in company.

sections.h2: Strength in the centre: passion and a struggle for the lead
paragraphs: Of the energies from 3 to 12, Strength is one of the most frequent in the centre: about one couple in twenty. For that the partners’ personal centres must add up to 11, 29 or 38: for example, 4 and 7, 5 and 6, 9 and 20, 13 and 16, or 18 and 20.

Inside such a couple you sense finely what the other needs, and you charge up and strengthen each other. The tension between you goes into passion. In the plus, one accepts the other’s lead where the other is stronger, and both know how to give way. The intentions are serious. In the minus — a struggle for the lead, and each has their own truth.

sections.h2: Advice for a couple with Strength

ul: **Keep a balance** between work and family, between stinginess and spending.
**Don’t decide in the heat of the moment.** An impulsive act of Strength costs more than it seems.
**Move more together.** Sport and active holidays are the best outlet for the couple’s energy.
**Take off the rose-tinted glasses.** Look at your partner soberly: see both the strength and the weakness.
**Don’t overstrain yourselves.** Strength is not an endless resource, and it needs replenishing too.

sections.h2: Strength in one partner’s personal chart
paragraphs: Strength in a personal chart is a trait of one person: inner power, endurance, the ability to cope where others give up. But it does not carry over into the couple’s chart: a couple’s point is a sum, not a copy. Two Strengths in one point give the couple a 22.

faq.q: What does 11 mean in destiny matrix compatibility?
faq.a: Strength in a couple is passion, mutual support and enough energy for two. The partners charge each other up and are energetic and active together. The minus is a struggle for the lead, each with their own truth, control over money and mockery of the partner.

faq.q: Does an 11 in a couple mean we will fight over who is in charge?
faq.a: Not necessarily. The theme of leadership matters for such a couple, but in the plus it is settled like this: each leads where they are stronger and recognises the other’s strength. The struggle begins when the rules have not been talked through and both want to steer everything.

faq.q: Why is 11 in a couple Strength and not Justice?
faq.a: The destiny matrix uses the Marseille numbering: 8 is Justice, 11 is Strength. In the Waite deck these cards are swapped, so in tarot books Strength is numbered VIII. On our chart and in the couple reading, 11 is always Strength.

faq.q: Can Strength stand in the centre of a couple’s matrix?
faq.a: It can — for about one couple in twenty. For that the partners’ centres must add up to 11, 29 or 38, for example 4 and 7 or 13 and 16.

faq.q: What does 11 under the heart mean in compatibility?
faq.a: Under the heart in a couple’s matrix is the name for the point that shows what connects the partners. An eleven there is a union held together by mutual support and passion: you charge each other up, do sport and get things done together, and feel protected beside your partner.

seo.title: Destiny matrix compatibility 12: The Hanged Man in a couple
seo.description: Destiny matrix compatibility 12: a quiet union, care without counting and the risk of a sacrifice nobody asked for. Where The Hanged Man stands, centre too.

items.title: The 12 in a compatibility matrix: The Hanged Man in a couple
items.short: A twelve in a couple’s matrix gives a quiet, attentive union where the partners give way to each other, know how to listen and sense what is happening with the other even at a distance. Most often this energy stands in the couple’s values and where the reason the couple met is read, then in its common language and in the tasks of the tail, and often in the centre itself — in the atmosphere of the union. Its plus is care without counting and a calm harbour. Its minus is a sacrifice nobody asked for, living for the picture, and one partner holding the relationship together with all their strength.

sections.h2: The sums 12 and 39: where The Hanged Man in a couple comes from
paragraphs: Compatibility in the destiny matrix is read from a third, shared matrix: the matching points of two personal matrices are added together and the sum is reduced to a number from 1 to 22, by adding its digits if it is above 22. Yuliana Lisovskaya described the meanings of such a matrix in most detail in her book Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024); below is her school in our own words. The couple’s points have roles of their own, personal readings are not carried over to them, and the method gives no compatibility percentages.
Only two sums give a 12: 12 and 39.

**An example.** The partners were born on 18 September 1989 and 7 March 1994. The months give 9 and 3: 9 + 3 = 12 — the twelve lands in “What to create together”, in the sphere “Why you met”. Their personal centres are also 9 and 3, so the twelve stands in the couple’s centre too.

**An example with reduction.** The partners were born on 21 May 1993 and 25 October 1991. In the point that makes up the couple’s common language, they have 18 and 21: 39, 3 + 9 = 12. This couple’s tail is 12-7-22, and it starts with the twelve.

sections.h2: Where the twelve stands most often
paragraphs: The twelve is the only energy from 3 to 12 for which the couple’s centre is among its five most frequent places. Most often it stands in “The couple’s values” — for almost 9 couples in a hundred. The shares cover all pairs of dates from 1900 to 2026; in brackets is the point’s letter in Lisovskaya’s book, transliterated from Russian.

sections.h2: Why you met: care in which nobody disappears
paragraphs: “Why you met” in the reading is two cards: the image of the couple and “What to create together”. For the twelve, “What to create together” is its second most frequent place after the couple’s values: it comes out when the months of birth add up to 12: January and November, February and October, March and September, April and August, May and July, or both in June.

**“What to create together”.** Lisovskaya reads this point only in the plus; she gives no separate answer for the twelve, and we derive it from The Hanged Man’s strong side. You were brought together to learn a kind of care in which nobody disappears: to look at life from a different angle, slow down, learn to wait — and still not lose yourselves in each other. Your shared task is a union where giving way is possible but not required.

**“Image of the couple”.** From outside you are a hospitable, peaceful, friendly couple. You openly look after each other, help others without expecting anything back and love the unusual — from odd hobbies to holidays where nobody else goes. You try to be active, but at the first chance you leave for somewhere with fewer people: a country cottage, the woods, the water. In the minus the image becomes a picture: everything for others and for “what people will say”, and nobody knows what is inside.

sections.h2: A common language of giving way
paragraphs: This point is a crossroads: on the relationship line it describes what the couple agrees on, and in the tail, where its difficulties begin.

**As a common language.** With a twelve you reach agreement by giving way: “let’s do it however suits you” is heard more often in your home than “I want”. You hear each other, sense the mood without words and are ready to wait until the other is ready. What you want is quiet, peace, an unhurried life and the chance to help.

**As an entry to the task.** The reverse side is that nobody says what they really want. Both give way, and decisions are made “because that’s how it has to be”, not because anyone wants them. Wishes pile up, and one day it turns out you are living a life neither of you chose. At the entry to the tail the twelve has to learn to name its wishes out loud.

sections.h2: The couple’s tasks: one holds on, the other reproaches
paragraphs: The couple’s tasks are the tail of the matrix, and it is read mostly in the minus. The twelve stands here often, in all three points of the tail.

**“Middle of the task”.** A twelve in the middle of the tail suggests that the key to the main task lies in changing perspective: looking at the situation from the other side, no longer waiting for things to change by themselves, and making up your mind to take a step.

**“Main task”.** Here Lisovskaya describes a recognisable story: one partner holds the relationship together with all their strength, gives way and adapts, and gets reproaches in return — and does not leave, because keeping the family matters more to them than themselves. The work of such a couple:

ul: personal boundaries and the ability to say no — including to each other;
shared goals instead of one shared sacrifice;
the ability to take responsibility instead of waiting for the other to decide;
realistic expectations of each other instead of inflated ones;
compassion that does not turn into pity.

sections.h2: A 12 in the couple’s centre — more often than it seems
paragraphs: A twelve stands in the couple’s centre for about one couple in sixteen — more often than any energy from 3 to 11. The couple’s centre is the sum of two personal centres, and a twelve comes out, for example, with centres of 5 and 7, 4 and 8, 3 and 9, or 6 and 6.

The atmosphere inside such a couple is quiet and attentive. The partners are tactful, give way to each other, will always listen and help, and often sense what is happening with the other even at a distance. A characteristic trait: one is ready to do everything for the other and nothing for themselves. And another, almost amusing one: such couples take a long time to get going, and, as Lisovskaya observes, they need a noticeable push from outside to marry.

In the minus the atmosphere grows heavy. The parents have great power over the couple. Pressure through pity. A relationship on the principle of “we’ll take what there is for now” instead of love. Each pulls in their own direction, and then sacrifices themselves for show.

sections.h2: Money comes with time
paragraphs: **“Where it leaks” and “Success and the union”.** The twelve’s holes are debts and overdue payments, one partner’s dependence on the other and a strange feeling of unfairness even in prosperity: “everything comes easy to others, but for us…”. Status affects the union through a fear of growth: one is afraid of their own ideas and does not grow, so as not to overtake the partner or be left without support.

**“Home and things”.** In the plus everything earned goes to the family and the partner. You respect any work, are disciplined with money, pay on time, do not borrow and can say no to those who are always asking. In the minus — envy of what others have, inability to manage savings, an eternal “just in case”.

**“Path to prosperity”.** Prosperity comes to the twelve slowly — through patience and service: work that helps people, unconventional occupations, a business that brought in nothing for a long time and then took off. Lisovskaya tells such couples plainly: prosperity will come with time.
**“Way into money”.** The twelve’s income is held back by a fear of its own ideas and a habit of waiting. The task is, one day, to stop waiting for the right moment.

sections.h2: Under the heart: care and quiet joys
paragraphs: Searches call this point “under the heart”; the reading calls it “What connects”: this is where what brings two people closer is read.

With a twelve, what connects you is care and quiet joys for two. Walks without a destination, a film under one blanket, a board game until late at night, a new place found by chance. Helping others, which you do together — volunteering, an animal shelter, a neighbour you take groceries to. And that very feeling: you know how the other is, even when they are in another city.

sections.h2: Gentle parents
paragraphs: This sphere is about caring for the younger ones — your own children, if you have or will have them, and everyone you look after.

**“What you teach”.** The twelve teaches children compassion, patience and the ability to see a situation through someone else’s eyes. The minus is teaching a child to sacrifice themselves and to think that only convenient people are loved.
**“Parents together”.** With a twelve you are gentle, attentive parents who forgive a great deal. The risk is parents who live only for the children and leave nothing for themselves and each other.

sections.h2: Quarrels about sacrifices and quiet joys for two
paragraphs: **Where it sparks.** With a twelve in the conflicts point you quarrel about sacrifices. “I gave up everything for you”, “I put up with it, and you…”. Pressure through pity, grudges, hysterics, an endless tally of who sacrificed what.

**What fills.** The twelve’s strength is restored by walks, films and games for two, unusual pastimes and new places. This point is not read in the minus: even the tendency to slow down is a way of coming back to each other here.

sections.h2: The twelve’s two minuses
paragraphs: Lisovskaya describes the twelve’s minus in a couple as two paths, and they are worth knowing in order to notice them in time.

ul: **The sacrificial one.** Everything for others and for the picture; what matters is what people will say. Decisions, including about children, are made “because that’s how it has to be”. Outside, an ideal family; behind a closed door, hardship.

**The harsh one.** Together the couple puts pressure on those around them: relatives, colleagues, the state are cast as the culprits for their failures. When there are no outside culprits, the couple turns on each other.

paragraphs: This describes an energy, not a verdict: the same twelve can be a quiet harbour or a quiet trap. The difference is whether the two say out loud what they expect.

sections.h2: The couple’s values: giving without counting
paragraphs: Most often the twelve stands in “The couple’s values” — for almost 9 couples in 100. It is one of the five main cards of the reading. Its number is not added up from the partners’ points but recalculated from the couple’s purposes, so only 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 and 21 occur in this point. For Lisovskaya it is the couple’s spiritual purpose: its values and the path the two are to walk together.

**For a couple with a twelve, what counts is not what they got but what they managed to give.** They skip a seaside holiday to spend a month of weekends driving a friend’s boxes across town, are not afraid of pauses and see life from a different angle than their relatives. The difficulty is when the giving starts being counted: one keeps giving way and silently waits to be noticed, the other does not notice, and one day generosity turns into the reproach “I did everything for you…”.

sections.h2: Advice for a couple with The Hanged Man

ul: **Each stay self-sufficient.** Work of your own, interests of your own, a life of your own besides the couple.
**Move away from dependencies**, including on each other.
**Don’t blame your partner** — neither for your sacrifices nor for your failures.
**Add warmth.** Spoiling those close to you is not a weakness but a remedy for self-sacrifice.
**Work out where jealousy comes from**, if there is any.
**Keep away from a toxic circle** — people beside whom both of you become smaller.
**Patience.** Prosperity and change will come, but in their own time.

sections.h2: A 12 in one of you
paragraphs: A personal twelve is about one of you: the ability to wait, to look from a different angle and to give way. A couple’s matrix is a different calculation, and a personal twelve does not pass into it: it adds up with the partner’s number. If both have a twelve in one point, the couple will have 24 there, that is, a six.

faq.q: What does 12 mean in destiny matrix compatibility?
faq.a: It is the energy of care, patience and the ability to look at life from a different angle. A union with it is quiet and attentive; the partners give way to each other and help others. The minus is self-sacrifice, living for the picture, and one partner holding the relationship together with all their strength.

faq.q: Does a 12 in a couple mean someone will be the victim?
faq.a: No. It is one of the energy’s possible minuses, not fate. The twelve shows that the theme of giving way and sacrifice matters for the couple. In the plus you look after each other without counting and do not disappear in the process; in the minus one dissolves into the other. The couple’s task is personal boundaries and shared goals.

faq.q: Why does the 12 stand in the couple’s centre so often?
faq.a: The couple’s centre is the sum of two personal centres, and the most frequent centres in people are numbers from 5 to 11. Their sums often give 12: 5 and 7, 6 and 6, as well as 4 and 8, 3 and 9. That is why a twelve stands in the centre for about one couple in sixteen — more often than any energy from 3 to 11.

faq.q: What does a 12 in “Why you met” mean?
faq.a: It is the twelve’s second most frequent place in a couple, after the values. It means you need the union in order to learn a kind of care in which nobody disappears — to see life differently, slow down and not lose yourself in the other. This point is read only in the plus.

faq.q: Why does a couple with a 12 need a push to get married?
faq.a: That is how Lisovskaya describes the atmosphere of a couple with a twelve in the centre: the partners take a long time to settle into the relationship, are slow to decide and can live for years without an official status. Often an outside event becomes the push — a move, a request from the parents, a new job, buying a home together.

seo.title: Destiny matrix compatibility 13: Death in a couple
seo.description: Destiny matrix compatibility 13: where Death occurs in a couple, how to read it in the centre, the tail and money, its plus and minus, an example and advice.

items.title: Arcanum 13 in a compatibility matrix: Death that renews a couple
items.short: 13 in destiny matrix compatibility is the energy of Death, which a couple does not bring with them but gives birth to together. It does not foretell a break-up. It is a union that knows how to close chapters — a past marriage, life with parents, an old city, a habit that has had its day — and start the next one without parting. Below is where 13 occurs in a couple’s matrix, what it means at each point, how it looks in the plus and the minus, and what helps a couple with this energy.

sections.h2: How 13 gets into a couple’s matrix
paragraphs: Compatibility here is read by the school of Yuliana Lisovskaya, Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024). An ordinary matrix is calculated for each partner by date of birth, then the matching points are added together: centre with centre, month with month, task with task. If the sum is above 22, its digits are added: 27 gives 9, 35 gives 8. This produces a third matrix — the couple’s matrix — and it is read by its own rules: the couple’s centre, for example, describes the atmosphere between two people, not the character of one of them.

The thirteenth has a special property here. No sum above 22 reduces to 13: the largest that 23–44 give after their digits are added is 12. So 13 in a couple comes only from a sum of exactly 13 — for example, 6 and 7, 4 and 9, or 1 and 12. At that point each of you has a number below thirteen, and neither has a Death of their own there. The energy of change is born of the meeting itself. In the couple Lisovskaya analyses in the book (dates 12.03.1963 and 05.10.1966), 13 stands in the “why you met” point, and the author reads it as an experience the two are living through for the first time — together.

The most frequent point can be checked without a calculator. The “why you met” point adds the months of birth. If you have January and December, February and November, March and October, April and September, May and August, or June and July, the total is 13, and this energy stands here for you. It happens for about 8 couples in 100, and 13 is the most frequent number in this point overall.

The centre does need a calculation. An example: the dates 18.05.1993 and 13.09.1987. The centre of the first matrix is 9, of the second 4; their sum is 13, and that is the couple’s centre. In a personal chart the centre ranges from 3 to 14 plus 16, 18, 20 and 22, so 13 in the couple’s centre comes from four combinations: 3 and 10, 4 and 9, 5 and 8, 6 and 7.

sections.h2: Where 13 occurs in a couple’s matrix
paragraphs: The thirteenth occurs in 14 points of the couple’s matrix. It never appears in the common language point — the start of the couple’s tail: only 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 and 21 come up there.

paragraphs: Lisovskaya’s card for this energy is written by sphere — atmosphere, image, finances, tasks — rather than for each point. Where the author has no separate text, what follows is our reading based on the meaning of the point and the arcanum.

sections.h2: Why you met: to start again as two
paragraphs: This point is read only in the plus: it answers what the couple needs to create together. With 13 it is a new chapter that neither of you would have opened alone. Such couples often come together at a turning point: after a divorce, after a move, when one has just left a job they disliked or a relationship that was destroying them. The meeting becomes the point after which the old life ends and the new one begins straight away for both.

In everyday life this shows in decisiveness. A couple with 13 in this point does not drag things out for years: they move in together quickly, marry quickly, easily decide on a child, a mortgage, a move to another city. One helps the other close what has dragged on for years — quit a job, stop justifying themselves to their parents, get the divorce that kept being put off. If someone has children from a previous marriage, the other accepts them as part of their new life, not as an obstacle.

In the couple reading this point stands in the sphere “Why you met” next to the image of the couple — how others see you. Together they answer why you are in each other’s lives: with 13 in either of them, the answer is to show yourselves and others that after an ending there is a beginning.

sections.h2: The atmosphere inside the couple: 13 in the centre
paragraphs: The couple’s centre is what happens between you when nobody is watching. The thirteenth in the centre gives a union that lives through several versions of itself without falling apart.

**In the plus** it is a calm relationship with shared goals. The partner’s past is accepted here: a former marriage, mistakes, debts, a child from a first relationship — all of this is part of the person, not a reason for interrogation. Each has their role, and the roles can change: one goes off to study, the other takes on more of the household, and a year later it is the other way round. The partner has the right to outgrow their former self, and the other does not demand back the person they first met. Much joy in small things and a strong feeling of being protected — precisely because change is not frightening.

**In the minus** there is more change than one of the two can bear. An emotional seesaw: today they decided to move, tomorrow they changed their minds, a week later they are packing boxes again. One tries to remake the other — change their job, their circle, their way of life. The other clings to the familiar and nit-picks at every detail, just so that something stays the same. A separate trap is the shadows of exes: the partner is credited with the traits of a former husband or wife and blamed for things they never did. “You’re just like him” is a phrase after which the conversation is no longer about the person sitting there.

sections.h2: The couple’s tasks: 13 in the tail
paragraphs: The sphere “The couple’s karmic tail” has three points: entry to the task, the middle and the main task. 13 occurs in the main task (about 6 couples in 100) and in the middle (about 4 in 100), but not at the entry. Lisovskaya reads these points mostly through the minus: they show what the couple is learning from.

With 13 the main lesson is to separate. To help each other leave the parental nest: stop clearing the purchase of a sofa with your mother, move out of the parents’ flat where you have been living “temporarily” for three years, buy a home of your own or move away. The birth of a child can become the task too — after it the old couple ends and a family is born. This also covers a partner quite unlike the previous one and the temptation to reject that difference, distance and separations, one partner’s lack of seriousness, the influence of relatives.

The hardest part of the task is a crisis. A couple with 13 in the tail learns at turning points: losing a job, a move, a difficult conversation about the future. The lesson is to live through them as a test for two, not as proof that the choice was a mistake. And to see one’s own mistakes, not only the other’s: “I kept quiet too when I should have spoken” is a turning-point phrase in such couples. If 13 stands in the middle of the tail, it shows what the main task opens through: the need to finish something before moving on.

sections.h2: 13 under the heart: what connects the couple
paragraphs: In searches the “what connects” point is called “under the heart”: in a personal matrix the same point of the relationship line carries that label. In a couple’s matrix it shows the positive potential: the events and questions that bring two people closer. With 13, what connects you is beginnings. The move you made together, the first renovation of your own flat, the year when both of you changed jobs — such events become your shared supports, remembered ten years later.

This point stands in the sphere “Relationship and common language” between two others: each partner’s success and status, and the common language. 13 under the heart suggests how to reach agreement: not to patch up the old endlessly, but to admit when something has had its day and decide together what will take its place. Couples with this energy make up well through action — clearing out the box room, throwing out the old, going somewhere they have never been.

sections.h2: 13 in the couple’s money
paragraphs: The money sphere in the couple reading is a line of three points: the way into money, the path to prosperity and the place where money leaks. 13 occurs in all three and also in the attitude to material things.

ul: **Way into money** (about 3 couples in 100) shows where income stalls. With 13 it is fear of change: clinging to a job that stopped growing long ago because leaving is frightening. A cushion saved in advance helps avoid this: with six months in reserve, the decision to change jobs stops being a leap into the abyss.

**Path to prosperity** (about 3 in 100): prosperity comes through bold change — a new profession, moving to where pay is higher, giving up the unnecessary. The couple can get its bearings quickly, cut spending and always keeps a reserve.

**Where it leaks** (about 4 in 100). The same point is responsible for how each partner’s success and status affect the union. With 13 the holes are debts shifted onto the partner, laziness about sorting out finances and, above all, rejection of growth. One gets a promotion or starts a business, and the other, instead of rejoicing, feels left behind.

**Attitude to material things** (fewer than 2 in 100): the ability to clear out — to give up unnecessary subscriptions, things kept “just in case”, spending out of habit. In the minus — debts and a general lack of financial know-how.

paragraphs: Lisovskaya’s financial advice for this energy is simple: build a financial cushion in advance, not when the change has already happened.

sections.h2: The couple’s image, what fills it and what can spoil it
paragraphs: **How others see the couple.** From outside, a couple with 13 is living proof that life goes on after hard times. Often it is not a first marriage, and there may be children from previous relationships. The couple is active, sociable, likes to travel and try unusual things. In the minus the image becomes one of people without brakes: they take risks with themselves and with money, the relationship looks immature from outside, and one partner may one day leave without explanation.

**What fills the union.** Novelty in everything: trips, moves, a change of scene, frank conversations, making things together, good habits taken up as two — from morning runs to a rule of no phones at dinner. A shared aspiration restores strength too: when a couple has a goal for the coming year, it is easier for it to get through hard times.

**What can spoil it.** The quarrels of a couple with 13 grow from two places. The first is more change than one can bear: one changes everything in sight and demands that the other keep up; the other resists and nit-picks. The second is the past: old grudges, comparisons with exes, fear that it will all happen again. Until the past is closed, the quarrels are with someone other than the person beside you.

sections.h2: The couple as parents: 13 in the children points
paragraphs: The sphere “The couple as parents” has two points: parents together — how you support each other in this role — and what you teach the child. 13 occurs in both, more often in the second.

**What you teach** (about 4 couples in 100). With 13 you teach a child not to be afraid of endings: to give up a club they no longer love without guilt, to get through a move and a change of school, to let go of an old friendship. It is good when this is done out loud: “yes, it’s sad, and still we are starting something new”. In the minus there is too much change in the child’s life — new cities, schools, rules — and nothing for them to lean on.

**Parents together** (fewer than 2 in 100). A couple who rebuild their life around the child’s stages — nursery, school, growing up — and know how to let go in time. The theme of separating from parents, which a couple with 13 resolves for themselves, is passed on here: to raise a person who will leave for their own life, and to be glad of it.

sections.h2: What helps a couple with 13

ul: Keep a financial cushion before a change, not after it.
Finish one change before starting the next: a move, then a change of job, not everything in one month.
Don’t compare your partner with exes — neither out loud nor to yourself. Talk honestly about the past once, so as to close it.
Rejoice in your partner’s growth, even if it changes the familiar arrangement.
Look for the good in your partner and tell them about it; give keepsake presents — things that mark a stage you have come through together.
Understand your partner’s love language: words matter to one, deeds to another, time together to a third.
Look after islands of constancy — a shared breakfast at weekends, traditions — that you can lean on when everything around you is changing.

paragraphs: The method gives no compatibility percentages, and 13 in a couple’s matrix is not a verdict on the relationship but its theme.

faq.q: Does 13 in compatibility mean the couple will split up?
faq.a: No. In a couple’s matrix Death speaks of the end of forms, not of relationships: a former job, a former city, former roles. A couple with 13 knows how to live through such endings and stay together. The difficulty lies elsewhere — in the speed of change: if one changes faster, the other needs time, and that is worth discussing out loud.

faq.q: Why is there a 13 in our couple if neither of us has one?
faq.a: That is how it should be. 13 in a couple’s matrix comes only from a sum of exactly 13, so at that point each of you has a smaller number: for example, 5 and 8 or 3 and 10. Neither has a thirteenth of their own there — the energy of change is created by the union itself, and you will be living through it for the first time, together.

faq.q: What does 13 under the heart mean in compatibility?
faq.a: In a couple’s matrix the under-the-heart point is called “what connects”. With 13 you are brought closer by shared beginnings: a move, a home of your own, a new life after a hard period. Such couples find it easier to make up through doing something together — clearing out the old and deciding what will replace it.

faq.q: How can we find where our 13 is without a calculator?
faq.a: One point is easy: add up your months of birth. If the total is 13, for example May and August, 13 stands in the “why you met” point. The other points, including the centre and the couple’s tail, are calculated from the two people’s full matrices, and they need a calculation from two dates.

faq.q: If we both have 13 in our personal matrices, are we compatible?
faq.a: Matching numbers in personal charts are not compatibility. If both have 13 in the same point, the couple’s matrix will have not 13 but 8 there: 13 + 13 = 26, and 2 + 6 = 8. A shared experience of change will help you understand each other, but the union has to be read from the couple’s matrix.

faq.q: Is 13 in a couple connected with the death of one of the partners?
faq.a: No. Neither in a personal matrix nor in a couple’s matrix does the Death arcanum speak of dying or of how long anyone will live, and the method makes no such predictions. In a couple 13 is about the completion of stages: relations with parents, past unions, an old way of life.

seo.title: Destiny matrix compatibility 14: Temperance in a couple
seo.description: Destiny matrix compatibility 14: a union that negotiates. Where Temperance occurs, what it means in the centre, tail and money, and when only one gives way.

items.title: Arcanum 14 in a compatibility matrix: Temperance and the art of agreement
items.short: 14 in destiny matrix compatibility is Temperance, the energy of measure and harmony. A couple with it argues with words rather than slammed doors, knows how to live within its means and can bring together very different people — in character, habits, faith, family. The reverse side is an imbalance in which the same partner always gives way. Below is how 14 appears in a couple’s matrix, where it occurs, what it means in the centre, in the tasks, in money and in the children points, and what helps a couple with this energy.

sections.h2: Where 14 in a couple’s matrix comes from
paragraphs: A couple’s matrix is a third chart built from two personal ones. The scheme was described in most detail by Yuliana Lisovskaya in her book Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024): the matching points of two people are added together, and a sum above 22 is reduced by adding its digits. The points have their own meaning in a couple: the couple’s centre, for example, is the atmosphere between the partners, not the character of either one.

14 in a couple always comes from a sum of exactly 14. Larger sums, from 23 to 44, give no more than 12 once their digits are added, so there is no other way. Hence a simple consequence: at the point where a couple has 14, each partner has a smaller number — 5 and 9, 6 and 8, 3 and 11. Neither has a Temperance of their own there: a couple does not bring measure and harmony with them but works them out together.

The centre, the fourteenth’s most frequent point, is calculated from the full matrices. An example: the dates 12.06.1990 and 25.11.1986. The centre of the first chart is 11, of the second 3, together 14. In all, five combinations of personal centres give a couple’s centre of 14: 3 and 11, 4 and 10, 5 and 9, 6 and 8, 7 and 7. The last is curious: two people with The Chariot in the centre — the energy of drive and movement — together get Temperance. Two fast, decisive people learn to slow down beside each other.

The second most frequent point can be checked in your head. The “why you met” point adds the months of birth: February and December, March and November, April and October, May and September, June and August, or both in July give 14.

sections.h2: Where 14 occurs and how often
paragraphs: In a couple’s matrix the fourteenth occurs in 14 points. It never appears in the common language point, where the couple’s tail begins: only multiples of three come up there.

paragraphs: Lisovskaya describes the energy by spheres of the couple’s life rather than for each point. For the points she has no separate words on — the children points, for example — what follows is our reading based on the meaning of the point and the arcanum.

sections.h2: 14 in the couple’s centre: an atmosphere of harmony
paragraphs: The centre is what happens between you without witnesses. With 14 the question here is one of measure: how much closeness and how much of one’s own each needs, how much activity and how much rest.

**In the plus** you resolve contradictions by talking. An argument about where to spend the holiday ends not in a grudge but in a plan: a week at the sea for one, a week in the mountains for the other, or a third option nobody thought of at first. Each understands the other’s needs — not only hears the words but sees when the partner is tired. The couple has a balance between doing things and quiet time together, and gratitude and patience are said out loud. Peace of mind is valued above things here: better a small flat and calm evenings than a big one and quarrels over a loan. The partners are often close in position, sometimes in profession too — it is easy for them to understand each other’s work.

**In the minus** the balance breaks one way. One partner always gives way — in choosing the holiday, in spending, in whose parents to visit for the holidays — and the other does not even notice. There is no common language, conversations stall, and it grows cold between the two. The feeling of safety disappears, jealousy appears, sometimes attempts at control — checking up, calling, demanding explanations. There is another imbalance too: one shuts themselves off from family problems and pretends they do not exist, while the other carries them alone. In the worst case both stop understanding why they are in this relationship.

sections.h2: Why you met: to bring different things together
paragraphs: This point is read only in the plus: what the couple is to create together. Lisovskaya has no separate text on it for 14, and the meaning is derived from the energy’s plus. With Temperance the couple’s task is to find the middle where each alone would go to an extreme. People of different temperaments, cultures, faiths, habits and sometimes countries meet, and together they create a third way of living — not his and not hers, but shared.

In everyday life this looks like constantly assembling compromises. A holiday table from two cuisines. If the family has two languages, the child grows up with both. Holidays by turns: this time one chooses, next time the other. The meeting is needed so that both learn patience and see that difference does not drive people apart if it is given room.
In the sphere “Why you met” this point stands next to the image of the couple. If 14 stands in both, it is especially visible from outside: a union where very different people keep their balance.

sections.h2: The couple’s tasks: 14 in the tail
paragraphs: In the reading the couple’s karmic tail is three points: entry to the task, the middle and the main task. 14 occurs in the main task (about 6–7 couples in 100) and in the middle (about 4 in 100). These points are read mostly through the minus — as trials on which the couple grows.
The main task with 14 is to reach agreement and not lose it. The trials on the way:

ul: **haste** — deciding for the partner what they think without hearing them out; drawing conclusions from a single act;
**suppressed feelings** — keeping quiet about dissatisfaction until it bursts out over a trifle;
**idealisation and perfectionism** — expecting flawlessness from the partner and the relationship, and then being disappointed;
**other people’s opinions** — living with an eye on parents, friends and neighbours more than on what the two of you need;
**control** — a wish to manage the partner, their time, their circle;
**betrayed trust** and a lost balance, after which the union has to be put back together.

paragraphs: If 14 stands in the middle of the tail, it shows the way to the main task: through patience, through the ability to wait for the right moment for a conversation and not to act rashly.

sections.h2: Under the heart: what connects a couple with 14
paragraphs: The “what connects” point is the one searches call “under the heart”: in a personal matrix the same point of the relationship line carries that label. In a couple it shows the positive potential — the events and questions around which two people grow closer.

With 14, what connects you is a good conversation: the kind after which both feel lighter, though you started from different positions. Shared plans worked out together bring you closer, as does any situation where you found the middle — agreed about children, money, relatives. Calm rituals work well: evening tea without phones, a walk at weekends, a talk about the week. In the sphere “Relationship and common language” this point stands next to the point of success and status: with 14 under the heart, one partner’s successes do not become a competition if they are talked about as the family’s achievement.

sections.h2: 14 in the couple’s money
paragraphs: The finances of a couple with Temperance are about balancing income and spending, not about bursts.

ul: **Where it leaks and how success affects the union** (about 5 couples in 100). The holes of 14 are imbalance: one saves, the other spends; one depends entirely on the other’s money. Prosperity for show belongs here too — expensive things for others to see — and envy of those who have more. When one earns noticeably more, the balance is easily lost, and a conversation about money turns into a conversation about power.
**Way into money** (about 4 in 100): income stalls because of impulse purchases and a budget without a plan. A simple rule helps: discuss a big purchase in advance and wait at least a week.

**Path to prosperity** (about 3–4 in 100): living within one’s means without fuss or keeping up with the neighbours. The couple is content with what it has, knows how to wait for the moment to buy, helps those close to them and always pays back what it borrows — and the same comes back to it.
**Attitude to material things** (fewer than 2 in 100): order without clutter, spending in tune with income.

sections.h2: The couple’s image, what fills it and what can spoil it
paragraphs: **How others see the couple.** Modest, calm, tolerant, hard-working, making sure everyone around them is comfortable. “Just like everyone else” is what people might say of them, and there is no reproach in it: such people are the ones others lean on. Sometimes it is a union of people of different cultures or faiths who keep their balance. In the minus something else is visible from outside: one always gives way, and the other does not notice.

**What fills the union.** Calm time together, making things together — from renovation to a shared hobby — the partner’s charm and taste, the feeling that life is going to plan. A couple with 14 recovers not in a noisy crowd but on quiet weekends when there is no need to hurry anywhere.

**What can spoil it.** Coldness, no common language, jealousy and arguments in which nobody hears the other. The most insidious is one-sided giving way: for years one agrees for the sake of peace, and then the peace collapses all at once because what has built up breaks through.

sections.h2: The couple as parents: 14 in the children points
paragraphs: **What you teach** (about 4 couples in 100). With 14 a child learns measure and patience from you: to negotiate rather than fight over a toy; to wait rather than demand at once; to respect those who live differently. In a family where two cultures or two traditions meet this is especially visible: the child grows up thinking that different things can live side by side. In the minus the parents pull in different directions — one allows everything, the other forbids everything — and the child quickly learns to play on it.

**Parents together** (about 2 in 100). A tandem in which the parents stand in for and support each other: when one is tired, the other takes the evening on without keeping score or reproaching. The minus is when everything falls on one, and the other considers that normal.

sections.h2: What helps a couple with 14

ul: Don’t jump to conclusions about your partner: ask first, then decide.
Don’t project your fears and wishes onto them — “you should want the same as I do”.
Keep an eye on the tally of giving way: if the same partner always gives way, the balance is already lost, even if there are no quarrels.
Plan the budget together and avoid impulse purchases.
Be able to wait for the right moment for a hard conversation — but don’t put it off for years.
Look for the middle instead of extremes; develop the ability to listen and to empathise.
If a conversation does not work, bring in a third person — a family counsellor — not relatives.

paragraphs: The method gives no compatibility percentages: 14 in a couple’s matrix speaks of what the couple needs to work on, not of whether the two people suit each other.

faq.q: Is 14 in compatibility a good couple?
faq.a: The method has no good and bad arcana of a couple. 14 gives a union the ability to negotiate and keep its balance, but in the minus that balance breaks: one gives way, and the other gets used to it. Which side shows depends on what the couple does with its disagreements.

faq.q: We both have a centre of 7, and the couple has 14 — is that possible?
faq.a: Yes, 7 + 7 = 14, and it is one of the five combinations of personal centres that give 14 in the couple’s centre. The others are 3 and 11, 4 and 10, 5 and 9, 6 and 8. Two energies of movement and drive together give an atmosphere of measure: beside each other you learn to slow down.

faq.q: What does 14 under the heart mean in compatibility?
faq.a: In a couple’s matrix it is the “what connects” point. With 14 you are brought closer by conversations after which both feel lighter, shared plans and compromises found — over money, children, relatives. For such a couple calm shared rituals matter more than loud events.

faq.q: We are very different. Does 14 in the couple help?
faq.a: Temperance in a couple’s matrix is precisely about a union of different people — in temperament, habits, culture or faith. Difference does not drive people apart if it is given room: both families’ holidays, two languages at home, holidays by turns. The danger is not the difference but one partner’s silent habit of always adapting.

faq.q: One of us always gives way. Is that the minus of 14?
faq.a: It looks like it. One-sided giving way is the main minus of Temperance in a couple: it is quiet from outside, there are no quarrels, but the peace rests on one person. The way out is not for the one who gives way to start fighting, but for both to count out loud who last chose the holiday, the spending, the celebrations, and agree to take turns.

seo.title: Destiny matrix compatibility 15: The Devil in a couple
seo.description: Destiny matrix compatibility 15: every point where The Devil occurs, passion and drive in the plus, control and jealousy in the minus, an example and advice.

items.title: Arcanum 15 in a compatibility matrix: The Devil in a couple — attraction and freedom
items.short: 15 in destiny matrix compatibility is The Devil, the energy of attraction, desire and drive. It gives a couple passion, the courage to talk about their wishes and ambitious shared goals, and it tests them with one question: are you together of your own free will, or because you cannot tear yourselves away? Below is where 15 comes from in a couple’s matrix, what it means in all 16 points where it occurs, in the plus and in the minus, and what helps such a couple.

sections.h2: How 15 ends up in a couple’s matrix
paragraphs: A compatibility matrix is calculated like this: an ordinary destiny matrix is built for each partner by date of birth, then the matching points are added together — centre with centre, day with day, task with task — and the sum is reduced to a number from 1 to 22. If the sum is above 22, its digits are added. The result is a third chart — the couple’s matrix. Yuliana Lisovskaya described this method and the meaning of the couple’s points in most detail in her book Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024): the points there do not mean what they mean in a personal chart.

A sum above 22 gives no more than 12 after its digits are added. So 15 in a couple comes only from a sum of exactly 15, and at that point each partner has a number below fifteen. Even if one of you has 15 in their personal matrix, it is not at the point where the couple has 15: the couple gives birth to the fifteenth itself.

The couple’s centre is the fifteenth’s second most frequent place after “The couple’s values” (covered below), and there is a paradox here. A personal matrix never has 15 in the centre: a person’s centre is 3–14, 16, 18, 20 or 22. Yet 15 stands in the couple’s centre for about 9 couples in 100 — the second most frequent number of a couple’s centre after 16. Five combinations of personal centres give it: 3 and 12, 4 and 11, 5 and 10, 6 and 9, 7 and 8. An example: the dates 06.11.1986 and 13.08.1984. The centre of the first matrix is 10, of the second 5, 15 in total. Neither of these people has or could have The Devil in their centre, but their couple does.

The third most frequent point can be checked without a calculation: the “why you met” point adds the months of birth. March and December, April and November, May and October, June and September, July and August give 15.

sections.h2: All the points where a couple can have 15
paragraphs: In a couple’s matrix the fifteenth has 16 possible points — more than most arcana: it even occurs in the common language and in “The couple’s values”, where only multiples of three come up.
