paragraphs: Lisovskaya sets out the energy by sphere — image, atmosphere, finances, tasks — rather than for each point. Where the author has no separate text, what follows is our reading based on the meaning of the point and the arcanum.

sections.h2: The atmosphere inside the couple: 15 in the centre
paragraphs: The couple’s centre is what happens between two people away from view. With The Devil it is always hot here.

**In the plus** this is a couple where you can want things seriously. You talk openly about your desires — from intimacy to money and career — and do not shame each other for them. The partner’s dark sides are no news here and no reason to leave: they are known, accepted, and mistakes are forgiven. The support is powerful: if one decides to take a risk — start their own business, move, change profession — the other does not lecture but works out where to save. There is passion and a readiness to change for love. Sometimes it was this very union that helped one of the partners get out of a destructive relationship.

An important caveat from the author: even in the plus, one partner may want to possess the other. Hence hurt and jealousy where there is no cause — a short exchange of messages with a colleague, an evening with friends, being late at work. This is not a minus but a property of the energy, better known about in advance.

**In the minus** only attraction holds the couple together. Quarrels die down in an embrace, but none of them gets resolved. Pressure and domination appear, manipulation, a wish to own: checking the phone, an account of every evening, “you’re mine” in the sense of “you belong to me”. Drama becomes a habit, calm feels like boredom, and in a conversation nobody hears anybody.

sections.h2: Why you met: to break free
paragraphs: This point is read only in the plus: what the couple needs to create together. Lisovskaya has an observation about exactly this point: in her experience, 15 here very often means breaking free of a dependence. It can be anything that held a person: a harmful habit, a destructive relationship, a job they are afraid to leave, debts, the power of parents. The couple meets in order to become freer together than each was alone.

In everyday life this looks like a shared project of liberation. One gives up what was destroying them, the other is beside them — without lectures, with support. Together they pay off a loan that had been hanging over them for years. They make up their minds to live by their own rules, not as relatives expect. Wishes each had kept quiet about become a shared goal — and the couple pursues it with the grip the fifteenth gives.

In the sphere “Why you met” the image of the couple stands next to it. If there is a strong energy there too, their meanings add up: why you are in each other’s lives and how the union looks to people.

sections.h2: The couple’s tasks: where The Devil tests the union
paragraphs: The couple’s karmic tail has three points: entry to the task, the middle and the main task. 15 occurs in all three points: in the main task for almost 7 couples in 100, at the entry for 4, in the middle for 3. These points are read mostly through the minus: they are trials the couple learns from.
The fifteenth’s trials:

ul: **control** — checking up, surveillance, jealousy, bans dressed up as care;
**dependence** — material, when one cannot leave because they live on the other’s money, and any other kind;
**attempts to hold on to** the partner through intimacy, a child, money or status instead of reaching agreement;
**obsession** with a person, fear of losing them and a sense of hopelessness;
**silence about one’s wishes**: each wants their own thing and waits for the other to guess;
**a union that drags you down**: one leads the other from the plus into the minus — into debt, dubious schemes, a way of life that makes both worse;
**going back** to former destructive relationships or old habits.

paragraphs: The main task is to understand the thought with which Lisovskaya ends her chapter on the fifteenth: nobody belongs to anybody. A union with 15 in the tail grows stronger when each could leave — and stays of their own free will.

sections.h2: Common language: 15 in the point of desires
paragraphs: The fifteenth has this point and its neighbours 14 and 16 do not: only 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 and 21 come up here. 15 comes from combinations of personal points of 3 and 12 or 6 and 9 — for about 4 couples in 100. In the couple reading it stands in two spheres at once: in “Relationship and common language” as the common language, and in “The couple’s karmic tail” as the entry to the task.

The meaning of the point is what the couple strives for, its shared wishes and agreements. With 15 the wishes are strong and shared: a home, money, status, intimacy, travel — the couple wants a great deal and knows how to get it. Agreement is easiest when the wishes are named directly: “in three years I want my own business”, “I want a second child”, “I want more time for myself”. But this point stands on the line of tasks, so it can also work as resistance: one partner’s wishes suppress the other’s, and agreements are made under pressure. Then “we want” really means “I want, and you agree”.

sections.h2: 15 under the heart: what connects the couple
paragraphs: In searches the “what connects” point is called “under the heart”: that is how the same point of the relationship line is labelled in a personal matrix. In a couple it shows the positive potential — the events and questions that bring two people closer.

With 15, what connects you is bold desires and honesty about them. The moment when one confesses something they kept quiet about for years, and the other neither laughs nor judges, brings you closer. So do shared risky decisions you made as two and pulled off — a move, a business, a big purchase. And so does a shared victory over what held you: a debt paid off, a habit dropped, a talk with your parents after which you finally live as your own family. This point stands between the common language and the point of success and status: with 15 under the heart, one partner’s success becomes a shared pride if wishes are talked about rather than guessed.

sections.h2: 15 in the couple’s money
paragraphs: A couple with The Devil has a real appetite for money. The question is who is in charge of whom — you of the money, or it of you.

ul: **Where it leaks and how status affects the union** (about 5 couples in 100). The fifteenth’s holes are greed and a thirst for fast money. One pushes the other towards a dubious decision “for the family”; one is forever dissatisfied with the other’s earnings, compares and presses. When status and income become the measure of a person, the union starts to rest on money.

**Way into money** (about 4 in 100): income stalls because of a gambling streak — risky investments, easy money that promises a lot and fast. A simple limit helps avoid this: how much you can lose without harming the family, and not a penny more.

**Path to prosperity** (about 4 in 100): clear shared goals, hard but well-paid work, extra earnings, investments. Prosperity is sturdier when there is honesty and generosity in it: a couple with no debts and room for charity.
**Attitude to material things** (about 2 in 100): the ability to earn and to spend with pleasure; in the minus — things as a way to hold on to love or to buy it.

sections.h2: The couple’s image, what fills it and what can spoil it
paragraphs: **How others see the couple.** A passionate, vivid, unusual couple, often successful and with status. They think freely, are not afraid of experiments, and people feel a little uneasy and very curious around them. Sometimes people know their story: together they got out of what held them. In the minus the image darkens: a couple who indulge each other in everything, passive aggression in public, habits that those around them notice before the partners themselves do.

**What fills the union.** Bold wishes said out loud, variety, freedom and trust, sincerity. And — unexpectedly for The Devil — discipline: a shared routine, sport, order in their affairs. A couple with 15 recovers when passion and excitement go together with structure rather than instead of it.

**What can spoil it.** Jealousy, pressure, a wish to possess, dramatising. Every argument quickly becomes a question of power: who will give way to whom, who will keep hold of whom. A quarrel does not solve the problem; it tests who holds on harder.

sections.h2: The couple as parents: 15 in the children points
paragraphs: **What you teach** (about 4 couples in 100). With 15 you teach a child to want boldly and to achieve their aims — and to know the limit. It is good when at home you can openly say “I want” and get an honest answer rather than shame. The minus is control: choosing the child’s friends, clubs and future profession for them, keeping hold of them with money and presents.

**Parents together** (about 2–3 in 100). A strong tandem with a shared goal — to give the children opportunities the parents never had. In the minus the child becomes a battlefield in a struggle for power or a way of holding on to the partner, and the author names this plainly among the fifteenth’s tasks.

sections.h2: The couple’s values: together of your own free will
paragraphs: The fifteenth’s most frequent point is “The couple’s values”, one of the five main cards of the reading: 15 stands here for 11 couples in 100. The number of this point is not added up from the partners’ points but recalculated from the couple’s purposes, so only multiples of three occur in it. For Lisovskaya it is the couple’s spiritual purpose — its values and the path the two are to walk together.

**With 15 in the values, what matters most is staying together by choice, not on a chain.** The Devil brings the force of desire and honesty about the dark side: here people say out loud what they want, even the awkward things, and let each other go to work up north for six months if one of them needs it. The minus is when the wish to be close becomes the wish to own: checking the phone, choosing the other’s friends, holding them with money or guilt.

sections.h2: Plus or minus: five questions for a couple with 15
paragraphs: The same energy gives both a passion that holds by love and a grip that holds by habit. Simple questions help tell one from the other — an honest answer to them will say more than the number in the matrix.

ol: Can you spend an evening apart without reporting where you were and with whom?
After a quarrel, do you agree on the substance — or only make up, so that a month later it all happens again?
Does each of you know what the other really wants — from a holiday to plans for five years?
Do you discuss money without reproaches and comparisons with other people’s incomes?
If you imagine that both of you were free to leave — would you stay?

paragraphs: If the answer to most of the questions is “yes”, the fifteenth works in the plus in your couple. If “no”, it is not a verdict but a list of where to start the conversation.

sections.h2: What helps a couple with 15

ul: Talk about your wishes out loud, secret ones included — and listen to your partner’s without mocking.
Learn to master your emotions and settle conflicts peacefully: an agreement, not a making-up after a storm.
Leave harmful habits behind together: shared sport, a shared routine, a shared house rule.
Give the family more time than work when work starts eating up everything.
Don’t buy love with presents and don’t hold on to your partner with money, a child or status.
Set shared goals — and check that they are shared, not just one person’s.
Remember the main thing: nobody belongs to anybody. Good relationships with 15 are those in which both could leave and stay of their own free will.

paragraphs: The method gives no compatibility percentages. 15 in a couple’s matrix is neither a verdict nor a promise of eternal passion, but the theme of the union: an attraction that either makes both of you freer or keeps you on a chain.

faq.q: Which arcana is 15 compatible with?
faq.a: The method has no lists like “15 goes with 3 and 6, not with 4 and 9”, and 15 in a personal matrix makes no one incompatible with anyone. Compatibility is read from the couple’s matrix: the matching points of two charts are added together, and you look at what came out in each point of the couple. A query of two numbers, such as “15 and 6”, is a combination of arcana within one matrix — a separate topic.

faq.q: Why do we have 15 in the couple’s centre if a personal matrix never has it there?
faq.a: The couple’s centre is the sum of two personal centres. A person’s centre is never 15, but the sum of two centres can be: 7 and 8, 6 and 9, 5 and 10, 4 and 11, 3 and 12. So the atmosphere of the fifteenth appears only in a couple: it is an energy two people create together.

faq.q: What does 15 under the heart mean in compatibility?
faq.a: In a couple’s matrix it is the “what connects” point. With 15 you are brought closer by bold desires and honesty about them, by shared risky decisions you managed to pull off, and by a shared victory over what held each of you — a debt, a habit, someone else’s power.

faq.q: Does 15 in a couple mean infidelity and dependence?
faq.a: No. Lisovskaya lists the fifteenth’s minuses, dependencies included, but these are possible scenarios of the energy, not facts about a particular couple. In the plus the same energy gives passion, powerful support and the courage to talk about desires. The matrix shows a theme to work on, not something that has already happened.

faq.q: We both have 15 in our personal matrices. Is that good for the couple?
faq.a: Matching numbers in personal charts are not yet compatibility. If both have 15 in the same point, the couple’s matrix will have 3 there: 15 + 15 = 30, and 3 + 0 = 3. A shared language of desires will help you understand each other, but the union is read from the couple’s matrix, not from coincidences.

faq.q: What does 15 in the “why you met” point mean?
faq.a: It is the sum of the months of birth, for example May and October. In Lisovskaya’s observation, 15 here is very often connected with breaking free of a dependence. The meaning of the meeting is to free yourselves together from what held each of you and to turn the fifteenth’s grip towards shared goals.

seo.title: Destiny matrix compatibility 16: The Tower in a couple
seo.description: Destiny matrix compatibility 16: a union that grows stronger through trials. Where The Tower stands and how a couple can get through crises together.

items.title: Arcanum 16 in a compatibility matrix: The Tower — a union that grows stronger through trials
items.short: 16 in destiny matrix compatibility is The Tower, the energy of sudden change and of a truth that can no longer be ignored. In a couple’s matrix it does not predict a break-up. Its main idea in Yuliana Lisovskaya’s reading: trials gone through together make a union stronger. Below is how 16 appears in a couple’s matrix, why it is the most frequent number of the couple’s centre, what The Tower means at each point, and how a couple with it can get through crises without destroying each other.

sections.h2: How The Tower appears in a couple’s matrix
paragraphs: Compatibility by the destiny matrix is calculated from two dates of birth. Each partner’s personal matrix is built, then the matching points are added together and the sum is reduced to 22: if it is larger, its digits are added. This method is described in most detail in Lisovskaya’s book Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024). The couple’s points are read in their own way: the centre, for example, is the shared atmosphere between the two people, not anyone’s character.

16 in a couple comes only from a sum of exactly 16: sums from 23 to 44 give no more than 12 after their digits are added. So at the point where the couple has The Tower, each of you has a number below sixteen. If one partner has 16 in the centre of their personal matrix, the couple’s centre will be anything but 16. The couple’s Tower is created by the meeting itself.

16 stands in the couple’s centre for about 10 couples in 100 — more often than any other number. The explanation is arithmetical: most people’s centre is between 5 and 11, around 8 on average, and the sum of two centres most often ends up near 16. There are six combinations: 3 and 13, 4 and 12, 5 and 11, 6 and 10, 7 and 9, 8 and 8. There is an example in the book itself: for the couple with the dates 12.03.1963 and 05.10.1966 the personal centres are 5 and 11, and the couple’s centre is 16. The author’s conclusion about this couple is worth remembering for anyone with The Tower in the centre: what is said in a quarrel stays in the memory for a long time, so sharp edges are best avoided.

One point can be checked without a calculation: the “why you met” point adds the months of birth. April and December, May and November, June and October, July and September, or both in August give 16.

paragraphs: Lisovskaya writes about the energy by sphere — image, atmosphere, finances, tasks — rather than for each point separately. Where the author has no text of her own, what follows is our reading based on the meaning of the point and the arcanum.

sections.h2: The couple’s centre: an atmosphere tempered by trials
paragraphs: The centre is what is between you when nobody is watching. The Tower here means the couple’s life will not be smooth, and the question is how you get over the bumps.

**In the plus** it is very strong support. You go through any trial hand in hand: redundancy, a move, a renovation that dragged on for a year, a hard period for your parents. One takes on the other’s problems when they cannot cope. In unexpected trouble you stay calm and make serious decisions quickly — sell the car, move, change jobs — without months of doubt. You see each other’s potential and help it unfold, and you respect the partner’s outlook even when it differs from yours. Hence a feeling of stability that, paradoxically, comes not from a calm life but from the certainty that together you will withstand anything.

**In the minus** the tension comes out. Irritation and aggression over trifles, mutual jealousy and barbs, threats to leave as a way of applying pressure: “one more time and I’m gone”. Duties are not shared out, and each is sure they carry more. The partner’s needs are ignored until they explode. For The Tower, words said at the breaking point are especially dangerous: they cannot be taken back, and they are remembered for years.

sections.h2: The couple’s tasks: the collapse of an invented image
paragraphs: The couple’s karmic tail is made up of three points: entry to the task, the middle and the main task. 16 occurs in the main task (about 7 couples in 100) and in the middle (about 2–3 in 100), but not at the entry. These points are read mostly through the minus.

The Tower’s main trial is the collapse of an invented image. At first each falls in love with a picture: reliable, cheerful, practical, romantic. Then the picture collapses — the partner turns out not to be the person the imagination drew. The task of a couple with 16 in the tail is to live through this moment and get to know the real person, rather than leave to look for a new picture.

ul: **loss of self-control** — decisions made in the heat of the moment, a slammed door, things said in anger;
**a run of hard situations** to be lived through together: it seems the troubles never end, and it is important not to start blaming each other for them;
**going to an extreme** — one seeks salvation in the spiritual, the other in the material, and they stop understanding each other;
**looking different ways in trouble** — when something bad happens, each goes through it alone, looking in their own direction.

paragraphs: If 16 stands in the middle of the tail, it shows the way to the main task: through crises that bring to light what had been kept quiet.

sections.h2: Why you met: to build something of your own
paragraphs: This point is read only in the plus — what the couple needs to create together. Lisovskaya has no separate text for 16 here, and the meaning is derived from the energy’s plus. With The Tower a couple meets in order to build something of its own where something collapsed. The acquaintance often happens at a breaking point for one or both: after losing a job, a divorce, a move, when the old life has already fallen apart and the new one has not yet begun.

Such couples build together in the literal sense: a house, a country cottage, a renovation, a business from scratch. The story of how they met is often unusual — stuck together in a lift, got talking in a queue for paperwork after a flood, met somewhere neither had meant to be. The meeting is needed so that both can see: from the rubble you can put together something sturdier than before.

sections.h2: 16 under the heart: what connects the couple
paragraphs: In the couple reading this point is called “what connects”, and in searches it is looked for as “under the heart” — after the label of the same point in a personal matrix. It shows what brings you closer.

With 16, what connects you is what you have lived through together. A night at an airport when every flight was cancelled, the first winter in an unfinished house, a year when there was no money at all — afterwards you say “we got through that” and feel bound more tightly than by vows. Shared building projects connect you too — from a renovation to a business — and many small happy moments between the big events. In the sphere “Relationship and common language” this point stands next to the point of success and status: with 16 under the heart, one partner’s sudden failure does not drive the couple apart if the other says “we’ll manage”.

sections.h2: The money of a couple with The Tower
paragraphs: The Tower’s finances are about suddenness. What matters is not whether a change will happen but whether the couple is ready for it.

ul: **Where it leaks and how status affects the union** (about 5 couples in 100). The holes are a sudden loss of job or income, after which the whole way of life has to be rebuilt; fear of change; a habit of expecting the worst, which itself gets in the way of taking risks where they are worth taking.

**Way into money** (about 4 in 100): income stalls because of different views on money. The partners often grew up in families with different levels of wealth, and what seems a normal expense to one looks like extravagance to the other. A rule invented by the two of you, rather than inherited from parents, helps.

**Path to prosperity** (about 4 in 100): a shared budget and large joint investments, building something together, strict discipline by rules you wrote yourselves. System and patience are what turn the energy of change into capital.
**Attitude to material things** (about 2 in 100): care for things — mending rather than throwing away; in the minus — living in expectation of a catastrophe.

sections.h2: How the couple is seen, what fills it and what can spoil it
paragraphs: **How others see the couple.** Active people with an unusual story of how they met, who are always building, renovating, making something. From outside the couple may seem anxious — too ready for the worst. In the minus the image becomes one of eternal unlucky ones to whom something is always happening. A large age gap or completely different views on life may also set tongues wagging.

**What fills the union.** Making things together, looking after the home together, spiritual practices, the ability to accept what cannot be changed. And above all — many small happy moments: coffee on the balcony you have just glazed, an evening when everything finally worked out. Passion fills The Tower too — especially after making up.

**What can spoil it.** Aggression and irritation, ultimatums, jealousy and barbs. Two scenarios are recognisable. The first is the dam: one keeps quiet for years, stores up grievances, and then leaves, and the partner cannot understand what happened. The second is the demolition: one stages stress tests — a quarrel, an ultimatum, an “either-or” — to make sure they are loved. Most dangerous of all is the habit of having it out at the peak of emotion: The Tower remembers every word.

sections.h2: Children: 16 in the parents points
paragraphs: **What you teach** (about 4–5 couples in 100). With The Tower you teach a child not to fear change and to tell the truth, even an awkward one. The child sees that after something hard you can rebuild: a move, a change of school, a loss is not the end of the world. In the minus they grow up expecting a catastrophe or in an atmosphere of quarrels that break out without warning.

**Parents together** (about 3 in 100). A tandem that holds firm in hard periods: the first year with a baby, sleepless months, adolescence — the parents do not share out blame but share out night duty. The minus is when in trouble each pulls their own way, and the child ends up caught in the crossfire.

sections.h2: Scheduled maintenance instead of emergency repairs: what helps

ul: Talk about what is creaking while it is still small: once a month, a calm conversation about what has built up.
Agree in advance: in a quarrel nobody threatens to leave and nobody goes for a sore spot.
In a crisis, first name what in the relationship is worth keeping, and only then decide what to take apart.
Treasure the small good moments and keep the focus on the good.
Make up and build the relationship through creativity and things you do with your hands together.
Try new things without hasty decisions or needless risk: a cushion before the change, not after.
Spare each other’s strength and don’t brush it off when your partner is struggling.
Decide together and support each other in hard times — even if only one of you caused the trouble.

paragraphs: This is the author’s practice, not a forecast: 16 in a couple does not predict a break-up, and the method gives no compatibility percentages.

faq.q: Does The Tower in compatibility mean a break-up?
faq.a: No. In a couple’s matrix The Tower speaks of crises, not of the end of the union. Lisovskaya puts its key like this: trials gone through together make a relationship stronger. A break-up is one possible outcome of the minus, not something written in the matrix.

faq.q: Why does 16 stand in the couple’s centre so often?
faq.a: The couple’s centre is the sum of two personal centres. Most people’s centre is between 5 and 11, around 8 on average, and the sum of two such numbers is most often close to 16. That is why The Tower is the most frequent number of a couple’s centre: it stands there for about 10 couples in 100.

faq.q: One of us has 16 in the centre of their personal matrix. Is that the same thing?
faq.a: No, these are different things. A personal centre of 16 is about the person’s character. The couple’s centre is the sum of two centres, and if one is already 16, the sum will be greater than 16 and give a different number. For example, 16 and 3 give 19, and 16 and 7 give 23, that is, 5.

faq.q: What does 16 under the heart mean in compatibility?
faq.a: In a couple’s matrix it is the “what connects” point. With 16 you are brought closer by what you have lived through together: hard periods after which you say “we got through that”, shared building projects and renovations, small joys between the big events.

faq.q: What should a couple with 16 do in a crisis?
faq.a: First agree on the rules of a quarrel: no threats to leave and no going for sore spots. Then name what is valuable in the relationship and what you will definitely keep, and only after that sort out what has broken. The Tower forgives a crisis but does not easily forgive words said at its peak.

seo.title: Destiny matrix compatibility 17: The Star in a couple
seo.description: Destiny matrix compatibility 17: a union that inspires. Where The Star occurs, what it means in the centre, image and tasks, and when a couple becomes a show.

items.title: Arcanum 17 in a compatibility matrix: The Star — a couple that inspires
items.short: 17 in destiny matrix compatibility is The Star, the energy of inspiration, hope and sincerity. A couple with it often discovers only together who they want to be, and does not hide its feelings — a rare case when the pretty picture of a relationship turns out to be true. The Star’s shadow is a shop window instead of a life and lightness without responsibility. Below is how 17 gets into a couple’s matrix, where it occurs, what it means in the centre, the image, the tasks and money, and what helps such a couple.

sections.h2: Where 17 in a couple’s matrix comes from
paragraphs: A couple’s matrix is built from two personal matrices: the partners’ matching points are added together, and a sum above 22 is reduced by adding its digits. Yuliana Lisovskaya described this in most detail in her book Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024), and in her reading the couple’s points have their own meanings: the centre is the shared atmosphere between two people, the day is the couple’s image for others, the month is why the couple met.

17 comes only from a sum of exactly 17: anything above 22 gives 12 or less once its digits are added. At the point where the couple has The Star, each partner has a number of their own, below seventeen. A couple does not bring the energy of inspiration with it — it lights it itself.

The seventeenth’s most frequent point is the centre, and here The Star shows something impossible in a personal chart. A person’s centre never holds 17: only 3–14, 16, 18, 20 and 22 stand there. Yet in a couple’s centre 17 occurs for about 9 couples in 100. Six combinations of personal centres give a couple’s centre of 17: 3 and 14, 4 and 13, 5 and 12, 6 and 11, 7 and 10, 8 and 9. An example: the dates 03.06.1985 and 10.12.1993. The centre of the first matrix is 10, of the second 7, together 17.

Two points can be checked from the dates without a calculation. The image of the couple is the sum of the days of birth; numbers above 22 are reduced first: the 23rd gives 5, the 29th 11, the 30th 3. If the sum is 17, The Star stands in the image of the couple. Why you met is the sum of the months: May and December, June and November, July and October, August and September give 17.

sections.h2: Where The Star occurs in a couple’s matrix
paragraphs: 17 occurs in 14 points. It never appears in the common language point, where the couple’s tail begins: only multiples of three come up there.

paragraphs: Lisovskaya’s card for this energy is divided by sphere — image, atmosphere, finances, tasks — rather than by each point. For points without a separate text from the author, what follows is our reading based on the meaning of the point and the arcanum.

sections.h2: The Star in the couple’s centre: a union that inspires both
paragraphs: The couple’s centre is what happens between you when there is no audience.

**In the plus** it is a union that inspires. Often it is together that people understand who they want to be: one writes music no one hears, and the other persuades them to perform; she has dreamt for years of her own patisserie, and her partner is the first to work out how much is needed to start. You say plainly what you like and what you don’t, are not shy of tenderness in public, are patient and know how to forgive. The relationship is simple in a good sense: no games, no checking up, no masks. It is that rare case when the couple in the photographs and the couple in the kitchen are the same people.

**In the minus** being in love does not grow into responsibility. While things are easy, all is well, but as soon as the question of marriage, a shared home or a child comes up, the couple stalls and sometimes splits up. Things are left unsaid. One fits the partner to their ideal and compares them with it, and does not accept their pursuits — “what sort of job is that”. Sometimes the choice of partner was made under pressure from parents, and it is felt for years. There may be shyness that does not pass even after many years, and ultimatums instead of conversations.

sections.h2: The couple’s tasks: where The Star learns responsibility
paragraphs: In the couple reading the karmic tail has three points: entry to the task, the middle and the main task. 17 occurs in the main task (about 6 couples in 100) and in the middle (about 3 in 100), but not at the entry. These points are read mostly through the minus — as trials.
The seventeenth’s trials:

ul: **comparisons** — with exes, with friends, with couples on social media, with the ideal each of you has drawn;
**pride in status** — one puts themselves above the other and belittles them: “I earn the money, I’m better known, I know best”;
**an admirer instead of a partner** — one expects admiration rather than a conversation between equals;
**material dependence**, into which one tries to put the other;
**fear of one’s own dream** — being afraid to pursue it and getting in the way of the partner’s dream so as not to be left behind;
**home life following the parents’ script**, in which neither recognises themselves;
**flirting on the side, threats to leave for someone else, constant criticism**.

paragraphs: The main task is to take responsibility and stay yourself. In the couple Lisovskaya analyses in the book (dates 12.03.1963 and 05.10.1966), 17 stands both in the main task and in the image of the couple. The author draws a conclusion from this: the tasks of such a couple may be lived out in public, before others’ eyes, and outside circumstances affect how the two cope with them.

sections.h2: Why you met: to become yourselves
paragraphs: This point is read only in the plus: what the couple needs to create together. The author has no separate text on it for 17; the meaning is derived from the energy’s plus. The Star here says the couple met so that each could open up and become themselves. The partner becomes the one who believed first: in a talent, a business, a move, a dream others laughed at.

Such couples create things that inspire others too: a shared creative project, a business grown from a hobby, a home people come to for hope. The meeting is needed so that both can see that dreams come true when beside you there is a person who supports them rather than competes with them.

sections.h2: How others see the couple: brightness or a shop window
paragraphs: The image of the couple is the sum of the days of birth, and 17 stands here for about 4 couples in 100.

**In the plus** it is a bright, sincere, open and stylish couple who are a pleasure to watch. Sometimes it is a union of well-known people or professionals in the same field. Those around them feel that these two are fated for each other. A little superstitious — the couple has its own signs and rituals.

**In the minus** — a shop window. The relationship is put on display, and behind the pretty wrapping there is emptiness: perfect photographs from a holiday after which you did not speak for a week. Or the opposite skew: too much openness about private life in public, or else a closed couple whose smiles hide something untrue.

sections.h2: 17 under the heart: what connects the couple
paragraphs: Searches call the “what connects” point “under the heart”: that is how the same point of the relationship line is labelled in a personal matrix. In a couple it shows what brings two people closer.

With 17, what connects you is a shared dream and support for each other’s projects. The evening when one showed the other an unfinished piece of work and heard not criticism but “keep going” brings you closer. So does a success you worked towards together — the first exhibition, the first client, the first trip to the place you dreamed of. This point stands in the sphere “Relationship and common language” next to the point of success and status, and with The Star under the heart one partner’s success takes no light from the other, as long as you remember who believed in whom first.

sections.h2: The money of a couple with The Star

ul: **Way into money** (about 4 couples in 100): income stalls when talents go unused. One draws beautifully but works where that is not needed; the other has been putting off their own business for years. A simple step helps avoid this — give the talent at least one paid attempt.

**Where it leaks and how status affects the union** (about 4 in 100). The Star’s holes are chasing a beautiful life and easy money, debts paid off with new debts, naive trust in those who promise a lot, sudden large purchases, including on one’s looks.

**Path to prosperity** (about 4 in 100): money through creativity and experience, support for each other’s projects, rationality. After big expenses the couple gets new opportunities, there is always some side work or a reserve, and what is earned goes on making shared wishes come true.
**Attitude to material things** (about 2 in 100): things as part of the beauty of life; in the minus — spending on impressions rather than on what is needed.

sections.h2: What fills it and what can spoil it
paragraphs: **What fills the union.** The partner’s charm, walks by the water and in nature, romance and the state of being in love, which such couples know how to prolong for years. And big successes in their work: when things go well for each, the couple gains strength.

**What can spoil it.** Things left unsaid and ultimatums. One is hurt but keeps quiet, the other has no idea until they hear “either you change or I’m leaving”. Comparisons with an ideal also spoil the union: a partner who is constantly compared stops trying.

sections.h2: The couple as parents: 17 in the children points
paragraphs: **What you teach** (about 4 couples in 100). With The Star you teach a child to believe in themselves and not hide their talents: to show a drawing, to sing in front of guests, to dream out loud. In a home where dreams are supported, a child grows up feeling that their aspirations matter. In the minus the parents see the child as a continuation of their own dream — “you’ll be a musician, since it didn’t work out for me” — or compare them with other children.

**Parents together** (about 3 in 100). A couple who are an example to the child: two people, each with work they love, who support each other. The minus is parents competing for the child’s love and admiration.

sections.h2: What helps a couple with The Star

ul: Don’t compare your partner with ideals — neither with exes nor with other people’s husbands and wives.
Don’t get in the way of your partner showing themselves; support their dream, even if it changes your plans.
Let go of past relationships so as not to measure the present one by them.
Take responsibility for serious steps rather than only enjoying the lightness.
Trust and be yourself — without the role your partner expects.
Don’t sacrifice your career for your partner, and don’t make them choose between “me or your work”.
Don’t play at love for an audience: what matters lives at home, not in the feed.

paragraphs: The method gives no compatibility percentages. 17 in a couple’s matrix describes where the union is strong and where it has room to grow, not whether the two people suit each other.

faq.q: Why do we have 17 in the couple’s centre if a personal matrix never has 17 there?
faq.a: The couple’s centre is the sum of two personal centres. A person’s centre is never 17, but the sum of two centres can be: 8 and 9, 7 and 10, 6 and 11, 5 and 12, 4 and 13, 3 and 14. So the atmosphere of The Star appears only in a couple: two people create it together, and neither brings it with them.

faq.q: What does 17 under the heart mean in compatibility?
faq.a: In a couple’s matrix it is the “what connects” point. With 17 you are brought closer by a shared dream, support for each other’s projects and successes you worked towards together. A simple rule works well: be the first to rejoice in your partner’s good fortune.

faq.q: We look like a beautiful couple from outside, but inside it’s empty. Is that 17?
faq.a: It looks like The Star’s minus in the image of the couple: the relationship lives in a shop window, and behind it there is little conversation and closeness. It is not a verdict. It helps to shift attention from how you look to what you do together when nobody is watching — and to start talking about what has gone unsaid.

faq.q: How can we tell whether 17 is in the image of the couple?
faq.a: Add up your days of birth, reducing numbers above 22 first: the 23rd is 5, the 24th 6, the 28th 10, the 30th 3, the 31st 4. If the total is 17, for example the 12th and the 5th, The Star stands in the image of the couple: that is how others see you.

faq.q: What if 17 stands both in the image and in the couple’s tasks?
faq.a: That was the case for the couple Lisovskaya analyses in the book. Her conclusion: the tasks of such a couple are lived out in view, and what happens around them affects how the two cope. It helps to keep a boundary between the shared and the private: deal with hard things at home, not in front of witnesses.

seo.title: Destiny matrix compatibility 18: The Moon in a couple
seo.description: Destiny matrix compatibility 18: understanding without words and a fog of things unsaid. Where The Moon occurs, what it means in a couple and how to keep trust.

items.title: Arcanum 18 in a compatibility matrix: The Moon — a couple who understand without words
items.short: 18 in destiny matrix compatibility is The Moon, the energy of sensitivity, intuition and mystery. A couple with it understand each other without needing words, protect each other’s personal space and discover something new in the partner every year. The Moon’s shadow is fog: things left unsaid, jealousy over what was imagined, secrets that become weapons. Below is where 18 occurs in a couple’s matrix, what it means in the centre, the common language, the tasks and money, and how a couple with The Moon can clear the fog.

sections.h2: How The Moon gets into a couple’s matrix
paragraphs: A couple’s matrix is calculated from two personal ones: the partners’ matching points are added together, and a sum above 22 is reduced by adding its digits. Yuliana Lisovskaya described this method and the meaning of the couple’s points in most detail in her book Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024). It is one author’s practice, not a general canon of the method, and the couple’s points there do not mean what they mean in a personal chart: the centre is the atmosphere between two people, not anyone’s character.

18 in a couple comes only from a sum of exactly 18 — numbers above 22 give no more than 12 after their digits are added. At the point where the couple has The Moon, each of you has a number of your own, below eighteen.

An example with four Moons at once: the dates 25.01.1986 and 16.03.1992. These people’s centres are 10 and 8, and the couple’s centre is 18. Their karmic tasks are 14 and 4, and the couple’s main task is also 18. And the entry points of the relationship line and tail in their personal charts are 6 and 12, so the couple’s common language is 18 again. This couple’s tail is 18-9-18; The Moon sounds in it twice, and again in the atmosphere and in “The couple’s values”. Lisovskaya holds that a repeated energy speaks louder than the rest: for such a couple the theme of trust and honesty is the main one.

A couple’s centre of 18 comes from six combinations of personal centres: 4 and 14, 5 and 13, 6 and 12, 7 and 11, 8 and 10, 9 and 9. The “why you met” point can be checked in your head — it is the sum of the months of birth: June and December, July and November, August and October, or both in September give 18.

sections.h2: Where The Moon occurs in a couple’s matrix
paragraphs: The Moon occurs in 16 points of a couple’s matrix — including two where only multiples of three come up: in the common language 18 stands for one couple in fourteen, and in “The couple’s values” for one in nine, more often than anywhere else.

paragraphs: Lisovskaya describes the energy by sphere — image, atmosphere, finances, tasks — rather than by each point. Where the author has no text of her own, what follows is our reading based on the meaning of the point and the arcanum.

sections.h2: The Moon in the couple’s centre: a fine mutual feeling
paragraphs: The couple’s centre is what is between you when nobody is watching. With The Moon it is a space of fine feelings.

**In the plus** the partner is first of all a friend. You understand each other without words: from the way the door closed it is clear what kind of day it was. High sensitivity here is not a weakness but a tool — you notice tiredness, hurt, anxiety before anyone mentions them. Personal space is respected: each may have their own evening, their own room, their own thoughts, and that is no cause for suspicion. There are often shared spiritual values. Over time the couple grows together and stands up for each other no matter what, and each year each discovers something new in the other. Lisovskaya has a piece of advice worth remembering: do not speak badly of your partner, even in anger and even to friends.

**In the minus** it is unclear what you are to each other — allies or opponents. Secrets told in confidence become weapons in quarrels: “remember, you said so yourself”. The union may rest on advantage or on escape from other problems. Disappointment over trifles, fear, a ban on seeing those close to you, crossed boundaries — reading messages, checking where the other has been. Nobody gives way, and one partner’s irresponsibility drags both into murky stories.

sections.h2: Common language: 18 in the point of desires
paragraphs: The Moon has this point and its neighbours 17 and 19 do not: only 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 and 21 come up here. 18 comes from personal points of 3 and 15, 6 and 12, or 9 and 9 — for about 7 couples in 100. In the couple reading it stands in two spheres: in “Relationship and common language” as the common language and in “The couple’s karmic tail” as the entry to the task.

The meaning of the point is what the couple strives for, its shared wishes and agreements. With The Moon you reach agreement by intuition: much is clear without words, wishes are guessed, plans seem to form by themselves. The couple dreams of similar things — a quiet home, work in which you can be yourselves, a life away from prying eyes. But the point stands on the line of tasks and can work as resistance. Then “understanding without words” turns into “guessing and taking offence”: each is sure they know what the other wants, and nobody checks. Agreements remain unspoken, and the unspoken is not carried out.

sections.h2: The couple’s tasks: where illusions collapse
paragraphs: The couple’s tasks in the reading are its tail of three points. 18 occurs in all three: in the main task for about 5–6 couples in 100, at the entry for 7, in the middle for 3. These points are read mostly through the minus.

ul: **a false image** created at the start of the acquaintance — you showed yourself better than you are, or saw in the partner what is not there — which later collapses;
**hidden feelings** — tenderness seems a weakness, love goes unspoken, hurts go unnamed;
**a union on one shaky support** — looks, money, connections — without which it is unclear what holds it together;
**adapting to the partner**, which ends in irritation: agreeing for years and then exploding;
**jealousy and grudges from invented stories** — “you were probably thinking of her”, “I know what you meant to say”;
**quarrels out of nothing** and a test of trust;
**dependence on approval** — one does nothing without asking the other.

paragraphs: The main task is to lead the relationship out of the fog into clarity: to talk about feelings out loud, to check guesses with a question rather than a grudge.

sections.h2: Why you met: to learn to trust
paragraphs: This point is read only in the plus: what the couple needs to create together. Lisovskaya has no separate text for 18 here; the meaning is derived from the energy’s plus. The Moon says the couple met in order to learn to trust — themselves, their intuition, each other — and to see beneath the surface. Often these are people with unusual interests or professions who, beside each other, stop being shy about them.

Such couples create things that call for intuition and imagination: creative projects, a business of their own, a home with a special atmosphere where guests feel at ease, though they cannot explain why.

sections.h2: 18 under the heart: what connects the couple
paragraphs: Searches call the “what connects” point “under the heart”: that is how the same point of the relationship line is labelled in a personal matrix. In a couple it shows the positive potential — what two people come together around. The Moon stands here for about 4 couples in 100.

With 18, what connects you is shared secrets in a good sense: your own words, games and rituals that only you know about. Night-time conversations about your innermost things — fears, dreams, childhood — bring you closer, together with the certainty that what is said will stay between you. So does a shared dream you are not yet showing anyone. In the sphere “Relationship and common language” this point stands between the common language and the point of success and status: with The Moon under the heart, the couple rests not on achievements but on trust, and looking after it matters more than any victory.

sections.h2: The Moon in the couple’s money
paragraphs: Money for a couple with The Moon is a zone of fog unless order is brought to it.

ul: **Way into money** (about 4 couples in 100): income stalls because it is unclear where money comes from and where it goes. The dullest and most effective step helps — write down your spending for at least a month.

**Path to prosperity** (about 4 in 100): a business of your own or a family business, shared creative projects with a good income, honest work. Friendship and money are not mixed: they neither lend nor borrow, and that keeps relations with people clean.

**Where it leaks and how status affects the union** (about 3–4 in 100). The Moon’s holes are secret stashes kept from the family, debts, living on the parents’ money, living for the day without looking ahead, naivety and dodging responsibility. Reputation is a separate hole: one murky story can cost more than lost money.
**Attitude to material things** (about 2 in 100): money without counting and without a plan; in the plus — things with a story and meaning rather than whatever is in fashion.

sections.h2: The image, what fills it and what can spoil it
paragraphs: **How others see the couple.** A private couple even in the plus — which is why rumours circulate about them. Unusual professions, an interest in esoterica, psychology, art. You can talk to them about anything. There may be a large age gap. In the minus — a very secretive couple who exaggerate, leave things unsaid and complain about fate or each other.

**What fills the union.** Fantasies, a sense of mystery and of being desired, games for two, an unusual shared interest — from astronomy to old cameras — spiritual practices, the partner’s self-development. The Moon is fed by everything that leaves room for imagination.

**What can spoil it.** Secrets used against the partner, quarrels out of nothing, crossed boundaries. And suspicion: The Moon easily fills in reality, and an evening without a call turns into a story that never happened.

sections.h2: The couple as parents: 18 in the children points
paragraphs: **What you teach** (about 4 couples in 100). With The Moon you teach a child to listen to their intuition, to use their imagination and not to fear the dark — literally and figuratively. Such a home has many fairy tales, games and conversations about feelings. In the minus the parents’ anxieties pass to the child: they are frightened with what the parents themselves fear, or what is happening is not explained, and the child imagines the worst.

**Parents together** (about 3–4 in 100). A couple who sense the child and each other finely in this role: they understand when each needs a rest. The minus is secrets from the child and from each other about the child, agreements each understands in their own way.

sections.h2: The couple’s values: a shared inner world
paragraphs: Most often The Moon stands in “The couple’s values” — for 11 couples in 100, more often than in the centre. It is one of the five main cards of the reading, and it is calculated not by adding the partners’ points but from the couple’s purposes: that is why only 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 and 21 occur here. For Lisovskaya this point is the couple’s spiritual purpose, its values and shared path.

**For a couple with 18 in the values, the shared compass is intuition, one for the two of them.** What they value most is out of sight: understanding at a glance, fantasies, secrets that need no explaining, a flat both turned down in the lift without a word to each other. The difficulty is when intuition gives way to anxiety: each fills in the gaps for the other, and instead of a question there is a scene played out in the head, and the secret that connected them becomes a wall.

sections.h2: What helps a couple with The Moon

ul: Accept that your partner sometimes needs to withdraw into themselves. It is a way of recovering, not a lack of love.
Don’t shift your fears and guilt onto your partner.
Don’t fill in the other’s thoughts for them: check any guess with a question.
Talk about feelings out loud, even if it seems obvious.
Learn to see the long view and to trust: plan for more than tomorrow.
Work on mood swings — your own, not only your partner’s.
Find shared goals and dreams, and compare notes on them from time to time.
Don’t speak badly of your partner — neither out loud nor behind their back.

paragraphs: The method gives no compatibility percentages, and The Moon in a couple’s matrix predicts neither infidelity nor a break-up. It shows where the couple risks fog and how to clear it.

faq.q: Does The Moon in compatibility mean deception and infidelity?
faq.a: No. Lisovskaya’s list of The Moon’s minuses includes both deception and a test of trust, but these are possible scenarios of the energy, not a fact about a couple. In the plus the same Moon gives a rare understanding without words, friendship within love and care for each other’s boundaries.

faq.q: My partner withdraws into themselves. Does it mean they don’t love me?
faq.a: For a couple with The Moon, most often not. Lisovskaya advises plainly to accept the partner’s need to withdraw into themselves sometimes: it is a way of recovering. What is worrying is something else — if the withdrawal turns into secrets and silence replaces talking about what matters.

faq.q: What does 18 in the couple’s common language mean?
faq.a: It is the point of shared wishes and agreements; in the reading it is also the entry to the couple’s task. With 18 you reach agreement by intuition and dream of similar things. The risk is unspoken agreements: each is sure they know the other’s wishes, and nobody checks them.

faq.q: What does 18 under the heart mean in compatibility?
faq.a: In a couple’s matrix it is the “what connects” point. With The Moon you are brought closer by shared secrets in a good sense — your own words, games and dreams that only you know about — and by evenings when you can talk about your innermost things and know it will stay between you.

faq.q: We have 18 both in the centre and in the tasks. Is that bad?
faq.a: It means that The Moon’s theme sounds loudly in the couple: both the atmosphere and the main trials are tied to trust and honesty. It is not the number that makes this bad but the fog. Couples who learn to talk about feelings directly turn a repeated Moon into a rare depth of relationship.

seo.title: Destiny matrix compatibility 19: The Sun in a couple
seo.description: Destiny matrix compatibility 19: warmth, success and family first. Where The Sun occurs, what it means for a couple, and how to make sure both partners shine.

items.title: Arcanum 19 in a compatibility matrix: The Sun — is there enough light for two?
items.short: 19 in destiny matrix compatibility is The Sun, the energy of warmth, success and the joy of living. A couple with it is warm and hospitable, family comes first, and each grows in their own work. The Sun’s main question in a couple is whether there is enough light for two: in the strong version both shine; in the weak version, one becomes the sun and the other its reflection. Below is how 19 appears in a couple’s matrix, where it occurs, what it means at each point and what helps such a couple.

sections.h2: How 19 appears in a couple’s matrix
paragraphs: Compatibility by the matrix is calculated like this: a personal matrix is built for each partner by date of birth, then the matching points are added together and reduced to a number from 1 to 22. If the sum is above 22, its digits are added. The result is the couple’s matrix, and its points have their own meanings: the centre is the atmosphere between two people, the day is how others see the couple, the month is why it met. Yuliana Lisovskaya analysed the meaning of the couple’s points in detail in her book Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024); below is her reading of The Sun in our own words.

The arithmetic here is stricter than it seems. Sums from 23 to 44 give 12 or less after their digits are added, so 19 in a couple is always a sum of exactly 19. At the point where the couple has The Sun, each partner has a number below nineteen: this couple’s light is born of the meeting, not passed from one to the other.

The centre is The Sun’s most frequent point in a couple, about 7 couples in 100. And it is a place where 19 never occurs in a personal chart: a person’s centre is only 3–14, 16, 18, 20 or 22. Six combinations give a couple’s centre of 19: 9 and 10, 8 and 11, 7 and 12, 6 and 13, 5 and 14, 3 and 16. An example: the dates 11.06.1990 and 17.01.1985. These people’s centres are 9 and 10, and their couple’s centre is 19.

Two points can be seen straight from the dates. Why you met is the sum of the months of birth: July and December, August and November, September and October give 19. The image of the couple is the sum of the days of birth, where numbers above 22 are reduced first: the 25th counts as 7, the 28th as 10.

sections.h2: Where a couple can have The Sun
paragraphs: 19 occurs in 14 points of a couple’s matrix, and none of them dominates: apart from the centre, it is everywhere between 2 and 5 couples in 100. The Sun is absent from the common language point, where the couple’s tail begins — only multiples of three come up there.

paragraphs: Lisovskaya describes the energy by sphere — atmosphere, image, finances, tasks — rather than for each point. For the points she has no separate words on, what follows is our reading based on the meaning of the point and the arcanum.

sections.h2: The Sun in the couple’s centre: warmth that is shared
paragraphs: The centre is what is between you without witnesses.

**In the plus** it is respect and care. Each is successful in their own work, and one’s success does not threaten the other: the partner’s promotion is celebrated together rather than prompting a count of who is in charge now. Family comes first, the home is cosy, and one feels protected by the other. Love is often expressed generously — presents, trips, surprises — but it does not rest on them: there are couples from well-off families whose love has nothing to do with money. The Sun tends to renew and simplify life: throw out the unnecessary, rearrange the furniture, invent a new family ritual.

**In the minus** warmth becomes heat. Total control — where were you, how much did you spend, why didn’t you call. Tension, restricting the partner in their work and in seeing those close to them: “why do you need this job, I’m earning”. Arrogance and comparisons — with exes, with friends, with those who have achieved more. In the worst case one becomes a tyrant and the other lives in their shadow.

sections.h2: The couple’s tasks: the sun and its reflection
paragraphs: The sphere “The couple’s karmic tail” is three points: entry to the task, the middle and the main task. 19 occurs in the main task (about 5 couples in 100) and in the middle (about 2 in 100), but not at the entry. Lisovskaya reads these points mostly through the minus.

ul: **work at the family’s expense** — or the reverse imbalance: one’s whole life centred on the partner, with no work of one’s own;
**one partner’s lack of fulfilment**, which over time turns into resentment of the other;
**an inability to talk about problems**: everything is wonderful outside, while inside things pile up;
**inflated expectations** — of the partner, of the children, of oneself;
**selfishness and holding back feelings**;
**overprotection and inaction** — one does everything for the other, and the other gets used to doing nothing;
**harsh criticism and claiming the partner’s victories**: “I made you who you are”.

paragraphs: The main task is for both to shine. In the weak version one becomes the sun and the other its reflection, or the two compete for one stage. In the strong version one’s success makes the other glad, and glory is not divided but multiplied.

sections.h2: The money of a couple with The Sun
paragraphs: The Sun in money is about status and generosity. What matters is who is in charge of whom.

ul: **Way into money** (about 4 couples in 100): income stalls because of extremes. Either money goes on status — a car, a holiday, a restaurant, “like everyone else” — or, on the contrary, they economise so harshly that life loses its flavour. A shared plan helps avoid this: how much for joy, how much for the reserve.

**Path to prosperity** (about 4 in 100): a love of planning and accounting, shared budgets and shared ventures, strong fulfilment for each. Large investments in children — education, sport, travel. Stability, a reserve for a rainy day, honest success.

**Where it leaks and how status affects the union** (about 3 in 100). The holes are an obsession with money and status, greed or being spoilt. When income becomes the measure of a person, the one who earns less starts to feel like a guest in their own home.
**Attitude to material things** (about 2 in 100): accounting, order, a reserve; in the minus — stinginess or extravagance.

sections.h2: Why you met: to grow together
paragraphs: In Lisovskaya’s reading the “why you met” point answers what the couple needs to create together, and it is read only in the plus. Lisovskaya has no separate text for 19 here; the meaning is derived from the energy’s plus. The Sun says the couple met in order to grow together and shine for others. Beside each other both become more confident: one finally starts their own business, the other gets a position they had not dared to dream of.

Such couples create things that warm the people around them: a big hospitable home, family celebrations that bring all the relatives together, a business where friends work. The meeting is needed so that both can see that success as two is brighter than success alone.

sections.h2: The image, what fills it and what can spoil it
paragraphs: **How others see the couple.** A bright, warm, active, successful couple. Hospitable, often with several children, travelling or moving a lot. Both have status — sometimes gained together. Their prosperity is talked about, not always kindly. In the minus the image becomes heavy: jealousy of everyone, complaints about life, imbalance, indifference to other people’s troubles.

**What fills the union.** Vivid impressions, dreams come true, new acquaintances, honesty, passion and a love of life. The partner’s growth fills it especially, spurring the other to grow too: one passes an exam — the other finally signs up for a course.
**What can spoil it.** Control, arrogance and comparisons. The quarrels of a couple with The Sun often start with the words “but look at them” and end with someone feeling worse than the other.

sections.h2: The couple as parents: 19 in the children points
paragraphs: For The Sun both children points occur about equally often — around 4 couples in 100 each. It is one of the most “family” energies: Lisovskaya notes that couples with The Sun often have many children and invest a lot in them.

**Parents together.** A tandem where both are involved: two people sit in the front row at the school play, and two come to the parents’ evening too. Generous parents who spare neither time nor money on their children. The minus is competition: which parent is the favourite, who has given more.

**What you teach.** To enjoy life, to believe in oneself, not to be afraid of being noticed. The child grows up feeling loved and that their successes bring joy. The minus is overprotection and inflated expectations: deciding for the child, demanding nothing but victories from them, living through their successes instead of your own.

sections.h2: 19 under the heart: what connects the couple
paragraphs: “Under the heart” is what searches call the “what connects” point: in a personal chart this point of the relationship line carries exactly that label. With The Sun here (about 3 couples in 100), what connects you is shared victories and celebrations: a wedding that went on for three days, the first home of your own, the anniversary of a company you started as two at the kitchen table. Trips and everything that brings shared joy bring you closer. In the sphere “Relationship and common language” this point stands next to the point of success and status, and The Sun under the heart suggests that the union grows stronger when victories are called shared.

sections.h2: What helps a couple with The Sun

ul: Define shared goals and move in one direction.
Give attention both to your own interests and to shared ones: each has their own work, and the couple has its own time.
Respect your partner’s personal space and circle.
Say thank you out loud — for dinner, for support, for getting through something hard.
Rest together, without work and phones.
Share the housework equally, not by status: whoever earns more is not excused from the washing-up.
Support each other at hard moments and be tolerant of weaknesses — The Sun needs a cloudy day too.

paragraphs: This is the author’s view and our reading, not a forecast for a particular couple. The method gives no compatibility percentages.

faq.q: Is The Sun in a couple ideal compatibility?
faq.a: The method has no ideal couples and no compatibility percentages. 19 gives a union warmth, respect and shared success, but in the minus the same Sun gives control and competition. Which side shows depends on whether both partners shine.

faq.q: One of us is more successful. Is that the minus of 19?
faq.a: Not in itself. The minus begins when one partner’s success becomes the measure of the other: comparisons, “you’re nothing without me”, claiming victories. A couple with The Sun in the plus celebrates each one’s success as shared and helps the one who lags behind to grow rather than keeping them in the shadow.

faq.q: What does 19 under the heart mean in compatibility?
faq.a: In a couple’s matrix it is the “what connects” point. With 19 you are brought closer by shared victories and celebrations: a wedding, a home of your own, a shared business, trips. The union grows stronger when successes are called shared rather than divided by merit.

faq.q: Does 19 in the children points mean we will have many children?
faq.a: No, the matrix does not predict how many children there will be or whether there will be any. The “couple as parents” points describe what you are like together as the elders — for your own children, if you have or will have them, and for everyone you look after. The Sun here is generosity and warmth, and its risk is overprotection and inflated expectations.

faq.q: How can we tell that our Sun is in the minus?
faq.a: Look at three things: who makes the decisions, how other people’s successes are talked about, and who does the housework. If the same person always decides, successes are compared and the housework is shared out by status, The Sun is working in the minus. It is a reason to agree afresh, not a verdict.

seo.title: Destiny matrix compatibility 2: The High Priestess in a couple
seo.description: Destiny matrix compatibility 2 appears only if both partners were born on the 1st or in January. What The High Priestess means for such a couple.

items.title: The 2 in a compatibility matrix: The High Priestess in a couple and why she is so rare
items.short: A 2 in a couple’s matrix is a rare guest. It lands in only two points, and only when both partners have a 1 there: both were born on the 1st or both in January. Fewer than one couple in a hundred has it. If you do, the union is built on quiet understanding and on what you keep to yourselves, and the couple’s main lesson is to learn to talk about feelings out loud instead of storing them up.

sections.h2: Where a 2 in a couple’s matrix comes from
paragraphs: A couple’s matrix is calculated from two personal matrices: the partners’ matching points are added together and the sum is reduced to a number from 1 to 22. If the sum is above 22, its digits are added: 24 becomes 6, 39 becomes 12. This is how Yuliana Lisovskaya calculates it step by step in her book Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024), and this is how our compatibility calculator works.

Only one sum gives a 2 — 1 + 1. Everything above 22 is reduced to numbers from 3 to 12, and there is no 2 among them. So a 2 appears in a couple only where both partners have a 1. And a 1 occurs in a personal matrix in just two places: the day point, if a person was born on the 1st, and the month point, if they were born in January. Hence the two points of a couple where a 2 is possible:
