paragraphs: A 2 takes both points at once only for couples where both were born on 1 January. In the other points of a couple’s matrix — the atmosphere, money, tasks, under the heart — there is never a 2. There is no 1 in a couple at all: the sum of two numbers cannot give 1.

**An example.** The partners were born on 1 March 1990 and 1 October 1992. Their days of birth give a 1 each, 1 + 1 = 2, and the 2 lands in the image of the couple. Their months give 3 and 10, 13 in total, so in the sphere “Why you met” this couple reads 2 and 13 together. Another couple: 14 January 1991 and 25 January 1994. Two January months, 1 + 1 = 2 — the 2 lands in the card “What to create together”, and the image of the couple here is 21.

sections.h2: The 2 in the “Why you met” point
paragraphs: Lisovskaya reads this point only in the plus: it answers what the couple is to create together and what to learn. For the 2 the author sets this answer out in detail — it is one of three energies that have one in the book. In short, you were brought together to learn how to handle feelings: not to hide them, not to spill them out and not to use them as a lever.
In life this is made of concrete things:

ul: **Speak instead of storing up.** “You’re late again — fine, whatever” is a phrase after which the hurt lives on for a week. “I felt lonely this evening — let’s agree to call each other” is a phrase after which it is gone.

**Don’t threaten to leave.** “Then live on your own”, thrown out in a quarrel, is exactly the lever the 2 teaches you to give up. Words used to apply pressure are more dangerous for this couple than any row.
**Accept what is weak and dark in the other.** Not only what they shine at in company, but their fears, outbursts and oddities too — and do not pretend they are not there.

**Don’t discuss your partner behind their back.** If a friend, your mother or a colleague hears about your quarrels before the two of you have talked, for the 2 that is a sign the conversation has gone the wrong way.
**Lower your demands and let go of jealousy.** Expecting the other to guess for themselves and being angry that they didn’t is The High Priestess’s favourite trap.
**Decide the question of family and children consciously** — together, out loud, without “it’ll sort itself out”.
**Deal with family scripts.** Beliefs like “feelings are not talked about” or “to endure is to love”, picked up from mothers and grandmothers, are part of this couple’s work too.

paragraphs: The good news is that a couple with a 2 in this point has everything it needs to succeed: both sense each other finely. What is usually missing is only the courage to speak first.

sections.h2: The 2 in the “How others see the couple” point
paragraphs: This point shows the image the couple projects to the world, and it is read both ways.

**In the plus** you are one couple in public and another at home. Acquaintances learn about your life after the fact: about the wedding from the rings, about the move from the new address. Guesses circulate around you, and you neither deny nor confirm them. Yet with each other you are honest, with nothing left unsaid, and you talk heart to heart late into the night. Often you are opposites who complement each other precisely: one flares up, the other calms things down; one talks, the other listens. Such a couple quickly gets a shared budget, shared plans and a wish for a family.

**In the minus** reserve in public turns into coldness at home. One muffles the other’s feelings — “don’t start”, “you’re imagining things” — and heart-to-heart talks give way to polite silence. Everyone sees the seesaw of “we love each other — we’re splitting up”, but nobody knows why it swings. Intolerance appears: of habits, of friends, of the partner’s tears. In the 2’s minus Lisovskaya lists much heavier stories as well, but that is a list of the energy’s possible expressions, not a description of your couple.

sections.h2: The quiet background the 2 brings into a couple
paragraphs: Lisovskaya also describes the general background of a couple with a 2, even though a 2 can never stand in the centre of a couple’s matrix. This background belongs to the two points where it does occur, and it is recognisable at once. Reserve and modesty. Understanding without words: a glance across the table is enough to leave a party. Sympathy with nothing put on for show. If something is wrong, it will be said gently and in private, not in front of everyone.

One more trait the author considers normal for the 2 is long hesitation over choices. They view a flat ten times, spend a month choosing a holiday, and answer “so, shall we get married?” with “let’s think a bit more”. This is not indecision but the 2’s way of testing a decision by feeling. Things go wrong only when doubt becomes an excuse to decide nothing.

sections.h2: The 2 together with the second card of the meeting
paragraphs: Our reading treats the sphere “Why you met” as a pair of cards: the image of the couple and “What to create together”. If the 2 stands in one of them, the other is almost certainly a different energy, and the meaning of the meeting is made of both. The pluses of the two cards weave into what you are together for, the minuses into what may go wrong. This is not a karmic task but something quite down to earth: what you are building and what you trip over.

In such a pairing the 2 is responsible for quiet and depth. If the second card is loud and busy, the 2 says: amid all the doing, don’t forget each other. If the second card is quiet too, it warns: silence for two is good while it is full, and dangerous when something unsaid hides behind it.

sections.h2: What a couple with a 2 is advised to do

ul: **Each find a support of your own.** Not in the partner but in yourself — an occupation, a place, a circle — so that after a breakdown you come back to the conversation quickly rather than licking your wounds for weeks.
**Create comfort both at home and in the relationship.** Rituals for two — evening tea without phones, a walk on Sundays — are no trifle for the 2 but a way of saying “I’m with you” without words.
**Keep in touch with your families.** A couple with a 2 easily shuts itself off from the world; living ties with relatives keep it from closing in completely.
**Change life gradually.** Sharp turns — “that’s it, we’re moving”, “that’s it, we’re splitting up” — do not suit the 2. It is better to try a little at a time and talk it over along the way.
**Share what is deep.** A feeling you consider a weakness often turns out to be the most valuable thing you have entrusted to your partner.

sections.h2: A 2 in a partner’s personal matrix is something else
paragraphs: If a 2 stands in the personal matrix of one of you, it is a trait of that person: their intuition, their reserve, their habit of keeping quiet about what matters. It does not pass into the couple’s matrix by itself — it adds up with the partner’s number in the same point and gives a different number. A 2 for one and a 9 for the other in the day point give an image of the couple of 11, not 2.
And one more mix-up from searches: “the destiny matrix of two people” is not about arcanum 2 but about the couple’s calculation itself from two dates of birth.

faq.q: Why is there no 2 at all in our couple’s matrix?
faq.a: That is the case for the vast majority of couples. A 2 appears only if both partners were born on the 1st or both in January — fewer than one couple in a hundred. The absence of a 2 says nothing about the quality of the union: the theme of feelings and openness in your matrix is carried by other energies.

faq.q: Can a 2 stand in the centre of a couple’s matrix?
faq.a: No. The couple’s centre is the sum of two personal centres, and a person’s centre is never less than three. The sum of two centres starts at six and never reduces to a 2. The same goes for all the other points except the image of the couple and “What to create together”.

faq.q: Why is there never a 1 in a couple’s matrix?
faq.a: Because the sum of two numbers from 1 to 22 gives neither 1 nor a number that reduces to 1. The Magician never comes up in a couple’s matrix — Lisovskaya notes this herself, and a check of every date confirms it.

faq.q: Is a 2 in a couple a good sign or a bad one?
faq.a: Neither. A couple’s matrix gives no grades and no compatibility percentages. The 2 shows where your strength lies — in deep understanding without words — and where the risk is: in the unsaid that piles up. Which of the two outweighs depends on whether you talk to each other.

faq.q: We were both born on 1 January. What does that mean for the couple?
faq.a: Your 2 stands in two points at once — in the image of the couple and in “What to create together”. The theme of The High Priestess sounds louder: from outside you are a private couple people guess about a lot, and your shared task is to learn to talk about feelings. Read the two points separately, but remember that they speak of the same thing.

seo.title: Destiny matrix compatibility 20: Judgement in a couple
seo.description: Destiny matrix compatibility 20: family and kin — relatives, traditions, children and a shared budget. Where Judgement occurs and how to keep boundaries.

items.title: Arcanum 20 in a compatibility matrix: Judgement — the couple, kin and family
items.short: 20 in destiny matrix compatibility is the Judgement arcanum, and in a couple its key is family and kin. It covers relations with relatives, traditions, inheritance, the parents’ influence on the union, and the question of when and how children will come into the couple’s life. In the plus such a union becomes part of the family line and rests on forgiveness and trust; in the minus it drowns in relatives’ meddling and unspoken grievances. Below is how 20 appears in a couple’s matrix, where it occurs and what it means in the centre, money, tasks and the children points.

sections.h2: How 20 appears in a couple’s matrix
paragraphs: For compatibility a third matrix is calculated — the couple’s matrix. Each partner’s personal matrix is taken, the matching points are added together, and the sum is reduced to 22: if it is larger, its digits are added. Yuliana Lisovskaya described this method and the meaning of the couple’s points in most detail in her book Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024). The couple’s points are read in their own way: the centre, for example, is the atmosphere between the partners, not the character of one of them.
20 in a couple is always a sum of exactly 20: sums above 22 give no more than 12 after their digits are added. So at the point where the couple has Judgement, each of you has a number below twenty.

An example shows that the couple’s energy does not repeat the partners’ energies: the dates 30.05.1995 and 09.04.1990. Both people have 10 in the centre — The Wheel of Fortune, the energy of change and chance. Together 10 and 10 give 20, and Judgement stands in the couple’s centre. Two people who each live by turns of fate together build a family with roots. Curiously, these people also have 20 in their personal matrices — both in the middle of the karmic tail. But in the couple that point holds 4: 20 + 20 = 40, and 4 + 0 = 4. The partners’ own twentieth and the couple’s twentieth are different things. In all, a couple’s centre of 20 comes from six combinations of personal centres: 4 and 16, 6 and 14, 7 and 13, 8 and 12, 9 and 11, 10 and 10.
By the months of birth, 20 can be seen in the “why you met” point: August and December, September and November, or both in October.

sections.h2: Where 20 occurs in a couple’s matrix
paragraphs: The twentieth occurs in 14 points, and it is spread evenly: in the centre for 6 couples in 100, in the other points for roughly 3 to 4. It is absent from the common language point, where the couple’s tail begins: only multiples of three occur there.

paragraphs: Lisovskaya describes the energy by spheres of the couple’s life rather than for each point. For points she has no separate words on, what follows is our reading based on the meaning of the point and the arcanum.

sections.h2: Judgement in the couple’s centre: an atmosphere of forgiveness
paragraphs: The centre is what happens between you when there are no witnesses.

**In the plus** it is comfort and complete trust. Each takes the other into account in everything: before accepting a weekend invitation they call the partner, before changing jobs they talk it over. The couple has equality and willingness to give way, and both understand the value of marriage. Mistakes are forgiven here — and not kept up the sleeve for the next quarrel. The moral support is so strong that the partner is backed even when they are wrong: in public each takes the other’s side, and they sort it out later, in private. The relatives accept the partner as one of their own.

**In the minus** the couple closes off from each other. They blame the partner without owning their own part: “you’re the one who said the wrong thing to Mum”. There is a sudden cooling, when yesterday it was warm and today it is cold, and nobody explains why. Neither can say what they feel or what they dislike — for years they put up with what could have been discussed in an evening. Indecision, control and refusal of help appear. A separate crack is children: one wants a child, the other is not ready, and the conversation is put off until it becomes a quarrel.

sections.h2: The couple’s tasks: owning your part and reaching agreement with the relatives
paragraphs: In the reading the couple’s karmic tail is three points: entry to the task, the middle and the main task. 20 occurs in the main task (about 4 couples in 100) and in the middle (about 3 in 100). These points are read mostly through the minus: they are trials through which the couple grows.

ul: **admitting mistakes** — one’s own, not only the partner’s; for this couple “I was wrong” is a turning-point phrase;
**a union “for the sake of something”** — for the sake of a flat, of status, of calming the parents down;
**a union by the relatives’ approval** or with their mediation: the parents introduced them, the parents hurried them, the parents chose;
**a love that is obstructed** by age, status, faith or the traditions of two families;
**the relatives’ rejection of the partner** — a mother-in-law who for years calls her daughter-in-law by her surname, a father-in-law who does not say hello;
**a false image** that collapses when you get to know the person within their own family;
**a partner who decides nothing without their parents** — from the colour of the wallpaper to where to go on holiday;
**boundaries with relatives** that are either missing altogether or impenetrable.

paragraphs: The main task is to own your part of a mistake and to agree on boundaries with both families: what the two of you decide, and where the parents’ opinion is advice rather than an order.

sections.h2: The money of a couple with Judgement
paragraphs: For a couple with the twentieth, money is tied to family — and that is both a support and a risk.

ul: **Way into money** (about 4 couples in 100), the twentieth’s second most frequent point. Income stalls when the couple does not want to keep a shared budget: each has their own money, their own decisions, their own debts. Instability and extremes belong here too — harsh economy followed by wasteful spending. A shared budget with a discussion of risks helps: before a big expense, a conversation rather than presenting the partner with a done deal.

**Path to prosperity** (about 4 in 100): prosperity grows after the wedding or the birth of a child. Opportunities come through family — a shared business with relatives, help from parents, an inheritance. Planning together, care for things, shared comfort and order.

**Where it leaks and how status affects the union** (about 3 in 100). The holes are a lost inheritance and lawsuits with relatives, savings squandered, giving up the material for the sake of extreme convictions.
**Attitude to material things** (about 3 in 100): an orderly home, things that last a long time, much passed down from generation to generation.

sections.h2: The couple’s image, what fills it and what can spoil it
paragraphs: **How others see the couple.** A couple who put their family first and open up only to their own. A traditional couple, sometimes with many children. There may be a large difference in age, status, looks or faith — and it does not get in the way of happiness. In the minus — a closed couple whose words and deeds diverge, whose marriage looks from outside like a union of convenience, and whose relatives are surprised at their decisions — for example, that they do not want children. There is another extreme too: they go nowhere without each other, not even to see friends on their own.

**What fills the union.** A shared venture, growing together, spiritual practices. And above all — any events lived through together bind them: a wedding, a housewarming, a hard year, the birth of a child, parents moving closer — everything becomes part of a shared story.

**What can spoil it.** Silence about what one dislikes, blame, relatives’ meddling. The habit of silently grading the partner and keeping a tally that will one day be presented in full — for all the years at once — is dangerous. The reason for a serious quarrel often comes from the family — an inheritance, a country cottage, who looks after the grandchildren — and a conversation about it quickly becomes a conversation about whose family matters more.

sections.h2: The couple as parents: 20 in the children points
paragraphs: For Judgement both children points are home ground: the family line and its continuation.

**Parents together** (about 4 couples in 100). Family as a line: the elders are united, the grandparents are close by, celebrations bring several generations together. The parents support each other in decisions about the child and do not argue in front of them. The minus is when decisions about the children are made not by the parents but by their parents.

**What you teach** (about 4 in 100). To respect one’s roots, to know the family’s history, to forgive and to admit one’s mistakes. The child grows up feeling part of something bigger. In the minus traditions become an obligation: “everyone in our family is an engineer” or “that’s not how we do things”, and it is hard for the child to choose their own path.

sections.h2: Why you met: to become a family
paragraphs: The point answers what the couple needs to create together, and it has no minus. Lisovskaya has no separate text for 20 here; the meaning is derived from the energy’s plus. Judgement says the couple met in order to become a family in the full sense — to join two family lines, pass traditions on, close old family grievances with forgiveness. Such a meeting often reconciles relatives too: two families who did not know each other before become one.

Such couples create a home where people gather for the holidays, family traditions that will outlive them, sometimes a shared family business. A difference in age, faith or background does not get in the way here but becomes part of the shared story: the children grow up knowing both family trees.

sections.h2: 20 under the heart: what connects the couple
paragraphs: The query “20 under the heart in compatibility” is about the “what connects” point: in a personal matrix it is labelled “Under the heart”. With 20 here (about 3 couples in 100), what connects you is family events and traditions: Sunday lunch at the parents’, a Christmas tree decorated the old way, a wedding album you look through on your anniversary. Forgiveness brings you closer too — the evening when one admitted a mistake and the other chose not to bring it up again. In the sphere “Relationship and common language” this point stands next to the point of success and status: with Judgement under the heart, family matters more than career, and the couple should make sure this is a shared choice rather than one partner’s sacrifice.

sections.h2: What helps a couple with 20

ul: Value family traditions and pass them on — but choose which of them are yours.
Agree on boundaries with relatives as two, and hold them as two.
Admit your mistakes without waiting for them to be proved.
Say what you dislike while it is a small thing, not after a year of silence.
Look for a compromise on the question of children: when, how many, how — discuss it in advance.
Respect your partner’s opinion even when it differs from their parents’.
Support your partner’s aspirations and share love and care generously.

paragraphs: The method gives no compatibility percentages: 20 in a couple describes the theme of the union — family and kin — not how strong it is.

faq.q: Our relatives are against our union — is that because of 20?
faq.a: The matrix does not explain relatives’ behaviour. But if 20 stands in the couple’s tasks or in the point “what can spoil it”, the theme of relatives is one of the main ones for you, and Lisovskaya names the family’s rejection of the partner among the trials of this energy. What works is an agreement between the two of you: what you decide yourselves and how you respond to interference together.

faq.q: We both have a centre of 10, and the couple has 20. What does that mean?
faq.a: 10 and 10 give 20 — that is how the couple’s centre adds up for people who each have The Wheel of Fortune in the centre. Two people who live by turns of fate together get the atmosphere of Judgement: family, roots, traditions. But if both have 20 in the same point, the couple will have 4 there: 20 + 20 = 40, and 4 + 0 = 4.

faq.q: What does 20 under the heart mean in compatibility?
faq.a: In a couple’s matrix it is the “what connects” point. With 20 you are brought closer by family events and traditions — holidays with relatives, anniversaries, a shared history — and by forgiveness: the ability to admit a mistake and not bring up the other’s.

faq.q: One of us wants children and the other isn’t ready. Is that about 20?
faq.a: It is one of the difficulties Lisovskaya names in the twentieth’s minus. The matrix does not decide for a couple whether there will be children, but it suggests that the conversation about them must not be put off: the longer it waits, the more painful the argument. Her advice is to look for a compromise rather than wait for someone to change their mind on their own.

faq.q: Does 20 in the couple’s money mean an inheritance?
faq.a: Inheritance is one of the twentieth’s money themes, in the plus and in the minus, but the matrix does not promise one. More broadly, 20 says the couple’s money is tied to family: prosperity grows after a wedding or the birth of a child, relatives help, and the risks are disputes over inheritance and a reluctance to keep a shared budget.

seo.title: Destiny matrix compatibility 21: The World in a couple
seo.description: Destiny matrix compatibility 21: where a couple has The World and what it means in the couple’s values, common language, centre, tasks and money.

items.title: Arcanum 21 in destiny matrix compatibility: The World — a couple with a wide horizon
items.short: 21 in destiny matrix compatibility is The World arcanum, the energy of wholeness, space and a shared picture of life. A couple with it is held together by shared views, talks a lot, moves and travels easily, and accepts the partner as they are. The World’s minus has two poles: stagnation, where life shrinks to four walls, and running in circles of “together — apart”. Below is how 21 appears in a couple’s matrix, why it most often stands in the couple’s values and the common language, and what it means at each point where it occurs.

sections.h2: How 21 ends up in a couple’s matrix
paragraphs: A compatibility matrix is built from two personal matrices: the partners’ matching points are added together and the sum is reduced to 22, adding its digits if it is larger. The result is a third chart — the couple’s matrix — and its points do not mean what they mean in a personal chart. Below, 21 is analysed following Yuliana Lisovskaya’s book Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024) — the most detailed description of this method.

21 in a couple comes only from a sum of exactly 21: sums from 23 to 44 give no more than 12 after their digits are added. At the point where the couple has The World, each partner has a smaller number — for example, 10 and 11 or 18 and 3.

After “The couple’s values” (covered below), the twenty-first’s most frequent point is the common language, where the couple’s tail begins. In a personal matrix this is the entry point of the relationship line and the tail, and only seven numbers occur in it: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 and 21. The sum of two such numbers is also a multiple of three, so the same set comes up here in a couple, and 21 stands in this point for about 11 couples in 100 — one in nine. It comes from the combinations 3 and 18, 6 and 15, 9 and 12. An example: the dates 17.09.1990 and 27.05.1994. These people’s relationship entry points are 18 and 3, the couple’s common language is 21, and the couple’s tail is 21-4-10.

A couple’s centre of 21 is rarer, about 5 couples in 100, and it is something a personal chart never has: a person’s centre is only 3–14, 16, 18, 20 or 22. In a couple, 21 in the centre comes from 3 and 18, 5 and 16, 7 and 14, 8 and 13, 9 and 12, 10 and 11. An example: the dates 08.04.1996 and 16.07.1989, centres 11 and 10, the couple’s centre 21.

sections.h2: Where The World occurs in a couple’s matrix
paragraphs: 21 occurs in 16 points of a couple’s matrix — more than its neighbours 20 and 22, which have neither the common language nor the couple’s values, where only multiples of three come up.

paragraphs: Lisovskaya’s card for this energy is written by sphere — image, atmosphere, finances, tasks — rather than for each point. Where the author has no separate text, what follows is our reading based on the meaning of the point and the arcanum.

sections.h2: Common language: 21 in the point of desires
paragraphs: In the couple reading this point stands in two spheres at once: in “Relationship and common language” as the common language, and in “The couple’s karmic tail” as the entry to the task. Its meaning is what the couple strives for, its shared wishes and agreements.

**In the plus** a couple with 21 has a shared picture of life. You agree on the essentials — how to live, where to live, what matters — and so you reach agreement on details easily. The wishes are big and shared: to live in another country, travel half the world, build a house by the sea, swap a profession for one you both dreamed of. The agreements are equal: nobody gives orders, decisions are made as two, and each leaves the other room.

**As resistance** the point shows where the couple stalls at the entry to its tasks. There are no agreements; each pulls in their own direction. They do not hear each other: one talks about moving, the other about renovating, and both are sure they are not understood. One imposes their views — on upbringing, on faith, on the right way to live. Until the couple has found a common language, all its other tasks are solved by force.

sections.h2: The atmosphere inside the couple: 21 in the centre
paragraphs: The centre is what happens between two people without witnesses.

**In the plus** it is an atmosphere of acceptance. The partner is not remade: they are accepted even in the minus, with their oddities and habits. You talk a lot — about everything, from the news to the meaning of life — and quarrels end in compromise rather than one person’s victory. There is no pressure, duties are split in half: whoever cooks does not wash up. The outlook is shared, and care is a natural part of the day.

**In the minus** — re-education. One tries to fit the partner to their own views, imposes a faith, a circle, a way of life. Life turns into a Groundhog Day routine: the same conversations, the same evenings. The couple has many secrets and illusions about the relationship: each lives in their own version of the union.

sections.h2: The money of a couple with The World

ul: **Way into money** (about 4 couples in 100), the twenty-first’s fourth most frequent point. Income stalls because of fear of the new: “old is better than new”, refusing change even when it pays, clinging to a job that has long been unsatisfying. A simple rule helps avoid this: once a year, review together what in your money has gone out of date.

**Path to prosperity** (about 4 in 100): patience in spending, things that last a long time, budget rules invented together. Savings, long-term investments, passive income. They take earning responsibly but lightly — without a cult of money.

**Where it leaks and how status affects the union** (about 3 in 100). The holes are greed, suspicion, demanding an account of every purchase, fixation on the material. When one loses their job, the other starts counting every penny out loud.
**Attitude to material things** (about 3 in 100): thrift and care for things and for nature — mend rather than throw away, give away rather than bin.

sections.h2: The couple’s image, what fills it and what can spoil it
paragraphs: **How others see the couple.** Freedom-loving and always ready to go: they travel a lot, have a modern view of relationships and are peaceable. They came together over a shared philosophy of life, and to many they are the ideal couple. There may be a marriage across nationalities, a move abroad, work on rotation or long business trips — and after separations they only miss each other more. In the minus the image shrinks: closed, quarrelsome, unwelcoming, with barbs in public.

**What fills the union.** Trips and moves, going back to places with good memories — that café, that beach — sport together, frank conversations, bold decisions, a balance between one’s own and the shared.
**What can spoil it.** Routine, re-educating the partner, secrets. And repeating the same hard conversations: The World easily closes into a circle where every quarrel follows the same script.

sections.h2: The couple as parents: 21 in the children points
paragraphs: **Parents together** (about 4 couples in 100), one of The World’s frequent points. Parents who open up the world to a child: they take them on trips, show them other cities and languages, teach that people live in different ways. They support each other in this role as equals — without “that’s your job”. The minus is when the parents each live their own life and the child shuttles between them.

**What you teach** (about 4 in 100). To look beyond one’s own backyard, to respect other people’s views, to see things through. In the minus — strictness and conservatism: “that’s not how we do things”, a ban on friends the parents dislike.

sections.h2: The couple’s tasks: stagnation or escape
paragraphs: The couple’s karmic tail is read from the entry through the middle to the main task. 21 occurs in all three: at the entry for 11 couples in 100 (more on this above, under the common language), in the middle and in the main task for about 4. These points are read mostly through the minus.
The World’s trials fall into two poles.

ul: strictness and conservatism — “we’ve always lived like this”;
harsh criticism of the partner’s interests and mockery of their plans;
a ban on seeing friends and relatives, up to living within four walls;
a routine in which nothing happens for years.
a relationship going round in a circle of “together — apart” that can neither continue nor end;
retreating to separate corners instead of talking;
no agreements, with each pulling in their own direction.

paragraphs: The main task is to go through difficulties together rather than run from them, and not to lock each other in. The World asks for both space and faithfulness at once.

sections.h2: Under the heart and why you met
paragraphs: **21 under the heart.** Searches call the “what connects” point “under the heart”: that is how the same point of the relationship line is labelled in a personal matrix. With 21 here (about 3 couples in 100), what connects you is shared travels and big goals: a trip you planned for a year, a move to a new country, a project bigger than both of you. Returns bring you closer too — after a business trip, after a separation, home.

**Why you met.** This point is read only in the plus, and 21 is uncommon here — about 3 couples in 100: it is the sum of the months of birth, September and December or October and November. Lisovskaya has no separate text on it, and by the meaning of the arcanum it reads like this: the couple came together to widen each other’s world — to pull each other out of the familiar circle and build a shared picture of life. Often one partner travels beyond their home town for the first time precisely thanks to the other.

sections.h2: The couple’s values: a whole that does not set
paragraphs: The twenty-first’s most frequent point is “The couple’s values”, one of the five main cards of the reading: 21 stands here for almost 13 couples in 100. Its number is not added up from the partners’ points but recalculated from the couple’s purposes, so only multiples of three occur in this point. For Lisovskaya it is the couple’s spiritual purpose — its values and the path the two are to walk together.

**With The World in the values, a couple puts life together as a whole and does not let it set.** Everything is in its place, and on just such a day one of them says “What if we…” — and soon there is a second-hand piano in the room that neither of them can play. The minus is guarding what has taken shape against change: the same weekend routes, the same jokes, “what for?” in reply to any idea, and the shared world turns into a museum where nothing may be touched.

sections.h2: What helps a couple with The World

ul: Keep up shared interests and find new ones.
Travel together more often — even just for a weekend in a nearby town.
Set big shared goals that span years.
Settle conflicts with words and don’t repeat the same hard conversational scripts.
Don’t forbid your partner their friends and relatives, and don’t re-educate them to fit your views.
Go through difficulties together rather than retreating to separate corners.
Be generous — to each other and to the people around you.

paragraphs: The method gives no compatibility percentages: 21 in a couple’s matrix describes the theme of the union, not how strong it is.

faq.q: Why does 21 stand in the couple’s common language so often?
faq.a: In a personal matrix only seven numbers occur at the relationship entry point — 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 and 21. In a couple this point is the sum of two such numbers, and the choice stays the same. So each of them comes up often, and 21 stands in the common language for about one couple in nine.

faq.q: What does 21 under the heart mean in compatibility?
faq.a: In a couple’s matrix it is the “what connects” point. With 21 you are brought closer by shared travels, big goals and returns after separations. Plans bigger than both of you work well: a move, a house, a shared business.

faq.q: Is a long-distance relationship a sign of 21?
faq.a: Not necessarily, but The World copes with it better than most. Lisovskaya describes couples with 21 who move abroad, work on rotation or spend long periods on business trips — and after separations only miss each other more. The matrix does not predict distance; it describes the fact that for a couple with 21 separation does not mean coldness.

faq.q: We keep getting together and splitting up. Is that the minus of 21?
faq.a: It is one of the two poles of The World’s minus — escape: a relationship going round in circles that can neither continue nor end. The other pole is stagnation. Lisovskaya sees the way out in going through difficulties together rather than separating, and in not repeating the same hard conversation.

faq.q: We both have 21 in our personal matrices. Is it a “double World”?
faq.a: No. Matching numbers in personal charts are a shared language, not compatibility: both need space, and that brings you closer. The shared risk is that when both run from routine, there is nobody to keep the home going. If both have 21 in the same point, the couple’s matrix will have 6 there: 21 + 21 = 42, and 4 + 2 = 6.

seo.title: Destiny matrix compatibility 22: The Fool in a couple
seo.description: Destiny matrix compatibility 22: freedom for two — trust without checking up, or living like flatmates. Where The Fool occurs and what it means for a couple.

items.title: Arcanum 22 in destiny matrix compatibility: The Fool — freedom for two
items.short: 22 in destiny matrix compatibility is The Fool, and its key in a couple is freedom. In the plus it is a union of two self-sufficient people who trust each other and so do not check up, take problems and money lightly and calmly start from scratch. In the minus it is freedom without boundaries: they live like flatmates, the status of the relationship is unclear, and an easy start breaks at the first serious step. Below is how 22 appears in a couple’s matrix, where it occurs and what it means at each point.

sections.h2: How 22 gets into a couple’s matrix
paragraphs: A compatibility matrix is calculated from the dates of birth of two people: each one’s personal matrix is built, the matching points are added together, and the sum is reduced to 22 by adding its digits if it is larger. Yuliana Lisovskaya described this method in most detail in her book Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024). 22 in such a matrix speaks of the union itself, not of either one. If 22 stands in the personal matrix of one partner, it is about that person, not the couple.

22 in a couple is always a sum of exactly 22: sums above 22 give no more than 12 after their digits are added. Hence a simple consequence: at the point where the couple has The Fool, each partner has a number below twenty-two. If one of you has 22 at some point of your personal matrix, the couple will have a different number at that point.

An example: the dates 12.04.1992 and 06.05.1997. Both centres are 11, together 22, and The Fool stands in the couple’s centre. For this couple it sounds twice more: in the points “parents together” (5 and 17) and “what you teach” (17 and 5). And the second partner has 22 in the middle of their personal karmic tail — but the couple has 8 there: 22 and 4 give 26, and 2 + 6 = 8.

A couple’s centre of 22 comes from six combinations of personal centres: 4 and 18, 6 and 16, 8 and 14, 9 and 13, 10 and 12, 11 and 11. It is uncommon, about 4 couples in 100: most people’s centre is between 5 and 11, and the sum of two centres rarely reaches 22.

sections.h2: Where a couple can have 22
paragraphs: The Fool has no favourite point in a couple’s matrix: in each of its 14 possible points it stands for 2–5 couples in 100. Most often — in the “parents together” point, least often — in the “why you met” point. It never appears in the common language point, where the couple’s tail begins: only multiples of three come up there.

paragraphs: Lisovskaya sets out the energy by sphere — image, atmosphere, finances, tasks — rather than for each point. For points she has no separate words on — the children points, for example — what follows is our reading based on the meaning of the point and the arcanum.

sections.h2: The couple as parents: 22 in the children points
paragraphs: It is worth starting with this sphere: “parents together” is The Fool’s most frequent point in a couple.

**Parents together** (about 5 couples in 100). Light-hearted, playful parents with whom the children have fun: a camping trip on a Friday evening because “why not”, a celebration out of nothing, permission to get dirty. The parents support each other without keeping score: when one is tired, the other takes the children for the whole day, and nobody keeps a log of who looked after them for how long. The minus is that there is no firm footing: the rules change every day, the parents behave like older brothers and sisters, and the child lacks adults to lean on.

**What you teach** (about 4 in 100). Courage, curiosity, a sense of humour, the ability to try new things and not fear mistakes. The child grows up feeling that the world is big and interesting and that failure is not a catastrophe. In the minus — inconsistency: allowed today, forbidden tomorrow, promises forgotten, and the child learns not to trust words.

sections.h2: What fills the union
paragraphs: The Fool stands in this point for 4–5 couples in 100. Moves and travel fill it, along with entertainment, a sense of humour, optimism and unconditional support. A couple with 22 recovers not on a scheduled holiday but on a spontaneous trip, in shared laughter at what seemed a disaster yesterday, in the certainty that the other will back any crazy idea. Strength also comes from each staying themselves: their own friends, their own interests, their own time — and the joy of being together again.

sections.h2: The money of a couple with The Fool

ul: **Way into money** (about 4 couples in 100). Income stalls because of carelessness: spending without control, debts, life without financial discipline, sometimes periods without work. A minimum of structure that does not stifle freedom helps avoid this: a cushion for three months and one rule about big purchases.

**Path to prosperity** (about 4 in 100): a light attitude to money in a good sense. The couple spends and gives a lot, but also easily starts from scratch, finds a way out of any problem and does not panic when something collapses. Sometimes well-off parents help.

**Attitude to material things** (about 4 in 100): they do not hold on to things — they give them away easily and move house easily with two suitcases. In the minus — uncontrolled spending and immaturity.

**Where it leaks and how status affects the union** (about 3 in 100). The holes are debts, unemployment, lack of discipline. When one partner cannot or will not earn, the other’s lightness quickly runs out.

sections.h2: How the couple is seen and what can spoil it
paragraphs: **How others see the couple** (about 4 couples in 100). A creative, vivid couple of adventurers, often with flexible hours. They take problems lightly and even in the plus may seem frivolous: “when will they ever grow up”, relatives say of a couple for whom everything is fine. In the minus it is visible from outside that this is a couple in name only: they do everything separately, live like flatmates, and the relationship is there to fill a void.

**What can spoil it** (about 4 in 100). Uncertainty: it is unclear whether you are together or not, whether you are a couple or “just seeing each other”. Selfishness, thoughtless actions, rigidity. And an imbalance Lisovskaya describes separately: one demands an account and is jealous, while not keeping their own rules.

sections.h2: The couple’s tasks: freedom and responsibility
paragraphs: The sphere “The couple’s karmic tail” has three points — the entry, the middle and the main task. 22 occurs in the middle (about 4 couples in 100) and in the main task (about 3 in 100), but not at the entry. These points are read mostly through the minus.

ul: **too much freedom and flirting** — what seems like lightness to one feels like neglect to the other;
**no boundaries and no responsibility**: nobody knows what is allowed and what is not until someone gets hurt;
**running from problems** while reproaching the partner — leaving, switching off, and casting the other as the culprit;
**control and jealousy** while not keeping one’s own rules;
**an easy start and problems at the serious steps**: they got together quickly and lived merrily, but at the question of a wedding, a mortgage or a child everything stalled;
**mood swings, mutual dependence, manipulation**.

paragraphs: The main task is to combine freedom with responsibility: to think about the consequences before a serious step, not after.

sections.h2: The Fool in the couple’s centre: trust without checking up
paragraphs: The couple’s centre is what happens between you without witnesses. 22 occurs here for 3–4 couples in 100.

**In the plus** it is a union of two self-sufficient people who entered the relationship consciously, having learned from past mistakes. The trust is such that there is no point in checking up: the phone lies on the table screen up, and nobody looks at it. You are like best friends — you laugh, travel, support each other’s interests and work. Faults are accepted, and a difference in age or status does not get in the way.

**In the minus** there is no certainty. The status of the relationship is unclear even to the partners themselves, and the union turns into a game with lots of flirting and few commitments. Selfishness, thoughtless decisions, rigidity: “that’s what I want, full stop”.

sections.h2: 22 under the heart and why you met
paragraphs: **22 under the heart.** Searches call the “what connects” point “under the heart”: that is how the same point of the relationship line is labelled in a personal matrix. With The Fool here (about 3 couples in 100), what connects you is adventures and laughter: a trip without a plan, the night the car broke down and you sang in a field until morning, jokes only the two of you understand. The ability to start again brings you closer too: a move, a new job, a new city — everything you did together from scratch.

**Why you met.** The Fool’s rarest point — about 2 couples in 100. It is the sum of the months of birth, and only October and December, or both in November, give 22 here. Lisovskaya has no separate text on it; by the meaning of the arcanum the couple met in order to start something new without fear — to teach each other lightness, to take a risk where neither would have dared alone.

sections.h2: What helps a couple with The Fool

ul: Give each other freedom without checking up — and agree where that freedom ends.
Think about responsibility before serious steps: a wedding, a home, a child call for a conversation, not an impulse.
Keep financial and moral independence: each with their own income and their own support.
Find a balance between your own wishes and caring for those close to you.
Forget the words “must” and “ought to” — and still do what you yourselves promised.
Take temporary separations calmly: a business trip is not infidelity, and an evening with friends is not an escape.
Accept your partner as they are, without trying to turn The Fool into a respectable person.

paragraphs: The method gives no compatibility percentages: 22 in a couple describes what the union rests on and where it needs boundaries.

faq.q: Does 22 in compatibility mean a relationship that isn’t serious?
faq.a: Not necessarily. A couple with 22 may look frivolous from outside even in the plus: lots of laughter, travel, freedom. But at its base is the trust of two self-sufficient people. Frivolity is The Fool’s minus: an unclear status and running from responsibility — and it can be worked on.

faq.q: Why is 22 so rare in the couple’s centre?
faq.a: The couple’s centre is the sum of two personal centres, and most people’s centre is between 5 and 11. To get exactly 22 you need 11 and 11, 10 and 12, or even rarer combinations. That is why The Fool stands in the couple’s centre for about 4 couples in 100 — less often than any number from 13 to 21.

faq.q: What does 22 under the heart mean in compatibility?
faq.a: In a couple’s matrix it is the “what connects” point. With 22 you are brought closer by adventures, spontaneous trips, shared laughter and the ability to start from scratch together. The union grows stronger when there is room for play in it.

faq.q: One of us has 22 in their personal matrix. Does that affect the couple?
faq.a: It is about the person, not the union. In a couple’s matrix the matching points are added together, and if one partner already has 22 there, the sum will be larger and reduce to a different number: 22 and 4 give 26, that is, 8. That is why The Fool in a couple is always assembled from two smaller numbers.

faq.q: How can a couple with 22 combine freedom and faithfulness?
faq.a: Lisovskaya advises giving the partner freedom without checking up, but thinking about responsibility before serious steps. In practice this is an agreement on boundaries: what is definitely off limits for each of you. Freedom within those boundaries is The Fool’s strength; rules for one partner only are its minus.

seo.title: Destiny matrix compatibility 3: The Empress in a couple
seo.description: Destiny matrix compatibility 3: where the three stands in a couple and how The Empress shapes home life, money, children and quarrels. With a worked example.

items.title: The 3 in a compatibility matrix: what The Empress means for a couple
items.short: A home where there is always food and guests, children, a shared business, money you want to invest in something — this is how the three looks in a couple’s matrix, the energy of growth and abundance. Most often it stands in the point of the couple’s common language and wishes — for one couple in seven. Its plus is a practical, warm, well-settled union. Its minus is a tally of “who has put in more”, jealousy, relatives who decide for the two of them, and an imbalance in which one partner grows while the other stays where they were.

sections.h2: Where a 3 in a couple’s matrix comes from: the sums 3 and 30
paragraphs: A couple’s matrix is a third chart put together from two personal ones. The partners’ matching points are added together, and a sum above 22 is reduced by adding its digits. This is how Yuliana Lisovskaya calculates it in her book Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024), and this is how our calculator works.

Two sums give a 3: 3 and 30. A sum of 3 is possible only as 1 + 2, and a person has a 1 only in the day and month of birth. So a 3 in a couple is almost always a reduced 30: 15 + 15, 12 + 18, 9 + 21, 8 + 22 and so on.

**An example.** The partners were born on 25 July 1992 and 25 September 1987. In the point that makes up the couple’s common language, both have 15: 15 + 15 = 30, 3 + 0 = 3. In the point “What fills the union” one has 14 and the other 16 — again 30 and again a 3. This couple’s tail is 3-7-13: it starts with the three as well.
A 3 in both partners’ personal matrices does not give a 3 in the couple: 3 + 3 = 6. The couple’s energy is always a sum, not a match.

sections.h2: The points where a 3 occurs
paragraphs: The three is spread unevenly across a couple’s matrix: two points — the common language and “The couple’s values” — give it to almost 27 couples in 100, while in the rest it stands for about four couples in a hundred or fewer. The figures are the share of all pairs of dates from 1900 to 2026; in brackets is the point’s letter in Lisovskaya’s book, transliterated from Russian.

sections.h2: Common language and entry to the task: the three’s most frequent place
paragraphs: The common language point shows what the couple strives for, what it agrees on and in what language the two understand each other. It stands on two lines at once: on the relationship line and at the start of the couple’s tail. That is why it is read both ways — as shared wishes and as the first resistance to those wishes.

**As a common language.** The three speaks the language of deeds and care. You want the same thing: a home that is warm and smells of good cooking, children or a shared business, things chosen with love, prosperity you can see. It is easier for you to make up through actions than words: one silently peels a tangerine for the other, the other goes out early to warm up the car. You make plans willingly and in detail — where the nursery will be, when you will get a plot of land, what you will plant.

**As an entry to the task.** The reverse side of the same wish is “we want everything at once”. You want to grow faster than money allows, and loans or help from parents come into play. Care replaces conversation: everyone is fed, everything is done, and nobody knows what the partner is unhappy about. A contest of “who has put in more” appears — money, effort, nerves. Immaturity grows here too: waiting for someone to decide for you — a mother, the partner, circumstances.

sections.h2: The three in the role of parents
paragraphs: The parents sphere is about what you are like together as the elders — for your own children, if you have or will have them, and for everyone you look after: nephews and nieces, younger siblings, godchildren.

**“Parents together”.** With a three you are generous, warm parents. The house is full of children — your own and other people’s — food, celebrations and noise. In this role you support each other with deeds: one puts the children to bed, the other does the washing-up, and nobody has to explain. The risk is spoiling them: presents instead of attention and “let them have everything we never had”. The second risk is an imbalance in which all the parenting falls on one partner while the other “helps”.

**“What you teach”.** The three teaches children to grow and create: to bake bread, look after plants, build a birdhouse, carry what they start through to a result they can touch. And it teaches that caring for loved ones is normal and joyful. The minus here is overprotection that keeps a child from growing up independent.

sections.h2: Presents, walks and the tally of “who has put in more”
paragraphs: **What fills.** The three restores a couple through joy and abundance: presents for no reason, walks, trips, making things together — from renovation to baking — shared purchases for the home, each other’s successes. This point is read in the plus even when the three itself is in the minus: after a hard month, a Saturday market, a new throw on the sofa or an evening when you made something with your hands together will bring you back to each other.

**Where it sparks.** If the three stands in the point that shows conflicts and non-acceptance, your quarrels are about contribution and recognition. Who earns more, who does more around the house, whose mother is right. This is where jealousy, rivalry and disdain for the one who brings in less or has “fallen behind” live. Another source of quarrels is an empty home: no comfort, no shared table, and the couple starts falling apart into two neighbours. And the relatives: if their word weighs more than your shared one, the three shows it quickly.

sections.h2: Money and home life in a couple with a 3
paragraphs: A couple has four money points, and the three occurs in each of them — for about three or four couples in a hundred.

**“Home and things”.** Your attitude to material things is that of good housekeepers: investing in the home, renovation, good furniture, the children’s future, saving and investing. A shared budget with sensible spending. In the minus — extravagance, living off parents or, on the contrary, stinginess in which money for comfort always seems a waste.

**“Way into money”.** For a couple with a three, difficulties with income mean feast or famine and material dependence: of one on the other or of both on their parents. The way out is shared goals you earn for, and work of one’s own for each, rather than one breadwinner and one dependant.

**“Path to prosperity”.** Prosperity comes through growth: a shared goal, family, children, a home, land, a shared business or one’s own. Lisovskaya notes that for such a couple an official marriage opens up opportunities — joint property and shared plans that are easier to pursue as two.

**“Where it leaks” and “Success and the union”.** Holes in the budget are spending on comfort, children and presents beyond what you can afford. And the three shows plainly how each partner’s status affects the union: one grows, the other stands still and starts to feel left behind. There is one remedy — each needs a life’s work of their own, outside the couple.

sections.h2: Under the heart: what connects a couple with a 3
paragraphs: In searches, the point that shows what connects a couple is called “under the heart”. Lisovskaya reads it as the union’s positive potential — the shared events and activities you come together around.

With a three, what connects you is what can be grown together. A home you have been doing up for years. A country cottage where every bush was planted by the two of you. Children, celebrations around a big table, a shared business that grew from a hobby into an income. The three under the heart asks you not to forget about pleasure: a dinner you both dressed up for means more to this couple than it seems.

sections.h2: Why you met: to grow something together
paragraphs: The sphere “Why you met” is made of two cards: the image of the couple and “What to create together”.

**“What to create together”.** Lisovskaya reads this point only in the plus, and for the three she gives a direct answer — fruitfulness, abundance, growth. You were brought together to grow something: a family, children, a shared business, a home, sometimes a move closer to nature. Sometimes the task is humbler and more important: learning to see the long view, to handle money as a family, or to thaw out after past relationships that left a chill.

**“Image of the couple”.** From outside you are a well-off, practical, well-matched couple in which the partners openly respect each other. There may be many children, or children from different marriages. Prosperity may arouse envy. In the minus the image changes: stinginess or lack of money, stagnation, small talk, public quarrels and jealousy, poor relations with relatives. If there are no children, everyone from an aunt to the neighbour pesters such a couple with advice.

sections.h2: The tasks of a couple with a 3: relatives, money, jealousy
paragraphs: The couple’s karmic tail is read mostly in the minus: what the couple has to go through. The key point is “Main task”; the middle and the entry reveal it.
**“Main task”.** With a three it is:

ul: to step out from under the influence of the mother and relatives and make decisions as two;
to get through a financial crisis and learn practicality instead of living from feast to famine;
to cope with jealousy and the temptations life throws up;
to arrive at shared values and stop waiting for someone to provide;
to go carefully through the theme of children — without pressure and without other people’s expectations.

paragraphs: **“Middle of the task”.** A three in the middle of the tail is rare — fewer than one couple in a hundred. It suggests where the way to solving the main task lies: through practical things — a shared budget, a home of your own, boundaries with relatives, the habit of carrying what you start through to a result.

sections.h2: Atmosphere: a 3 in the couple’s centre is very rare
paragraphs: A three stands in the centre of a couple’s matrix for about two couples in a thousand. The couple’s centre is the sum of two personal centres, and they give 30 in only a few combinations: 8 and 22, 10 and 20, 12 and 18, 14 and 16. Centres of 16, 18, 20 and 22 are rare in people, hence the rarity.

If the three is in the centre after all, the atmosphere inside the couple is comfort, order and good housekeeping, care, doing things together, sometimes being spoilt. Often one leads and the other is softer and more flexible. In the minus — no comfort, rows, jealousy, rivalry and belittling of the one who earns less.

sections.h2: The couple’s values: what grows from care
paragraphs: “The couple’s values” is one of the five main cards of the reading. Its number is not the sum of the partners’ matching points: it is recalculated from the couple’s purposes, so only multiples of three occur here — 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 and 21. The three stands in the values for almost 12 couples in 100 — its second place after the common language. For Lisovskaya this point is the couple’s spiritual purpose: its values and the path the two are to walk together.

**In the values, the three says: what matters to you is what grows from your care.** A warm home, a business raised from nothing, children, a garden that remembers who planted it — the couple measures life by what has come up. The difficulty is giving all the attention to the harvest and forgetting each other: talk only about the household, rest “once everything is done”, and one partner grows while the other gets stuck in daily chores and feels like an appendage to someone else’s success.

sections.h2: Advice for a couple with The Empress

ul: **A life’s work of one’s own for each.** Lisovskaya’s main advice for the three. When both grow, the tally of “who has put in more” disappears, and so does the feeling of falling behind.
**Learn to decide on your own.** Each partner’s independence does not get in the couple’s way; it protects it from immaturity.
**Find time for the two of you.** Without children, guests and housework — at least one evening a week.
**Talk about wishes directly.** Hints and resentment that the other “didn’t guess” do not suit the three.
**Think about making the relationship official.** The author advises marriage for the three: for this couple it is not a formality but the basis of shared prosperity.
**Work on jealousy** — by talking, not by checking up.

sections.h2: A 3 in a partner’s personal matrix is read differently
paragraphs: If a three stands in the personal matrix of one of you, it is that person’s trait: in a relationship they bring home, warmth and patience and expect appreciation in return. Their main imbalance is caring instead of talking. In a personal chart the three can also stand in the point under the heart, and there too it means care — but that is one person’s position, not the couple’s. A couple’s matrix is a separate calculation, and personal readings are not carried over to its points.

faq.q: What does 3 mean in a compatibility matrix?
faq.a: It is the energy of growth and abundance in a union: a home, children, a shared business, money invested in the future. Where exactly it works depends on the point. Most often the three stands in the couple’s common language — then you want the same things and understand each other through care and deeds.

faq.q: We have a 3 in our common language. Is that good?
faq.a: The matrix gives no grades. The three’s common language is a wish to build and grow together, and that is a good support. The risk is that care will replace conversation and wanting “everything at once” will pull you into debt. If you talk about what you want and both of you grow, the three works in the plus.

faq.q: Can a 3 be in the centre of a couple’s matrix?
faq.a: It can, but very rarely — for about two couples in a thousand. For that the partners’ centres must add up to 30: for example, 10 and 20 or 14 and 16.

faq.q: We both have a 3 in our personal matrices. Will the couple have one?
faq.a: Not necessarily. The points add up: two threes in the same point give a six. A three appears in a couple when the sum of the matching points equals 3 or 30.

faq.q: Does a 3 in a couple mean there will be children?
faq.a: No. The matrix predicts nothing about children. The three speaks of growth in general: it may be a family, a shared business, a home, a move or the ability to manage money together. What you grow is up to you.

seo.title: Destiny matrix compatibility 4: The Emperor in a couple
seo.description: Destiny matrix compatibility 4: where The Emperor stands in a couple, how he holds home life, money and roles, and why order without warmth turns cold.

items.title: The 4 in a compatibility matrix: The Emperor in a couple
items.short: Shared rules, savings for a rainy day, roles divided without argument and the feeling of a reliable person at your back — the four brings support and order into a couple’s matrix. Most often it lands in the material points — home life and money — and in the parents sphere. In the plus it is a solid union of two partners who cover for each other, with passion behind a closed door. In the minus — “everyone toes the line”, coldness and a struggle over who is in charge at home.

sections.h2: The sums 4, 31 and 40: how The Emperor appears in a couple
paragraphs: Compatibility by the destiny matrix can be looked at in two ways. The first is what each partner brings into the relationship from their personal chart. The second is the matrix of the couple itself: the matching points of two personal matrices are added together, and a sum above 22 is reduced by adding its digits. The result is a third chart, and this page is about it. The calculation and the meanings follow Yuliana Lisovskaya’s book Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024); it is her school, not a generally accepted canon, and the method gives no compatibility percentages.

Three sums give a 4: 4, 31 and 40. A sum of 4 is rare — for it one partner must have a 1 or a 2, and these are uncommon in people — so a four in a couple is usually a reduced 31 or 40: for example, 9 + 22, 15 + 16 or 20 + 20.

**An example.** The partners were born on 12 June 1993 and 25 June 1989. The material point is calculated from the year: 1 + 9 + 9 + 3 = 22 for one, 1 + 9 + 8 + 9 = 27 → 9 for the other. 22 + 9 = 31, 3 + 1 = 4 — the four lands in “Attitude to material things”. For the same couple the point “What fills the union” adds 18 and 13 — again 31 and again a four.

sections.h2: Where the four occurs and where it does not
paragraphs: The four hardly has favourite places in a couple: in most points it stands for two to six couples in a hundred, and only the centre is almost closed to it. The figures cover all pairs of dates from 1900 to 2026; the letter in brackets is the point’s label in Lisovskaya’s book, transliterated from Russian.

paragraphs: One point is missing from the list: “Common language” — also “Entry to the task” — never holds a four. Every couple has only 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 or 21 there: that is how this point is calculated.

sections.h2: Home life and money: the four’s main territory
paragraphs: **“Home and things”.** “Measure twice, cut once” is the main law of home life with a four. There is always money put by for a rainy day, big decisions are taken slowly, the important comes first — housing, a car, a cushion of savings — and the pleasant after. They neither lend nor borrow. They save with children in mind, so that they get more than you had. The home is in order, every thing has its place and every kind of spending its own column. In the minus seriousness turns into rigidity: “that’s not how we do things”, and no argument works.

**“Path to prosperity”.** Money comes to such a couple through a system: a stable job, a business of their own, long projects, rules they keep to for years. Separate savings pots for different goals suit the four — one for holidays, one for renovation, one for the children’s education.

**“Where it leaks” and “Success and the union”.** The four’s holes are not in spending but in narrowness of view: missed opportunities because something is “risky”, and quarrels over who controls the budget. Status and work affect the union through power: whoever earns more starts deciding for both. Lisovskaya advises such couples to share the running of the budget and the areas of responsibility rather than compete for the lead.

**“Way into money”.** Here the four is let down by slowness and caution: while you were doing the sums, the opportunity went. The task is to build a systematic income rather than wait for something to change by itself.

In the book, the budget in such couples is more often run by the man. In life something else matters more: that it is clear who is responsible for what, and that the two of you decided it together, out loud.

sections.h2: Parents with a four: a united front
paragraphs: This sphere is not only about children. It is about what kind of elders you become together — for your own children, godchildren, the younger ones in the family.

**“Parents together”.** With a four you are a dependable home base. The child has a routine, rules and the certainty of being protected. Parents in such a couple are a united front: one does not overrule the other’s decision, and you argue behind a closed door, not in front of the children. The minus is bringing up a child “the proper way” instead of “the way this child needs”, and strictness with little affection in it.

**“What you teach”.** The four teaches children to answer for their words, keep promises, plan and look after what they have earned. It teaches that an adult’s word is law. It is good when the child’s right to an opinion is added to this; bad when the rules become more important than the person they were made for.

sections.h2: Plans, strategies and arguments about power
paragraphs: **What fills.** The four is fed by shared goals and plans: drawing up a plan for the year together, setting out the budget, choosing a plot of land. Rules and order of their own, passion not shown in public, a feeling of being provided for. There is something unexpected too: organising celebrations and strategy games — chess, strategy board games, long matches in the evenings. This point is always read in the plus: even strictness works for you here.

**Where it sparks.** A four in the quarrels point says: you argue about power. Who decides, whose rules, why again without me. Nit-picking over details, tight control, decisions made for everyone. And the four’s particular trouble is a lack of visible emotion: you cannot tell from the partner’s face whether they are pleased or angry, so the other starts guessing, and then tires of guessing.

sections.h2: Under the heart: one team
paragraphs: In searches this point is called “under the heart”, and in our reading it is labelled “What connects”. It shows which shared undertaking holds the couple together best.

With a four, what connects you is building a life together: a home you put up according to plan, a family business, a big goal several years away that both are ready to put up with things for. And the feeling that you protect each other: in trouble, in an argument with relatives, in a conflict at work, the partner is always on your side. A four under the heart is “you and I are one team”, said not in words but in deeds.

sections.h2: Why you met: to build a stable life
paragraphs: **“What to create together”.** For the four Lisovskaya names plainly why you met: to build a stable life. To join forces, continue the family line, reach a steady income. And to learn — responsibility, mutual respect, sharing out roles and trust. Her list also has an item unexpected for The Emperor — learning gentleness. The author reads this point only in the plus.

**“Image of the couple”.** From outside you are a serious, practical, somewhat private couple, wrapped up in family. Reserved with outsiders, you do not let your own people be hurt. Often these are entrepreneurs or people with a solid position. In the minus the image hardens: one suppresses the other and does not let them speak, everyone “toes the line” even when visiting, and the couple goes nowhere and is friends with no one.

sections.h2: The couple’s tasks: gentleness, feelings and a shared wheel
paragraphs: In the couple’s tasks the four shows where order stops helping. These points are read mostly through the minus: what will have to change.
**“Main task”.** The four has to:

ul: handle harshness and anger so that they do not break the one close to you;
get what you want directly, without manipulation;
not set up rules that later get in your own way;
add movement and spontaneity to life;
learn to talk about feelings out loud;

share control instead of competing for it. The one used to carrying everything alone should hand over part of the wheel while staying in the important decisions. The one used to being decided for should not slide into passivity and dependence.

paragraphs: **“Middle of the task”.** A four in the middle of the tail suggests how to solve the main task: through structure. Agree on rules that suit both of you, write them down, and review them a year later.

sections.h2: Atmosphere: a 4 in the couple’s centre is rare
paragraphs: A four in a couple’s centre turns up for two couples in a thousand. The couple’s centre is the sum of two personal centres, and they can give 31 or 40 in only a few combinations: 9 and 22, 11 and 20, 13 and 18, 18 and 22, 20 and 20.

If the four is in the centre after all, the atmosphere inside the couple is passion, love and respect behind outward reserve. Trust and backing each other up, strictness without fanaticism, a conservative view of upbringing. According to Lisovskaya, such a couple has a certain passivity even in the plus. In the minus — despotism, nit-picking and a coldness in which the feelings are there but cannot be seen.

sections.h2: How a couple with The Emperor can keep from freezing

ul: **Agree on the framework.** Rules that suit both of you, not one.
**Share the budget and the responsibility.** Not “who is in charge” but “who is responsible for what”.
**Learn about money** — together, not with one who understands and one who trusts.
**Do sport together.** The four needs an outlet for its drive.
**Trust time with friends.** An evening the partner spends with friends is not a breach of order.
**Look after passion.** Surprises and spontaneity are the antidote to “on schedule”.

sections.h2: A 4 in a partner’s personal matrix
paragraphs: A four in the personal chart of one partner is that person’s own trait: they bring reliability and order into the relationship and need respect and clarity in return. This is a different calculation: a personal four does not pass into the couple’s matrix by itself but adds up with the partner’s number in the same point. Two fours in one point give the couple an eight.

faq.q: What does 4 mean in destiny matrix compatibility?
faq.a: Support, order and responsibility — that is what the four brings into a couple’s matrix. Most often it stands in the couple’s home life and money: you are thrifty, you save, you decide slowly and you share out duties. The plus is reliability and passion behind a closed door; the minus is coldness, control and a struggle for the lead.

faq.q: Can a 4 be in the couple’s common language?
faq.a: No. “Common language” — also “Entry to the task” — always holds a multiple of three for any couple: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 or 21. If you are looking for a four in the couple’s relationship, look at the cards “What connects” and “Success and the union”: it occurs there.

faq.q: Does a 4 in a couple mean one partner will be in charge?
faq.a: Not necessarily. The four says that the question of power and roles matters to you. In the plus the roles are shared out and suit everyone; in the minus there is a struggle over them. In the book the man decides, but for a couple it matters more that the roles are shared out at all, and out loud, rather than by gender.

faq.q: Why is a 4 almost never in the couple’s centre?
faq.a: For that the partners’ centres must add up to 31 or 40 — for example, 11 and 20 or 18 and 22 — and such high centres are rare in people. A four in the centre turns up for about two couples in a thousand.

faq.q: How can a couple with a 4 avoid turning into flatmates on a schedule?
faq.a: Talking about feelings out loud is The Emperor’s main task in a couple. And leave room for unplanned joys: a spontaneous trip, a surprise, an evening without a to-do list. You will have order anyway; warmth has to be added on purpose.

seo.title: Destiny matrix compatibility 5: The Hierophant in a couple
seo.description: Destiny matrix compatibility 5: shared rules, traditions, a careful budget and relatives who interfere. Where the five stands in a couple and how to read it.

items.title: The 5 in a compatibility matrix: The Hierophant and the couple’s rules
items.short: With a five, the union in a couple’s matrix is like a small school where both are teachers and pupils: rules and customs of their own, shared views, a carefully balanced budget and a partner who is also a best friend. The five is one of the most frequent energies in a couple, and it most often stands in home life, money and the parents sphere. Its minus is lecturing, the urge to remake each other and relatives who get in too deep.

sections.h2: The five’s four sums and an example from the book
paragraphs: A couple’s matrix is calculated separately from the personal charts: the two partners’ matching points are added together, and a sum above 22 is reduced by adding its digits. The result is a third chart with its own meanings for the points. The calculation and the meanings here follow Yuliana Lisovskaya’s book Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024); it is her school.
Four sums give a 5: 5, 23, 32 and 41. That is why it is frequent in couples: sums above 22 often reduce to exactly this number.

**A simpler example.** The material point is calculated from the year of birth. Someone born in 1990 has 1 + 9 + 9 + 0 = 19 there; someone born in 1993 has 1 + 9 + 9 + 3 = 22. 19 + 22 = 41, 4 + 1 = 5: any such couple has a five in “Attitude to material things”, whatever day and month the partners were born.

**An example from the book.** Lisovskaya analyses the couple born on 13 September 1970 and 2 July 1973. In the main task point the partners have 12 and 11, 12 + 11 = 23, 2 + 3 = 5. In our reading this couple’s tail is written as 6-11-5, in the book in reverse order, 5-11-6. The author describes the five in this analysis with the words “traditions”, “official marriage”, “rules and laws”, “like-minded people”, “knowledge and conversation” — that is its language.

sections.h2: The five’s most frequent places
paragraphs: In home life, money and parenting the five stands for almost one couple in eleven, and least often in the centre. Below are the shares across all pairs of dates from 1900 to 2026; in brackets is how Lisovskaya labels the point, transliterated from Russian.
