sections.h2: The five’s careful budget
paragraphs: **“Home and things”.** With a five the household is run conservatively and practically. Things are mended, not thrown away; grandmother’s tea set holds a place of honour; the budget is shared, purchases are for the family and the children, and savings grow slowly but surely. The good side is calm: you always have something to lean on. In the minus — fear of unnecessary spending, stinginess and perfectionism: a sofa takes six months to choose because the “right” one has not been found yet, while the old one is falling apart.

**“Path to prosperity”.** Money comes to a couple with a five through putting family first, through knowledge and playing fair by the rules. Study, a profession in which experience is valued, official employment, a shared business with clear rules — that is their road.

**“Way into money”.** The five’s income most often runs up against family: living off parents, family disputes and legal battles that drain energy, or a habit of not taking risks even when it is time to.

**“Where it leaks” and “Success and the union”.** The five’s hole is control. There is no shared budget, and one manages the other’s money “out of care”: hands it out, checks receipts, explains how it should have been done. Through status the five affects the union like this: whoever knows more or holds a higher position starts teaching the other how to live. It is better if each has a field of their own where they are the recognised master.

sections.h2: Parents with traditions
paragraphs: The parents sphere is read even without children: it is about what kind of mentors you are together — for your own children, if you have or will have them, for pupils, nephews and nieces, younger colleagues.

**“Parents together”.** The five makes you parent-mentors. The home has traditions — Sunday lunch, books before bed, a trip to the grandparents in the holidays — and the children know it will always be so. You support each other in this role with a single opinion: if the two of you decided, it is decided. The risk is bringing up a child by the rulebook rather than by the child, and arguing with your own parents about “the right way”.

**“What you teach”.** The five teaches knowledge, values and respect for elders: to read, to think, to keep one’s word, to know one’s roots. It is good when the rules come with an explanation of “why”. It is bad when the question “what for?” gets the answer “because that’s how it’s done”.

sections.h2: Traditions that nourish and lectures that start quarrels
paragraphs: **What fills.** The five’s strength is restored by doing things together and walks, family traditions, meeting other families, calm time for two. It matters that each grows in something of their own meanwhile — one learns a language, the other goes to a pottery class — and has the partner’s support. Here the five is always in the plus: even a love of order works for the union.

**Where it sparks.** The serious quarrels of a couple with a five here are about being right. The wish to remake the partner, lectures that “everything is wrong”, intolerance of other opinions, arguing for the sake of arguing. And, of course, the relatives: whose traditions come first, whose family to spend New Year with, who brings up the children how. There may also be disagreement about the most important thing — children, and whether a family in the usual sense is needed at all.

sections.h2: A model for others and laws of their own
paragraphs: **“Image of the couple”.** From outside you are a traditional, modest family that lives by its own rules and does not break them. Sometimes academic, sometimes religious, sometimes simply very “proper”. You are held up as an example, you are a single organism, people come to you for advice. In the minus the image is spoilt by snobbery and the certainty that you know best how others should live. There may also be rudeness towards those who live differently, and living at someone else’s expense with a high opinion of oneself.

**“What to create together”.** Lisovskaya has no “why you met” section for the five, but the meaning of the point — what the couple needs to create — can be read from the plus of the energy. You were brought together to build a family with laws of its own: your own traditions, holidays, way of reaching agreement. And to learn from each other — a profession, views, the ability to listen. This point is read only in the plus.

sections.h2: The couple’s tasks: relatives, boundaries and a rulebook of your own
paragraphs: The couple’s tasks are the bottom points of the matrix, its tail. Lisovskaya reads them mostly in the minus — as trials the union has to go through.

**“Middle of the task”.** A five in the middle of the tail is common — one couple in fourteen has it. It suggests that the key to the main task lies in rules and conversation: agreeing on the laws of your home rather than living by other people’s.
**“Main task”.** Here the five has to:

ul: move out of living with parents or at their expense;
stop the relatives interfering — sometimes it starts as early as the choice of partner;
build relations with each other’s families instead of fighting them;
decide together what your family will be: marriage, children, where to live;
learn to balance your differences without lecturing;
stop shutting yourselves off and stop remaking each other.

sections.h2: Under the heart: shared views and rituals
paragraphs: “Under the heart” in compatibility is the “What connects” point on the couple’s relationship line. Lisovskaya sees in it the union’s positive potential: what the two come together around.

With a five, what connects you is shared views and shared experience: study, books, long conversations about what matters, family rituals you invented yourselves. A church wedding or a formal ceremony, a yearly trip to the same place, a recipe handed down in the family — for this couple such things are not a formality but glue. And friendship: you not only love each other but respect each other’s minds.

sections.h2: Atmosphere: a 5 in the couple’s centre
paragraphs: The five takes the couple’s centre for about one couple in forty. It is the sum of two personal centres: for example, 9 and 14, 11 and 12, 10 and 22, or 16 and 16.

The atmosphere inside such a couple is trust and faithfulness. The partners are friends as well, with shared views and endless things to talk about. Authority in the family is accepted willingly: not because someone appointed themselves head, but because they are trusted in their field. Personal space is respected too. In the minus — tediousness, arguments over trifles, a habit of correcting the partner’s every word.

sections.h2: Advice for a couple with The Hierophant

ul: **Get on with the relatives, but don’t let them inside.** Respect — yes; the right to decide for you — no.
**Start holidays and places of your own.** Not only inherit other people’s traditions but create your own: your day, your café, your walk.
**Listen — to yourself and to your partner.** Sometimes the one who knows more is not the one who is right.
**Show yourselves independently.** Each has their own work, and the other supports it rather than grading it.
**Keep money by the rules.** For the five, prosperity comes through family, knowledge and honest, lawful ways.

sections.h2: A 5 in the partners’ personal charts is read differently
paragraphs: It is important to tell a five in the couple apart from a five in one of the partners. If it stands in the personal chart of one or both, values and rules — “the way we do things” — are a strong theme in the relationship. Common ground comes quickly when views coincide, and hard when each has brought their own rulebook into the home. Two people with fives would do well to agree in advance what one of them teaches and what the other does. Personal fives do not pass into the couple’s matrix: two fives in one point give the couple a ten.

faq.q: What does 5 mean in destiny matrix compatibility?
faq.a: It is the energy of shared rules, traditions, knowledge and conversation. A union with it rests on shared views and friendship, the budget is handled carefully and jointly, and authority is accepted willingly. The minus is lecturing, intolerance of other opinions and relatives who interfere in the couple’s life.

faq.q: Why is the 5 so frequent in a couple’s matrix?
faq.a: Four sums give it: 5, 23, 32 and 41. The sum of two numbers is often above 22 and reduces to a number from 3 to 12, and the five gets a noticeable share of those cases. In home life, money and parenting it stands for roughly one couple in eleven to thirteen.

faq.q: Does a 5 in a couple mean living by other people’s rules?
faq.a: On the contrary: the five’s task is to create your own. The risk is that the couple gets stuck in the parents’ rules or imposes its own on others. Lisovskaya’s advice is to get on with the relatives without letting them inside your boundaries, and to start traditions of your own.

faq.q: How often does a 5 stand in the couple’s centre?
faq.a: For about one couple in forty. For that the partners’ centres must add up to 23 or 32, for example 11 and 12 or 16 and 16. Then the atmosphere inside the union is trust, faithfulness and friendship.

faq.q: Is it good if we have a 5 in “Main task”?
faq.a: The matrix gives no grades. A five in the main task shows that the couple has to deal with the family’s influence and find its own rules: decide where and how to live, stop teaching each other. It is work, not a verdict.

seo.title: Destiny matrix compatibility 6: The Lovers in a couple
seo.description: Destiny matrix compatibility 6: a shared language of feelings, generosity, jealousy and a “peace, then war” seesaw. Where the six stands and how to read it.

items.title: The 6 in a compatibility matrix: The Lovers in a couple
items.short: Love, choice and beauty — that is what the six is about in a couple’s matrix: openness with no secrets, tenderness in public, deciding together even on small things, generosity and a wish to live beautifully. It is one of the most frequent energies in a couple: almost one couple in three has it in the point of common language and wishes. Its minus is the seesaw of “peace one day, war the next”, jealousy born of insecurity and words that hit exactly where it hurts, because you know each other too well.

sections.h2: Not a combination table: where a 6 in a couple comes from
paragraphs: Compatibility in the destiny matrix is not a comparison of two numbers. Tables like “6 goes well with 2, 4 and 14” compare arcana, not people. A couple’s matrix is built differently: the matching points of two personal matrices are added together and the sum is reduced to a number from 1 to 22 by adding its digits if it is above 22. This is how Yuliana Lisovskaya calculates it in her book Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024); the meanings of the points on this page follow her school — it is her practice, not a general canon of the method.
Four sums give a 6: 6, 24, 33 and 42.

**An example.** The partners were born on 7 June 1994 and 3 October 1990. In the point that makes up the couple’s common language, they have 9 and 15: 9 + 15 = 24, 2 + 4 = 6. The year of birth gives 5 and 19 — again 24 and again a six, this time in “Attitude to material things”. For this couple The Lovers sound both in their wishes and in their attitude to money.

**An example with the centre.** The partners were born on 14 December 1995 and 21 December 1990. Their personal centres are 10 and 14, 24 in total — the couple’s centre is a six. Both months are December, 12 + 12 = 24, and the six also lands in “What to create together”.

sections.h2: A frequency map: where The Lovers stand
paragraphs: Almost a third of all couples get a six in one and the same point — the common language. The second point is “The couple’s values”: the six is there for 22 couples in a hundred. In the others, except the centre, it stands for four to nine couples in a hundred. The shares are calculated across all pairs of dates from 1900 to 2026; in brackets is the point’s letter in Lisovskaya’s book, transliterated from Russian.

head: Sphere and card in the couple reading
Share of couples
rows: “Relationship and common language” — “Common language”; also “Entry to the task” in “The couple’s karmic tail” (D1)
“The couple’s values” — the couple’s spiritual purpose
“The couple’s karmic tail” — “Middle of the task” (D2)
“How others see the couple” — “How you are seen” (B)
“Relationship and common language” — “What connects”, under the heart (I)
“The couple’s money” — “Where it leaks”; also “Success and the union” (K)

sections.h2: Common language and entry to the task: almost one couple in three
paragraphs: The common language is the point where the relationship line and the couple’s tail meet. It is both the shared wishes and the first thing that gets in their way: it is read both ways.

**As a common language.** With a six you reach agreement through feelings. A decision is made when it “feels right” to both, not when the figures add up. You want the same thing: a love in which you can be yourselves, a beautiful life, a home you are glad to come back to, and a person beside you whom you choose afresh every day. You love talking about everything — from dreams to the colour of the curtains — and you are genuinely interested in the other’s opinion.

**As an entry to the task.** The six is the card of choice, and the resistance here is about choice too. Idealisation: the relationship has to be like a film, and the partner has to match the picture. Doubts: “did I choose right”, “what if there is better”. Insecurity, from which jealousy and control grow: checking where they are, who they are messaging, why they are taking so long to reply. At the entry to the tail the six has to learn to love a living person rather than an image.

sections.h2: Money for enjoying life
paragraphs: **“Home and things”.** For you money is a way to enjoy life. “We earn in order to spend” — without squandering, but without greed either: dinner at a good place, flowers for no reason, a trip you will talk about for years. Comfort and taste matter more than perfect order, and you choose big purchases together, arguing about the colour of the sofa until you are hoarse. In the minus — impulsive spending driven by emotion or, on the contrary, stinginess, mess and constant dissatisfaction with how much the partner brings in.

**“Path to prosperity”.** Money comes to a couple with a six through people: connections, socialising, work where taste, charm and the ability to please matter. Creativity, beauty, everything that makes life more pleasant — that is your territory.

**“Way into money”.** The six’s weak spot at the way into money is unstable earnings and a habit of spending according to mood. Buying something after a quarrel “to cheer yourself up” is the six’s typical hole in the budget.

**“Where it leaks” and “Success and the union”.** The six’s hole is gifts with strings attached and spending that replaces a conversation: an expensive present instead of an apology. And status affects the union through pride and admiration: the six needs to be proud of the partner, and when their successes become part of your image as a couple, one partner’s failure hits both.

sections.h2: The Lovers as parents
paragraphs: You may not have children — then these points speak of how the two of you look after the younger ones and those close to you.

**“Parents together”.** The six makes parents open in their love: they hug, praise, go to every school play and performance. The child sees that the parents love each other — and that is the best lesson you can give. The risk is making the child a participant in your seesaw: making up and quarrelling in front of them, or looking for an ally in them against the other parent.

**“What you teach”.** The six teaches choosing: friends, activities, one’s own taste. It teaches beauty and the ability to talk about feelings. The minus is expecting the child to live up to a pretty picture: grades, looks, “what will people say”.

sections.h2: Midweek dates and quarrels about love
paragraphs: **What fills.** You are restored by attention and closeness: a compliment that is not said out of habit, a date in the middle of the working week, a conversation about everything until midnight, a touch in passing. Even small joint decisions — which tiles, where to go on holiday — are not a burden for you but a reason to be together. Crises you have come through together fill you up too: after them you hold on to each other more tightly. Lisovskaya reads this point only in the plus.

**Where it sparks.** You quarrel seriously not over housework but over love. You are open with each other, so a word lands right on the sore spot. Jealousy, suspicion, checking messages, impulsive decisions that later have to be reversed. Peace gives way to war and war to peace, and both tire of the seesaw, although the love does not go anywhere. What is said in the heat of the moment is remembered for a long time here.

sections.h2: The couple’s tasks: to love a living person, not an image
paragraphs: In the couple’s karmic tail The Lovers speak of what gets in the way of love. These points are read first of all in the minus.

**“Middle of the task”.** Almost one couple in thirteen has a six in the middle of the tail. It says that the way to the main task lies through choice: to stop doubting your decision to be together and to choose each other again when things are hard.
**“Main task”.** Here The Lovers need to:

ul: learn to love themselves within the couple — sometimes one teaches this to the other;
let go of perfectionism and the ideal picture of the relationship;
stop remaking the partner to their own measure;
deal with a quick temper and with the insecurity that jealousy and control grow out of;
depend less on the relatives’ opinion;
recover together from a hard past experience, if one or both had one.

sections.h2: A couple people turn to look at
paragraphs: **“Image of the couple”.** This card comes from the partners’ days of birth. With a six you are a couple people turn to look at: beautiful, stylish, sociable, openly in love. You flirt with each other in front of everyone and tell stories in two voices, picking up each other’s sentences. In the minus the image comes in two kinds. Loud: showdowns in front of guests, jealousy for an audience, gossip — including about one’s own partner. Or, on the contrary, closed: a smooth façade in public, while what matters goes unsaid even between the two of you.

**“What to create together”.** Lisovskaya does not write separately about why a couple with a six met — the answer is made up of its plus. You were brought together to build a union where love is a daily choice, not an accident. Harmony, beauty, creativity, a home where both feel good. It is not read in the minus.

sections.h2: Under the heart with The Lovers: “we decided” itself
paragraphs: What searches call “under the heart” is, in a couple’s matrix, the card “What connects”: the shared events and questions that bring two people together.

With a six, what connects you is the feelings themselves and everything beautiful you do together. Anniversaries you never miss. Making things together — photographs, music, a renovation in which every corner has been discussed. Shared friends and parties where you are the best couple in the room. And decisions you make only as two: for the six, “we decided” is glue in itself.

sections.h2: A 6 in the centre: tenderness without secrets
paragraphs: About one couple in fifty-five gets a six in the couple’s centre. For that the partners’ personal centres must add up to 6, 24, 33 or 42: for example, 3 and 3, 8 and 16, 10 and 14, 11 and 22, 13 and 20.

The atmosphere inside such a couple is tenderness and trust. No secrets, many touches and conversations, duties shared equally, each other’s imperfections accepted. You make decisions together even on small things. In the minus — the same seesaw of “peace one day, war the next”, jealousy and words that wound.

sections.h2: The couple’s values: love as a daily choice
paragraphs: The six’s second most frequent point after the common language is “The couple’s values”, one of the five main cards of the reading: the six stands here for 22 couples in 100. This point is not added up from the partners’ points but recalculated from the couple’s purposes, so only 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 and 21 occur in it. For Lisovskaya it is the couple’s spiritual purpose — its values and the path the two are to walk together.

**With a six in the values, what matters most is choosing each other again, not from memory.** Love here is not a state you once fell into but a decision made anew: in the tenth year, on a Tuesday, after a row over an unwashed frying pan. The minus is when, instead of the person, you start choosing an improved version of them: “I love you, but if only you…” Each correction is small, yet together they say: you were accepted on conditions.

sections.h2: Advice for The Lovers

ul: **Take care with words.** The six’s most important rule: what is said in a rush of feeling is not forgotten.
**Don’t remake your partner to your standards.** You chose a living person, not a project.
**Let go of perfectionism.** There is no such thing as a perfect relationship; there is yours.
**Look for compromises.** “We” matters more than “I’m right”.
**Be honest and faithful** — for the six, trust is the foundation.
**Look after yourself.** Your appearance, interests, your own circle — it is easier not to be jealous when you love yourself.
**Pay less attention to other people’s opinions** — both relatives’ and followers’.

sections.h2: If one of you has a 6
paragraphs: A personal six describes one person: they bring warmth, taste and the ability to choose with the heart into a relationship, and they need reciprocity and appreciation themselves. It does not carry over into the couple’s chart by itself: at each point of the couple the personal number adds up with the partner’s number. Two sixes in one point give the couple a twelve.

faq.q: What does 6 mean in destiny matrix compatibility?
faq.a: A six in a couple’s matrix is the energy of love, choice and beauty. Most often it stands in the couple’s common language: you reach agreement through feelings and want a beautiful, warm life together. The plus is openness and tenderness; the minus is jealousy, idealisation and quarrels in which words hit exactly where it hurts.

faq.q: Why is a 6 so frequent in the common language?
faq.a: This point of a couple’s matrix takes only multiples of three: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 and 21. The six gets the largest share of them — almost a third of all couples. That is why for many couples the common language is The Lovers.

faq.q: Which arcana is the 6 compatible with?
faq.a: A couple’s matrix does not put the question that way. Compatibility here is not a combination of two numbers but a separate chart put together from two dates. The six in it describes what the union rests on and where it stumbles, but does not say who it “goes with”.

faq.q: Can a 6 stand in the centre of a couple’s matrix?
faq.a: It can — for about one couple in fifty-five. For that the partners’ centres must add up to 6, 24, 33 or 42, for example 3 and 3, 8 and 16 or 13 and 20.

faq.q: Does a 6 in a couple mean a love triangle?
faq.a: No. The Lovers in a couple’s matrix do not mean a third wheel. The six speaks of choice: choosing each other every day, not doubting the choice you made and not looking for “better”. With a six, jealousy grows out of insecurity, not out of facts.

seo.title: Destiny matrix compatibility 7: The Chariot in a couple
seo.description: Destiny matrix compatibility 7: a team on the move, money, relocations and a fight for the wheel. Where the seven stands and how a couple can read it.

items.title: The 7 in a compatibility matrix: The Chariot in a couple
items.short: A seven in a couple’s matrix makes the union a team on the move: each has their own road, and together there are relocations, hikes, shared projects, good earnings and strong passion at the start. Most often it stands in the attitude to money and home life and in the middle of the couple’s tail. Its plus is two people who walk side by side and protect each other. Its minus is a fight for the wheel, decisions made in the heat of the moment and a demand that the other give up their own goals for “shared” ones.

sections.h2: The seven in a chart of two dates: calculation and example
paragraphs: A search for “7 in compatibility” is almost always about the couple’s matrix. It is calculated like this: add up the matching points of two personal matrices and reduce each sum to a number from 1 to 22, adding its digits if it is above 22. The result is a third matrix — a portrait of the union. How to read the seven in such a matrix is set out below following Yuliana Lisovskaya’s book Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024): the meaning is hers, the wording is ours.
Four sums give a 7: 7, 25, 34 and 43.

**An example.** The partners were born on 3 January 1993 and 18 February 1992. The material point is calculated from the year: 1 + 9 + 9 + 3 = 22 and 1 + 9 + 9 + 2 = 21. 22 + 21 = 43, 4 + 3 = 7 — a seven in “Attitude to material things”. In the middle of the tail the partners have 5 and 20: 25, 2 + 5 = 7 — another seven. This couple’s tail is 3-7-13, and The Chariot stands right in its middle.

sections.h2: The seven’s route through the couple’s points
paragraphs: The seven has two favourite places — home life and the middle of the tail — and it is a rare guest in the couple’s centre. The share of couples covers all dates from 1900 to 2026; the letter in brackets is the book’s name for the point, transliterated from Russian.

head: Sphere and card in the couple reading
Share of couples
rows: “The couple’s karmic tail” — “Middle of the task” (D2)
“How others see the couple” — “How you are seen” (B)
“The couple’s money” — “Where it leaks”; also “Success and the union” (K)
“Relationship and common language” — “What connects”, under the heart (I)

paragraphs: The only point the seven never reaches is “Common language” (“Entry to the task”): only 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 and 21 stand there.

sections.h2: Money and home life: the seven at the wheel of the budget
paragraphs: **“Home and things”.** The seven treats money and things actively. You earn well, can run a shared business and often keep several projects going at once. You keep track of money and plan it, part with things easily — a move is not a tragedy for you but a reason to throw out what you do not need — and willingly help others. Lisovskaya’s main advice here is unexpectedly simple: the budget is better left in one pair of hands. If both pull on the wheel, this is the area that suffers.
**“Path to prosperity”.** The seven’s prosperity lies in movement: a business of your own, business trips, moving to where there are more opportunities, work that needs speed and decisiveness.
**“Way into money”.** The seven loses income through haste: you took on five projects and finished one. And through shifting responsibility: “you’re the one who should be earning”.

**“Where it leaks” and “Success and the union”.** The seven’s holes are uncontrolled spending, risky loans, a gambling streak, a wish to double the money fast. Debts secured against your home are especially dangerous: for the seven, “let’s take the risk” comes too easily. And status affects the union through career: an imbalance between work and the relationship, when one races ahead and the other is left waiting at home.

sections.h2: The couple’s tasks: where to go and who is driving
paragraphs: The couple’s tail shows the union’s trials, and it is read mostly through the minus: the key point is “Main task”, and the middle reveals it. For the seven it is almost always a question of the wheel and the direction.

**“Middle of the task”.** The seven is one of the most frequent energies in the middle of the tail: roughly one couple in twelve. It says that the key to the main task is direction. Decide where the two of you are going and keep to the course rather than dashing about. This is also often where a joint move lies that the couple needs to make up its mind about.
**“Main task”.** The seven brings into the main task:

ul: rivalry for the lead and control over each other;
the balance between career and relationship;
decisions made in the heat of the moment and conclusions drawn before everything is clear;
aimlessness: when the movement has stopped, neither knows why they are together;
possessiveness;
a demand that the other give up their own goals for “shared” ones that are in fact someone else’s;
the ability to restore strength carefully rather than take it from those close to you.

sections.h2: Parent-captains
paragraphs: If there are no children, these two points tell how you lead the younger ones — nephews and nieces, a team, those in your care.

**“Parents together”.** For the seven, children are part of the crew: they come along on hikes, rafting trips, moves and competitions. You are quick to stand up for your own and understand each other in this role without many words. The risk is a race: clubs, sports, achievements, and no time just to lie on the sofa together.

**“What you teach”.** The seven teaches setting goals and reaching them, not being afraid of the road, falling and getting up. It teaches independence. It is good when the right to rest and to lose is added to this; bad when the child becomes one more project that has to “take off”.

sections.h2: Movement that nourishes and a race that starts quarrels
paragraphs: **What fills.** The seven is charged by movement: sport, active holidays, travel, moving to a place you chose together. The partner’s successes and growth. Big purchases you worked towards together. It matters that you walk side by side, each on your own road: the seven needs a road of its own, and respect for it fills it more than any present. At the start of the union there is strong passion, and it is worth looking after. Even the seven’s minus turns into a plus here — that is how the author reads this point.

**Where it sparks.** With a seven in this point you quarrel about power and speed. Control and suppression, conflicts out of nothing, jealousy and envy of each other’s successes. Or the opposite trouble — indifference: each races off on their own business, and there is no support. One more trait of the seven in the minus is taking strength from those close to you: coming home drained and snapping at whoever is nearest.

sections.h2: Comrades from outside and a shared destination
paragraphs: **“Image of the couple”.** With a seven you are taken for friends and comrades rather than lovers: active, always ready to go, often entrepreneurs, both with strong characters. You often move house, as if looking for your home, and you are keen on hiking or even extreme sports. You stand up for each other no matter what. The seven’s minus in the image comes in two kinds. Active: they grab at things and drop them, rush, take risks, borrow. Passive: the passion has faded, there is no goal, and the two drag each other down.

**“What to create together”.** The book has no ready answer to this question for the seven, so we read it from the plus of the energy. You were brought together to arrive somewhere together: build a business, move, reach a goal that is beyond one person. And for each of you to stay on your own road along the way. It is read only in the plus.

sections.h2: Under the heart: a shared road
paragraphs: “Under the heart” is what searches call the “What connects” point. It speaks not of problems but of the couple’s resource: what brings you closer.

With a seven, what connects you is a shared road. Trips that leave you something to remember. A move you made up your minds to together. A shared project you started from scratch. Victories — your own and each other’s: the seven under the heart rejoices in the partner’s success as its own. And a feeling of being protected: in any scrape the other will be beside you, not in the stands.

sections.h2: A 7 in the centre: life on the move
paragraphs: A seven in the centre is rare: about one couple in seventy. For that the partners’ personal centres must add up to 7, 25 or 34: for example, 3 and 4, 11 and 14, 9 and 16, 12 and 22, or 16 and 18.

The atmosphere with a seven in the centre is constant movement and experiment. Each develops outside the family, you make decisions together and quickly, and you stand up for those close to you instantly. For all the activity, discipline and clear roles are needed, otherwise movement turns into bustle. In the minus — control, conflicts out of nothing and being tired of each other.

sections.h2: Advice for The Chariot’s crew

ul: **Alternate the race with rest.** Moderate activity saves both strength and the relationship.
**Define your status and roles.** What you are to each other and who is responsible for what — with nothing left unsaid.
**A life’s work of their own for each.** Don’t demand that the other travel only your road.
**Don’t hurry your partner.** Their pace is not yours, and that is normal.
**Don’t bring your failures home.** A setback at work is no reason to wage war at home.
**Find a safe outlet for your drive.** Sport, competitions, physical work.
**Talk about problems calmly**, without going straight on the attack.

sections.h2: A 7 in one of the partners
paragraphs: If a seven stands in the personal matrix of one of you, there will be movement and protection beside that person, and they need a road of their own and respect for it. What a seven brings to one person’s relationships is read in their personal chart — that is a different calculation. A personal seven does not pass into the couple’s matrix: two sevens in one point give the couple a fourteen.

faq.q: What does 7 mean in destiny matrix compatibility?
faq.a: In a couple the seven is responsible for movement, goals and teamwork. A union with it is like a crew: each develops in their own way, and together there are moves, projects and good earnings. The minus is a struggle for the lead, haste, risk and a demand that the other give up their own goals.

faq.q: Does a 7 in a couple mean we will keep moving house?
faq.a: Not necessarily, but the theme of changing place is alive for such a couple. Lisovskaya describes couples with a seven as often moving in search of their home, and among their tasks she names making up their minds about a joint move. For some it means a new city, for others a new flat or job.

faq.q: Why is a couple with a 7 advised to leave the budget to one partner?
faq.a: Because in a couple with a seven both are used to steering. If both pull the budget their way, a tug of war begins, and money suffers first. It is not about who is in charge but about who runs this particular area — by agreement.

faq.q: Is a 7 in the couple’s centre common?
faq.a: No, it is rare: about one couple in seventy. For that the partners’ centres must add up to 7, 25 or 34, for example 3 and 4, 11 and 14, or 16 and 18.

faq.q: What can we do if the passion in a couple with a 7 has faded?
faq.a: That is The Chariot’s passive minus: there is no goal, and the movement has stopped. A new shared goal brings it back — a trip, a project, a move — together with respect for each partner’s road. The seven does badly in still water, and so does the couple.

seo.title: Destiny matrix compatibility 8: Justice in a couple
seo.description: Destiny matrix compatibility 8: honest home life and money, the karmic tasks of the couple’s tail and quarrels about fairness. Where the eight stands.

items.title: The 8 in a compatibility matrix: Justice in a couple
items.short: A cool head and a warm heart — that is how the eight looks in a couple’s matrix. Duties are shared fairly, big purchases are decided together, there is a plan B and a reserve, and quarrels pass without scenes. Most often the eight stands in the couple’s home life and money and in the middle of its tail — where the union’s karmic tasks are read. Its minus is living like neighbours, broken promises and responsibility that swells into control.

sections.h2: How an 8 adds up: from the year of birth to the tail
paragraphs: A compatibility matrix is a third chart put together from two personal ones: the partners’ matching points are added up and reduced to a number from 1 to 22, adding the digits if the sum is above 22. Its points have their own meaning, given below following the school of Yuliana Lisovskaya, author of Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024). The method gives no compatibility percentages.
Four sums give an 8: 8, 26, 35 and 44.

**An example by year of birth.** The material point is calculated from the year of birth. Someone born in 1990 has 1 + 9 + 9 + 0 = 19 there; someone born in 1987 has 1 + 9 + 8 + 7 = 25, 2 + 5 = 7. 19 + 7 = 26, 2 + 6 = 8: any such couple has an eight in “Attitude to material things”.

**An example from the book.** Lisovskaya analyses the couple born on 3 December 1997 and 27 May 1999. In the middle of the karmic tail the partners have 20 and 15: 35, 3 + 5 = 8. The same sum appears in the point “What can spoil it” — and there is an eight there too. The couple’s tail is 6-8-11. Note: if the middle of the tail were recalculated from the ends, as in a personal matrix, it would come to 6 + 11 = 17. But in a couple the middle is not recalculated — it is also the sum of the two personal ones, and the result is 8.

sections.h2: Which points of a couple Justice occurs in
paragraphs: The eight is spread evenly over most points — for seven to nine couples in a hundred — and most often stands in home life and the middle of the tail. The count covers all pairs of dates from 1900 to 2026; in brackets is Lisovskaya’s letter, transliterated from Russian.

paragraphs: The only point where an eight never occurs is “Common language”, also “Entry to the task”: the number there is always divisible by three.

sections.h2: Money and home life: an honest account
paragraphs: **“Home and things”.** In home life the eight means order and honesty. Official employment, taxes paid on time, income and spending tracked in a spreadsheet or at least in one’s head. Big purchases are decided together and calmly, without “I’ve already bought it”. There is always a plan B and something put by for a rainy day. In the minus — either stinginess or reckless spending, secret stashes kept from each other, fear of change, and sometimes an imbalance: one “on principle” does not work while the other carries everything.

**“Path to prosperity”.** The eight grows rich on transparency and the law: official income, contracts, professions where precision and responsibility are valued. Dubious earnings are bad for such a couple: Lisovskaya advises plainly that they be given up.

**“Way into money”.** What stops the eight from earning more is caution and fear of change: “a bird in the hand”, even when that bird stopped feeding you long ago. Debts and overdue payments get in the way too, piling up while everyone pretends they are not there.

**“Where it leaks” and “Success and the union”.** The eight’s holes are debts, fines, overdue payments — everything not settled on time. And status affects the union through fairness: if one works more but gets less recognition, the eight will be sure to notice and make a note of it.

sections.h2: The couple’s karmic tasks: the middle of the tail and the main task
paragraphs: The couple’s karmic tail is three points at the bottom of its matrix, Lisovskaya’s D1, D2 and D. It is read mostly in the minus: what the couple has to go through, whether these are karmic lessons or simply life’s. The key point is “Main task”; the others reveal it.

**“Middle of the task”.** The middle of the tail is the eight’s second most frequent place, for almost one couple in twelve. It suggests that the key to the main task lies in honesty and agreements: calling things by their names, sharing responsibility, doing what was promised.
**“Main task”.** The eight sets the couple tasks like these:

ul: to admit their own fault instead of looking for someone to blame;
not to withdraw into themselves when the family has problems;
to pay off debts and not let overdue payments pile up;
not to turn responsibility into control and pressure;
to forgive rather than keep a tally of grievances;
to learn to shift perspective and understand the other instead of measuring everything by their own yardstick.

paragraphs: An eight in the couple’s tail does not mean “retribution” awaits you. Justice in a couple speaks of balance: who gives what, who takes what, who is responsible for what. The task is to make that balance fair to both.

sections.h2: Consistent parents
paragraphs: The parents points show what rules the two of you set for those who are younger — children, if you have or will have them, and everyone you are responsible for.

**“Parents together”.** With an eight you are consistent parents: the rules are the same for everyone, promises are kept, a punishment fits the misdeed. The child knows what to expect, and that gives them something to stand on. In this role you support each other with a single decision. The risk is dryness: everything is fair, but there is little warmth and spontaneity.

**“What you teach”.** The eight teaches honesty, responsibility for one’s actions, the ability to admit mistakes and to answer for one’s words. It is good if you show this by example: “I was wrong, I’m sorry” from an adult works better than any lecture.

sections.h2: Honesty that fills and a tally that starts quarrels
paragraphs: **What fills.** The eight’s strength is restored by honesty and openness: a frank talk after which everything is clear. Closeness of spirit, shared interests, predictability — for the eight, knowing that the partner will do what they promised is romance itself. Restraint in words, devotion. The author sees no minuses in this point.

**Where it sparks.** An eight in “Where it sparks” means quarrels about fairness. Who did more, who broke a promise again, why did you tell my mother about our affairs. Lack of initiative, insensitivity, a habit of judging by oneself and not noticing that the partner is hurt. Sometimes boredom leads to games with feelings. And a topic on which the eight is easily hurt: whether or not to make the relationship official.

sections.h2: Under the heart: agreements that hold
paragraphs: In our reading this is the card “What connects”; in searches it is “under the heart”. It is read as the union’s positive potential: what the two come together on.

With an eight, what connects you is agreements that hold. A shared plan set out for the year. A prenuptial agreement you drew up calmly and without hard feelings. A decision made together and carried out. Respect for each other’s families. An eight under the heart is trust tested in practice: “I know you’ll do as you said”.

sections.h2: Reserved from outside: the couple’s image and the meaning of the meeting
paragraphs: **“Image of the couple”.** Added from the days of birth, this point shows what guests see. With an eight you look from outside like a conservative, organised, pragmatic couple. Not spontaneous, direct, reserved — some even find you a little dry. But love and passion are there, just not on display. You take a long time to get the measure of each other and a long time to settle in together. In the minus the image is spoilt: the partner’s faults are put on show to make oneself look better; blunt directness makes guests uncomfortable; the couple lives like neighbours.

**“What to create together”.** Lisovskaya gives no direct answer here, but the eight’s plus suggests one. You were brought together to build an honest union: with clear rules, an equal contribution and respect for both families. Often — to make the relationship official and create a family where a word means something. This point has no minus.

sections.h2: An 8 in the centre: faithfulness and calm
paragraphs: About one couple in fifty gets an eight in the couple’s centre. For that the partners’ personal centres must add up to 8, 26, 35 or 44: for example, 3 and 5, 4 and 4, 12 and 14, 10 and 16, 13 and 22, or 22 and 22.

Inside such a couple there is faithfulness, reliability and respect for the traditions of both families. There are almost no conflicts, and when there are, they pass calmly. Duties are shared fairly, and nobody makes excessive demands. In the minus — living like neighbours: each lives inside themselves, promises are not kept, feelings hide behind rules.

sections.h2: Advice for a couple with Justice

ul: **Put your shared goals and the way to them into words** — out loud, or better still in writing.
**Set limits on advice and help.** How much you help relatives, who advises whom and when — agree in advance.
**Give up dubious earnings.** For the eight, “grey” money costs more than it seems.
**Let go of idealising your partner.** They do not have to match your yardstick.
**Think things through in advance.** Plan B is your superpower — use it.

sections.h2: An 8 in a partner’s personal matrix
paragraphs: An eight in a partner’s personal chart speaks of that person: in a relationship they value honesty and an equal contribution and cope badly with unfairness. It has to be read by its position in their personal chart — on the relationship line, under the heart and so on. A personal eight does not pass into the couple’s matrix: two eights in one point give the couple a sixteen.

faq.q: What does 8 mean in destiny matrix compatibility?
faq.a: Honesty, balance and responsibility — that is how the eight sounds in a couple’s matrix. A union with it is reserved on the outside and reliable on the inside: duties are shared, spending is discussed, there is a reserve. The minus is dryness, living like neighbours, broken promises and control.

faq.q: Is an 8 in the couple’s karmic tail a retribution?
faq.a: No. The couple’s tail describes the union’s tasks, not a punishment. An eight in it speaks of balance: admitting one’s fault, forgiving, paying off debts, not turning responsibility into control. Justice does not prove that what happened to you was deserved.

faq.q: Why is the middle of our tail 8, while another calculator shows a different number?
faq.a: In a couple’s matrix the middle of the tail is the sum of the middles of the two personal tails, not recalculated from the ends. That is how Lisovskaya’s book counts: for her couple born on 3 December 1997 and 27 May 1999 the middle is 8, while recalculation would give 17. Calculators that recalculate disagree with the book.

faq.q: With which partner centres does an 8 land in the couple’s centre?
faq.a: When their centres add up to 8, 26, 35 or 44 — for example, 3 and 5, 4 and 4, 12 and 14, or 13 and 22. This happens for about one couple in fifty.

faq.q: Does an 8 in a couple mean we have to get married?
faq.a: The matrix obliges nothing. But the theme of making the relationship official matters for the eight: in the plus the couple itself strives for a clear status; in the minus, reluctance to marry becomes a reason for quarrels. It helps to discuss honestly what “being together officially” means to each of you.

seo.title: Destiny matrix compatibility 9: The Hermit in a couple
seo.description: Destiny matrix compatibility 9: quiet for two, a shared language, money spent on knowledge and tail tasks, including the 9-9-9 tail only couples have.

items.title: The 9 in a compatibility matrix: The Hermit in a couple
items.short: Two people who are comfortable being silent together — that is how the nine comes together in a couple’s matrix. The union is calm and unhurried, with long talks about what matters, respect for boundaries and love shown in deeds rather than words. It is one of the most frequent energies in a couple: one couple in four has it in the point of common language and wishes. Its minus is each living on their own, problems piling up in silence and work quietly taking the place of family.

sections.h2: The sums 9, 27, 36 and the 9-9-9 tail
paragraphs: A compatibility matrix is a separate calculation: the matching points of two personal matrices are added together and reduced to a number from 1 to 22, by adding the digits if the sum is above 22. The result is a third chart — the couple’s chart. There is no generally accepted method of reading it; below is how Yuliana Lisovskaya reads the nine in a couple in her book Matritsa sudby: sovmestimost (Destiny Matrix: Compatibility, 2024). It is her practice, not a canon, and the method gives no compatibility percentages.
Three sums give a 9: 9, 27 and 36.

**An example from the book.** Lisovskaya analyses a couple born on 16 July 2003 and 1 September 2005. In the common language point the partners have 21 and 6: 27, 2 + 7 = 9. In the middle of the tail — 4 and 5, exactly 9. In the main task — 10 and 17: again 27 and again a nine. That gives the couple’s tail 9-9-9. A personal matrix never has such a tail: there the middle is recalculated from the ends, and it would come out as 9-18-9. In a couple the middle is the sum of the two personal ones — and The Hermit takes all three task points.

sections.h2: Where The Hermit stands in a couple
paragraphs: One couple in four gets a nine in the common language, and almost as many in “The couple’s values”; in the other points it stands for five to nine couples in a hundred, and less often in the centre. The count covers all pairs of dates from 1900 to 2026; in brackets is the point’s letter in Lisovskaya’s book, transliterated from Russian.

Share of couples

“The couple’s values” — the couple’s spiritual purpose
“The couple’s karmic tail” — “Middle of the task” (D2)
“The couple’s money” — “Where it leaks”; also “Success and the union” (K)

sections.h2: Common language and entry to the task: one couple in four
paragraphs: The common language point lies both on the relationship line and at the start of the couple’s tail, so it speaks both of what you want together and of what gets in your way.

**As a common language.** With a nine you understand each other without unnecessary words and agree on the essentials almost at once: where to live, what to learn, how to bring up children. You need meaning, depth and quiet. You want similar things — a home where each has a corner of their own, time for your own pursuits, conversations after which something becomes clearer. Your views of the world coincide, and you willingly learn from each other.

**As an entry to the task.** The reverse side is an agreement to keep quiet. A problem is not discussed because “it’s obvious anyway” or “it will pass”. Each withdraws into their own shell, and a month later it turns out you live in the same flat but in different worlds. At the entry to the tail the nine has to learn to come out of the quiet towards the other — especially when things are hard.

sections.h2: Money for books and a reserve just in case
paragraphs: **“Home and things”.** The nine handles money unhurriedly and thoughtfully. You spend a lot on study, courses and books — for you these are not expenses but investments. Otherwise you are cautious: you think over even a necessary purchase for weeks, compare, read reviews. There is always a reserve. In the minus — asceticism or stinginess: “we don’t need much” turns into “we don’t need anything”, and money stops coming in.

**“Where it leaks” and “Success and the union”.** The nine stands here often. The hole is an unwillingness to earn more than is needed for books and tea. And status affects the union through a shadow: sometimes one partner is more visible, better known, more successful, and the other stays in their shadow and does not grow. In her analysis of one couple where the nine stands both here and in the point “What can spoil it”, Lisovskaya reads it like this: the couple’s difficulties will hit both the budget and the relationship, and the couple has a strong wish to do everything themselves and prove they are right.

**“Path to prosperity”.** The nine comes to prosperity through knowledge and depth: expertise, consulting, a business of its own where experience is valued, teaching. It is important to decide together what level of prosperity you need — otherwise the nine stops at “enough”.

**“Way into money”.** The nine’s main brake in money is a lack of ambition. Lisovskaya notes that such couples often need someone to spur on their material wishes: a friend, a mentor, a shared goal such as a flat of their own.

sections.h2: The couple’s tasks: not hiding in a shell
paragraphs: The couple’s karmic tail is three points at the bottom of its matrix. The main task in it is read mostly in the minus, while the middle and the entry suggest how to approach it.

**“Middle of the task”.** A nine in the middle of the tail turns up for almost one couple in twelve. It suggests that the key to the main task lies in trust and the ability to listen: to stop, hear the other out, ask, rather than decide for them in your own head.
**“Main task”.** In the main task the nine needs to:

ul: not stifle each other’s interests, even if they seem odd;
know the boundaries: sense when to support the partner and when to leave them in peace;
reach out a hand in difficult times instead of hiding in a shell;
do more together — not just live side by side;
share and listen, building trust through conversation.

paragraphs: If the nine stands in all three points of the tail, as for the 9-9-9 couple from the book, this theme becomes the main one in the couple’s life: learning to be together without losing yourselves, and to be yourselves without walking away from the other.

sections.h2: Quiet parents
paragraphs: Parents in a couple’s matrix are not necessarily a mother and father: they are the two elders people come to for an answer — children, nephews and nieces, pupils.

**“Parents together”.** The nine makes you mentors who do not push. You answer questions seriously, read together, let a child be alone for a while. You support each other in this role calmly, without fuss. The risk is distance: the child lacks warmth and noise, because the house is always quiet and everyone is busy with their own things.

**“What you teach”.** The nine teaches children to think, to look for answers themselves, to value knowledge and solitude. It is good if the ability to talk about feelings is added to this — otherwise the child will learn the main rule of the house: hard things are not talked about.

sections.h2: Talks past midnight and quiet, long quarrels
paragraphs: **What fills.** The nine is filled by deep conversations — past midnight, about a book, about meaning, about the future. Respect for boundaries: nobody looks through the other’s phone or demands an account. The partner’s wisdom, foresight and patience. A little mystery, and shared interests that look odd from outside: astronomy, old maps, rare kinds of tea. According to Lisovskaya, this point always works for the couple.

**Where it sparks.** The nine quarrels quietly but for a long time. Each lives on their own, problems pile up, feelings cool. Work becomes more important than family, and there are fewer and fewer friends. Nit-picking and criticism of everything — from how the partner slices bread to what they read. Sometimes two people stay together not because they are happy but because they are afraid of being alone.

sections.h2: Under the heart: meaning and searching
paragraphs: Under the heart in the compatibility matrix is the card “What connects” — a point on the relationship line where the couple’s shared resource is read.

With a nine, what connects you is meaning and searching. Studying together, travelling to quiet places, a long project the two of you have pursued for years. A bookshelf put together jointly. Questions you look for the answers to as two. And a trust that needs no proof: the nine under the heart does not need loud declarations — it is enough to know that you are understood.

sections.h2: A quiet couple from outside and a shared meaning
paragraphs: **“Image of the couple”.** With a nine you are a calm, quiet, modest couple. You tell people about events after the fact and are reluctant hosts, but you can give sound advice. There may be a large age gap, or one partner may be well known and the other not. Your pace is slow in everything: a very long time may pass between the first date and the wedding. In the minus the image turns cold: a closed couple that looks odd from outside, partners who seem to come from different planets, and a condescending attitude to each other’s families.

**“What to create together”.** The book has no ready text on “why you met” for the nine; it is derived from its strong side. You were brought together to find your own meaning as two: to build a union where you can grow, learn and be yourselves. To learn wisdom and patience from each other. The author reads this point only in the plus.

sections.h2: A 9 in the centre: a corner of one’s own for each
paragraphs: A nine ends up in the centre for about one couple in thirty-six. For that the partners’ personal centres must add up to 9, 27 or 36: for example, 3 and 6, 4 and 5, 13 and 14, 11 and 16, 14 and 22, or 18 and 18.

When the nine is in the centre, each of you has your own time and place for solitude, and nobody takes offence. Attention to small things, love in deeds, trust and agreements. You take your time over every step, but every step is a conscious one. In the minus — coldness, the feelings have cooled, and the union is held together by habit.

sections.h2: The couple’s values: meaning reached together
paragraphs: In “The couple’s values” the nine stands for 22 couples in 100 — almost as often as in the common language. It is one of the five main cards of the reading, and it is calculated differently from the other points: the number is recalculated from the couple’s purposes, so only multiples of three occur here. For Lisovskaya this point is the couple’s spiritual purpose, its values and shared path.

**For a couple with a nine in the values, understanding matters more than getting things done.** Its path leads inwards: books, talks until two in the morning, decisions nobody outside understands — changing profession, studying again, moving to a small town. The difficulty is going into the depths alone: each thinks things through in silence and comes to the other with a finished conclusion, friends stop calling, and the path between the two lanterns grows over.

sections.h2: Advice for a couple with The Hermit

ul: **Talk in search of common ground.** Not to prove you are right but to find the point where you agree.
**Learn sincerity.** Saying “I feel bad” is not a weakness.
**Look at a problem from outside.** This comes easily to the nine — apply it to yourselves.
**More time as two** — not side by side but together.
**Decide on the level of prosperity you want** and work towards it rather than settling for “enough”.
**Learn about money** and vary your intimacy: the nine must not freeze into habit.

sections.h2: A 9 in a personal chart is a trait of the person, not the couple
paragraphs: A person with a nine in their personal matrix needs quiet, time of their own and conversations that get to the point. In the couple’s matrix their nine adds up with the partner’s number. Two nines in one point give the couple an eighteen.

faq.q: What does 9 mean in destiny matrix compatibility?
faq.a: The nine brings quiet, depth and respect for boundaries into a couple. A union with it is calm and unhurried: long conversations, shared views, love in deeds. The minus is each living on their own, problems piling up in silence, work taking the place of family.

faq.q: What does the couple’s tail 9-9-9 mean?
faq.a: It is a tail with a nine in all three task points. It never occurs in a personal matrix, but in a couple it is possible: the middle of the couple’s tail is added, not recalculated. The tasks of such a couple are not to hide from each other, to talk about what has built up and to do more together.

faq.q: Why do so many couples have a 9 in their common language?
faq.a: Every couple has a multiple of three in the common language: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 or 21. The nine gets a noticeable share of them — about a quarter of all couples.

faq.q: Does a 9 in a couple mean we will live apart?
faq.a: No. The nine speaks of a need for space of one’s own, not of separate lives. In the plus each has their own corner and their own time, and that protects the union. In the minus there is so much space that you lose each other — and that is the nine’s task.

faq.q: Is a 9 in the couple’s atmosphere rare?
faq.a: Fairly: a nine stands in the centre for about one couple in thirty-six. For that the partners’ centres must add up to 9, 27 or 36, for example 4 and 5, 13 and 14, or 18 and 18.
